43077510.titulo: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis.
43077510.autores: Jiang Q, Dikdan RJ, … Shi L (14 autores)
43077510.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
43077510.resumo: Em camundongos com TB, metabolômica dirigida e transcriptoma mostram que o controle agudo vem com ativação de mTORC1, glutaminólise, glicólise e metabolismo de arginina e serina; a infecção crônica reduz mTORC1, aumenta o catabolismo de BCAA e baixa a glutamina. Glutamina oral restaurou aminoácidos pulmonares, reforçou mTORC1 e reduziu moderadamente carga bacteriana e lesão; dados humanos reanalisados mostram queda de glutamina circulante na progressão.
43077510.resumo_original: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine-leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

resumo_blocos.racional: A desnutrição figura como o principal fator de risco para suscetibilidade, gravidade clínica e desfecho terapêutico desfavorável na tuberculose (TB). Sob a ótica da imunologia nutricional e do imunometabolismo, os autores investigaram como a disponibilidade de aminoácidos e o metabolismo mitocondrial moldam a defesa do hospedeiro durante a transição da infecção aguda para a infecção crônica por Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de metabolômica direcionada e perfilamento transcricional em modelo murino de tuberculose, comparando fases aguda e crônica da infecção. Realizaram suplementação oral de glutamina in vivo para avaliar homeostase de aminoácidos pulmonares, sinalização anabólica e desfechos microbiológicos, além da reanálise de conjuntos de dados metabolômicos humanos publicados durante a progressão para TB ativa.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O controle imune na fase aguda acompanhou-se de robusta ativação da sinalização associada a mTORC1, glutaminólise, glicólise, metabolismo de arginina e metabolismo de um carbono via serina. Na fase crônica, observaram-se queda na ativação imune e em mTORC1 e aumento do catabolismo de aminoácidos de cadeia ramificada, destacando leucina e glutamina como metabólitos discriminantes — sugerindo que a escassez de glutamina redireciona a leucina para oxidação mitocondrial e limita o anabolismo mediado por mTORC1. A suplementação oral de glutamina restaurou os níveis pulmonares de leucina, reativou mTORC1, reduziu moderadamente a carga bacteriana e a patologia pulmonar, mitigou a perda ponderal e refletiu a queda de glutamina circulante vista em coortes humanas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece um eixo mecanístico glutamina-leucina-mTORC1 diretamente transferível às investigações de imunometabolismo do hospedeiro no LUCHM, conectando restrição ou desbalanço nutricional à competência antimicrobiana e à preservação tecidual.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar se a razão glutamina/leucina e a ativação endotelial ou leucocitária de mTORC1 sofrem deslocamento análogo no modelo murino de malária cerebral por PbA e em mosquitos submetidos a repasto sanguíneo enriquecido em lipídios e glicose (HFHS).

43078841.titulo: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels.
43078841.autores: Bermann TL, Barbosa DAM, … da Luz Wallau G (30 autores)
43078841.resumo: Integra dados entomológicos, epidemiológicos e ambientais de 2015 a 2023 no Rio Grande do Sul com 665 novos genomas de DENV: Aedes aegypti se expandiu pelos municípios, quase metade superou 20 casos/100 mil hab. em 2023 e as linhagens virais persistem localmente entre anos, com duas regiões como polos de dispersão.
43078841.resumo_original: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

resumo_blocos.racional: Em 2024, o Brasil concentrou 70% dos casos mundiais de dengue, com expansão alarmante do vírus da dengue (DENV) e de vetores Aedes para zonas subtropicais e temperadas, tornando a doença recentemente endêmica no Rio Grande do Sul. O estudo buscou reconstruir como a invasão e os níveis de infestação de Aedes aegypti impulsionaram a dinâmica epidemiológica e genômica da transmissão em clima temperado entre 2015 e 2023.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de séries históricas entomológicas, epidemiológicas e ambientais do Rio Grande do Sul (2015–2023) combinada à geração e análise genômica de 665 novos genomas de DENV para rastrear persistência viral interanual e rotas de dispersão intermunicipal.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A expansão territorial de Aedes aegypti pelos municípios gaúchos foi acompanhada por acentuada escalada de casos a partir de 2020, levando quase metade dos municípios a ultrapassar o limiar de endemicidade de pelo menos 20 casos por 100.000 habitantes/ano em 2023. A análise filogenômica dos 665 genomas demonstrou persistência local contínua de linhagens virais ao longo de múltiplos anos sustentando surtos sazonais, identificando as regiões Noroeste e Metropolitana como principais polos de disseminação viral intraestadual em uma população humana majoritariamente naïf.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Contextualiza a expansão meridional de Aedes aegypti e da persistência endêmica de DENV no Brasil em áreas temperadas, reforçando a necessidade de correlacionar competência vetorial e tolerância térmica/metabólica em populações brasileiras acompanhadas pelo LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar se linhagens sulistas de Aedes aegypti estabelecidas no Rio Grande do Sul apresentam alterações na fisiologia do repasto sanguíneo, reservas lipídicas ou resposta antiviral por siRNA (Dicer-2/AGO2) sob temperaturas temperadas.

43079132.titulo: Volume Electron Microscopy of Cortical Organoids: Methods for Region Identification, Connectome Reconstruction, and Organelle Segmentation.
43079132.autores: Dallere S, Mattioni A, … Boido M (9 autores)
43079132.resumo: Fluxo de trabalho de vEM em organoides corticais humanos: CLEM, mosaico SEM de grande área, FIB-SEM e validação por TEM. Dos dois protocolos de inclusão comparados, DeFelipe e Fairén/Cano-Astorga permite segmentar sinapses e traçar neuritos; Deerinck dá mais contraste de membrana, mas limita a visualização da densidade pós-sináptica.
43079132.resumo_original: Volume electron microscopy (vEM) has become a powerful tool for 3D ultrastructural analysis of neural circuits, yet its application to human brain organoids remains limited, particularly for connectomic studies. Here, we established a comprehensive and scalable workflow for applying vEM to human cortical organoids, integrating correlative light and electron microscopy, large-area SEM (scanning electron microscopy) mosaic imaging, focused ion beam-SEM (FIB-SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) validation. By systematically comparing two embedding protocols in use, we demonstrated that the DeFelipe and Fairén (1993); Cano-Astorga et al. (2024a) method provides optimal compatibility with toluidine blue-stained semithin sectioning and enables reliable synapse segmentation and neurite tracing. In contrast, the Deerinck's protocol (2010) offers enhanced membrane contrast but limits postsynaptic density visualization. Using FIB-SEM imaging of peripheral, neuropil-like regions of cortical organoids, we achieved accurate 3D reconstruction of synapses, neurites and intracellular organelles, enabling quantitative assessment of synaptic apposition surfaces, neurite trajectories, and organelle distribution across defined cellular compartments. Together, our results demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of micro-connectomic reconstruction in human cortical organoids at nanometer resolution. This methodological framework expands the applicability of vEM to organoid systems and provides a robust foundation for future studies of human brain development, disease modeling, and therapeutic evaluation at the synaptic and subcellular level.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a microscopia eletrônica de volume (vEM) seja referência para reconstrução ultraestrutural 3D de circuitos neurais, sua aplicação a organoides corticais humanos permanece limitada por desafios de identificação regional e preservação sináptica. Os autores desenvolveram um fluxo escalável para viabilizar estudos microconectômicos e segmentação de organelas em organoides cerebrais humanos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Fluxo multimodal integrando microscopia correlativa óptica e eletrônica (CLEM), imageamento em mosaico por MEV de grande área (large-area SEM), microscopia eletrônica de varredura com feixe de íons focalizado (FIB-SEM) e validação por microscopia eletrônica de transmissão (TEM). Compararam sistematicamente os protocolos de inclusão de DeFelipe & Fairén (1993)/Cano-Astorga et al. (2024a) e de Deerinck (2010) em regiões periféricas tipo neurópilo de organoides corticais.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O protocolo de DeFelipe & Fairén/Cano-Astorga apresentou compatibilidade superior com cortes semifinos corados com azul de toluidina e permitiu segmentação confiável de sinapses e rastreamento de neuritos, enquanto o protocolo de Deerinck aumentou o contraste de membranas porém limitou a visualização da densidade pós-sináptica. Por meio de FIB-SEM em resolução nanométrica, reconstruíram em 3D sinapses, trajetórias de neuritos e organelas intracelulares, quantificando superfícies de aposição sináptica e distribuição subcelular de organelas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece parâmetros diretos de escolha de protocolo de inclusão (OTO/Deerinck vs. preservação de densidades sinápticas) e fluxo CLEM + mosaico SEM + FIB-SEM altamente transferíveis aos projetos de ultraestrutura 3D do LUCHM no CENABIO/UFRJ.

43079774.titulo: Extracellular Polyphosphate at the Host-Pathogen Interface: Emerging Roles in Virulence and Therapeutic Opportunity.
43079774.autores: Tennakoon A, Shrestha SK, Rijal R (3 autores)
43079774.resumo: Revisão sobre polifosfato extracelular na interface hospedeiro-patógeno: o polyP bacteriano de cadeia longa é em geral imunossupressor (prejudica a maturação do fagossomo, reprograma macrófagos, reduz a morte por complemento e a atividade de neutrófilos), enquanto o polyP curto do hospedeiro é pró-coagulante e inflamatório.
43079774.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP) is a conserved linear polymer of orthophosphate residues linked by phosphoanhydride bonds. Although polyP has long been studied for its intracellular roles in phosphate storage, energy metabolism, and stress adaptation, growing evidence indicates that extracellular polyP also influences host-pathogen interactions. In a subset of well-characterized bacterial systems, including mycobacteria and Neisseria species, extracellular or surface-associated polyP has been directly linked to impaired phagosome maturation, altered macrophage activation, reduced complement-mediated killing, and reduced neutrophil antimicrobial activity, whereas in other pathogens, polyP supports virulence primarily via intracellular mechanisms. PolyP chain length governs biological activity: long-chain bacterial polyP is largely immunosuppressive, whereas short-chain host polyP promotes procoagulant and inflammatory signaling, although context dictates specific outcomes. Here, we examine models of polyP externalization, detail how extracellular polyP impairs phagosome maturation, reprograms macrophages, and inhibits complement, evaluate interbacterial and probiotic barrier functions, and consider therapeutic opportunities targeting polyP metabolism.

resumo_blocos.racional: O polifosfato inorgânico (poliP) — polímero linear de resíduos de ortofosfato unidos por ligações fosfoanidrido — é classicamente estudado por suas funções intracelulares em reserva de fosfato, bioenergética e adaptação ao estresse. Esta revisão analisa evidências crescentes de que o poliP extracelular e associado à superfície atua como modulador direto de virulência e evasão imune na interface patógeno-hospedeiro.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão mecanística integrando modelos de externalização de poliP e dados funcionais em sistemas bacterianos bem caracterizados, como micobactérias e espécies de Neisseria, comparando efeitos dependentes do comprimento de cadeia entre poliP bacteriano de cadeia longa e poliP de cadeia curta derivado do hospedeiro.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O poliP extracelular ou de superfície bacteriana promove comprometimento da maturação do fagossomo, reprogramação/alteração da ativação de macrófagos, redução da lise mediada pelo sistema complemento e queda da atividade antimicrobiana de neutrófilos. Evidências comparativas mostram que o tamanho da cadeia dita o desfecho biológico: poliP bacteriano de cadeia longa exerce efeito majoritariamente imunossupressor, ao passo que poliP curto do hospedeiro estimula sinalização pró-coagulante e inflamatória de forma dependente do contexto, abrindo também frentes sobre barreiras probióticas e alvos terapêuticos no metabolismo de poliP.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente a expertise do LUCHM em polifosfato e acidocalcisomas à imunomodulação extracelular, coagulação e fagocitose, sugerindo que a distribuição de comprimento de cadeia do poliP pode distinguir papéis pró-coagulantes de papéis imunossupressores em infecções parasitárias.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar se Plasmodium ou exopolifosfatases/acidocalcisomas liberam poliP extracelular capaz de modular macrófagos, complemento ou cascata pró-coagulante microvascular na malária cerebral por PbA.

43082089.titulo: Sulfakinin Signaling Regulates Feeding and Energy Homeostasis in Hyphantria cunea: A Viable Target for Oral RNAi-Based Pest Control.
43082089.autores: Qi Q, Zhang J, … Cao C (7 autores)
43082089.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082089.resumo: Em Hyphantria cunea, o eixo sulfakinina (SK)/receptor (SKR) varia com o estado nutricional; silenciá-lo altera a homeostase energética, aumenta o consumo, esgota reservas, reduz a tolerância ao estresse e prejudica a reprodução. dsRNA produzido em bactéria e dado por via oral induziu RNAi, mortalidade larval e atraso de desenvolvimento.
43082089.resumo_original: Hyphantria cunea is a globally important pest of agricultural and forest ecosystems, owing its invasiveness to starvation tolerance, high feeding activity, and rapid reproduction. Neuropeptide signaling systems play a central role in regulating these key physiological processes. This study characterized the Sulfakinin (SK)/Sulfakinin receptor (SKR) pathway in H. cuneaand evaluated its potential for pest management. SK and SKR expression was influenced by nutritional status. Silencing SK or SKR disrupted energy homeostasis, increased food consumption, depleted energy reserves, reduced stress tolerance, and severely impaired reproduction. Conversely, SK peptide injection suppressed feeding during the early treatment period and significantly limited larval weight gain at 48-72 h. Furthermore, oral delivery of bacterially produced dsRNA targeting SK or SKR induced RNAi responses, resulting in increased larval mortality and delayed development. Collectively, these findings highlight the SK/SKR signaling pathway as a promising molecular target for sustainable RNAi-based strategies to control H. cunea.

resumo_blocos.racional: A praga invasora agrícola e florestal Hyphantria cunea destaca-se por elevada tolerância ao jejum, intensa atividade alimentar e rápida reprodução, processos coordenados por sistemas neuropeptidérgicos. Os autores caracterizaram a via da sulfacinina (SK) e seu receptor (SKR) como reguladora da homeostase energética e alvo molecular para controle baseado em RNAi oral.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise transcricional de SK e SKR sob diferentes estados nutricionais, ensaios de perda de função por silenciamento gênico de SK ou SKR, injeção de peptídeo sintético de SK avaliando consumo alimentar e ganho de peso larval em 48–72 h, além de entrega oral de dsRNA produzido em bactérias direcionado a SK ou SKR.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A expressão de SK e SKR respondeu diretamente ao estado nutricional. O silenciamento de SK ou SKR desregulou a homeostase energética, elevou o consumo alimentar, depletou reservas energéticas, reduziu a tolerância ao estresse e prejudicou severamente a reprodução; inversamente, a injeção do peptídeo SK suprimiu a alimentação no período inicial e restringiu significativamente o ganho de massa larval entre 48 e 72 h. A entrega oral de dsRNA bacteriano anti-SK ou anti-SKR desencadeou resposta de RNAi efetiva, elevando a mortalidade larval e atrasando o desenvolvimento.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece um paralelo direto para os programas de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas e eixo neuropeptidérgico em lepidópteros do LUCHM (Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis), validando dsRNA bacteriano oral contra receptores neuropeptidérgicos.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Mapear ortólogos de sulfacinina/SKR em Spodoptera frugiperda e testar se o silenciamento oral prejudica a integridade metabólica intestinal ou potencializa a letalidade de protoxinas Cry/Vip3 de Bacillus thuringiensis.

43077712.titulo: Natural Infection Induces Antibodies Targeting Pfs230 Domains D1M and D7D8 with Potential for Malaria Transmission Blocking.
43077712.autores: Harju T, Cao Y, Kumar N (3 autores)
43077712.resumo: Anticorpos naturais contra os domínios D1M e D7D8 de Pfs230 (candidato a vacina de bloqueio de transmissão) foram correlacionados em sorologia de Zimbábue (n = 301) e Tailândia (n = 44).
43077712.resumo_original: The natural immunogenicity of domain 1 (D1M) and domains 7 and 8 (D7D8) in Plasmodium falciparum transmission-blocking vaccine (TBV) candidate Pfs230 is assessed. Antibody reactivity by ELISA using endemic human sera from Zimbabwe (n = 301) and Thailand (n = 44) was evaluated. Regression analyses revealed significant positive correlations between responses to both domains. A 1-log increase in Pfs230-D1M reactivity predicted a 0.43- to 0.87-log increase in Pfs230-D7D8 reactivity across cohorts. Furthermore, Pfs230-D1M positivity increased the odds of Pfs230-D7D8 positivity by 59% to 89%. These data demonstrate that both Pfs230-D1M and Pfs230-D7D8 are highly immunogenic during natural infection, validating their potential as strong TBV candidates.

resumo_blocos.racional: A proteína de superfície de gametócitos/gametas Pfs230 é um dos principais candidatos a vacina de bloqueio de transmissão (TBV) contra Plasmodium falciparum, mas a imunogenicidade natural comparativa de regiões específicas da molécula em áreas endêmicas precisa ser quantificada. O trabalho avaliou respostas de anticorpos humanos contra o domínio 1 (D1M) e os domínios 7 e 8 (D7D8) de Pfs230.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios imunoenzimáticos (ELISA) utilizando soros humanos de áreas endêmicas para malária no Zimbábue (n = 301) e na Tailândia (n = 44), seguidos de análises de regressão para mensurar correlação quantitativa e razão de chances entre reatividade a Pfs230-D1M e Pfs230-D7D8.

Cada incremento de 1 log na reatividade a Pfs230-D1M previu aumento de 0,43 a 0,87 log na reatividade a Pfs230-D7D8, e a soropositividade para Pfs230-D1M elevou em 59% a 89% a chance de positividade para Pfs230-D7D8, confirmando que ambos os domínios são altamente imunogênicos durante a infecção natural.

43079506.titulo: A national geocoded inventory of Aedes mosquitoes in Kenya: integrating published, archival, and digital sources across 124 years.
43079506.autores: Muchiri SK, Mwangi LW, … Snow RW (8 autores)
43079506.resumo: Inventário nacional geocodificado de Aedes no Quênia, integrando fontes publicadas, de arquivo e digitais.
43079506.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes, represent growing public health threats in Kenya and across sub-Saharan Africa. In the absence of licensed vaccines for either disease in Africa, targeted vector control remains the primary prevention strategy, making accurate knowledge of Aedes species distributions essential. Global inventories of Aedes species are severely under-representative for Kenya, with existing repositories documenting fewer than 200 unique locations. No comprehensive, geocoded national inventory integrating published, unpublished, and digital sources has previously been assembled.
Three complementary approaches were used to assemble a national geocoded inventory of Aedes species in Kenya including (i) a systematic review of peer-reviewed literature, theses, and conference abstracts; (ii) digitisation of unpublished archival reports from the Ministry of Health, Division of Insect-Borne/Vector-Borne Diseases (DIBD/DVBD), regional and municipal councils; and (iii) cross-referencing with Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and Walter Reed Biosystematics Unit's (WRBU) VectorMap repositories. Data were extracted using a standardised template, de-duplicated, and geocoded using Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates, Google Earth, or census enumeration area shapefiles. Aedes species were classified as principal or possible secondary vectors based on confirmed field detection and, for the principal vector, an established role in transmission during dengue and chikungunya outbreaks reported in Kenya.
A total of 1,802 time-site records were identified across 855 unique locations between 1901 and 2024, documenting 104 Aedes species. Unpublished archival records contributed 51% of all records, with peer-reviewed articles accounting for 43%. The principal vector, Aedes aegypti was the most widely documented species, reported at 522 unique locations. Eight possible secondary vectors with confirmed DENV and/or CHIKV detection were documented, with Aedes mcintoshi, Ae. ochraceus, and Ae. tricholabis the most frequently recorded. Geographic coverage was concentrated along the coast and western Kenya, with notable surveillance gaps in northern and northeastern regions.
This inventory represents the most comprehensive geocoded database of Aedes mosquito species ever assembled for Kenya, substantially exceeding the coverage of existing global repositories. It provides an essential empirical foundation for disease and vector surveillance, ecological niche modelling (ENM) and sub-national targeting of vector control interventions in Kenya.

resumo_blocos.racional: Na ausência de vacinas amplamente licenciadas contra dengue e chikungunya na África, o controle vetorial direcionado depende criticamente de mapas precisos de ocorrência de mosquitos Aedes. Até então, repositórios globais sub-representavam severamente o Quênia, registrando menos de 200 localidades únicas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de três fontes complementares entre 1901 e 2024: (i) revisão sistemática de literatura revisada por pares, teses e resumos de congressos; (ii) digitalização de relatórios arquivísticos inéditos do Ministério da Saúde queniano (DIBD/DVBD) e conselhos regionais/municipais; e (iii) cruzamento com GBIF e VectorMap (WRBU). Os registros foram padronizados, deduplicados e geocodificados via GPS, Google Earth ou malhas censitárias, classificando vetores principais e potenciais secundários pela detecção confirmada de DENV e/ou CHIKV.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Foram consolidados 1.802 registros espaço-temporais em 855 localidades únicas, documentando 104 espécies de Aedes, com 51% dos dados oriundos de arquivos inéditos e 43% de artigos publicados. 43081930.titulo: Developmental site type, larval productivity, and insecticide susceptibility of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
43081930.autores: Zongo S, Toe HK, … Namountougou M (12 autores)
43081930.resumo: Tipo de criadouro, produtividade larval e suscetibilidade a inseticida de Aedes aegypti.
43081930.resumo_original: Arboviral diseases, including dengue and chikungunya, are increasing in sub-Saharan Africa. This study assessed Aedes aegypti larval productivity across three container types and examined associations with abiotic parameters and insecticide resistance patterns in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. From July to September 2024, a semi-field experiment was conducted at the Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme. Tires, terracotta jars, and buckets were exposed outdoors for natural colonization. Larval abundance and six abiotic parameters (pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity, total dissolved solids, and redox potential) were recorded over 11 rounds. Susceptibility bioassays were performed on emerging Ae. aegypti adults using deltamethrin (0.03%), bendiocarb (0.2%), and malathion (1.5%). A total of 14,020 larvae were collected, of which 93.13% were Ae. aegypti. Tires (mean = 83.3 ± 10.8 larvae/container) and terracotta jars (mean = 50.7 ± 7.4 larvae/container) harbored significantly more larvae than buckets (mean = 22.5 ± 3.3 larvae/container); tires and jars did not differ significantly. Generalized linear mixed model analysis showed no significant effect of abiotic parameters, while container type was strongly associated with abundance. Ae. aegypti populations were resistant to deltamethrin in all container types (mortality 5.2%-17.9%) and to malathion in both tested container types (mortality 88.4%-88.8%). For bendiocarb, populations were resistant in plastic buckets (85.3% mortality), showed suspected resistance in tires (91.6%), and were susceptible in terracotta jars (98.6%). Vector control should prioritize the management of tires and terracotta jars, and widespread pyrethroid resistance highlights the need for alternative tools.

resumo_blocos.racional: O avanço das arboviroses na África Subsaariana exige compreender quais tipos de criadouros sustentam maior produtividade larval de Aedes aegypti e como os adultos emergentes respondem aos inseticidas em uso. O estudo avaliou produtividade larval, parâmetros físico-químicos da água e resistência a inseticidas em Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Experimento em semicampo no Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme (julho a setembro de 2024, 11 rodadas) expondo pneus, potes de terracota e baldes plásticos à colonização natural. Mediram-se abundância larval e seis parâmetros abióticos (pH, temperatura, salinidade, condutividade, sólidos totais dissolvidos e potencial redox) analisados por modelos lineares mistos generalizados (GLMM), além de bioensaios de suscetibilidade em adultos emergentes com deltametrina (0,03%), bendiocarbe (0,2%) e malationa (1,5%).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Coletaram-se 14.020 larvas (93,13% de Ae. aegypti), com produtividade significativamente maior em pneus (média 83,3 ± 10,8 larvas/recipiente) e potes de terracota (50,7 ± 7,4) do que em baldes (22,5 ± 3,3), sem efeito significativo dos parâmetros abióticos no GLMM. Os adultos exibiram forte resistência à deltametrina em todos os criadouros (mortalidade de 5,2% a 17,9%) e resistência à malationa nos dois tipos testados (88,4%–88,8%); para bendiocarbe, houve resistência em baldes (85,3%), resistência suspeita em pneus (91,6%) e suscetibilidade em potes de terracota (98,6%).

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Demonstra que o tipo de criadouro (pneus e terracota) condiciona não apenas a densidade larval, mas também variações na suscetibilidade fenotípica de adultos emergentes a carbamatos, reforçando a necessidade de controle larvário e alternativas aos piretroides.

43083712.titulo: Down-Regulation of eIF3L Is Associated with Decreased Susceptibility of Helicoverpa armigera to Cry1Ac.
43083712.autores: Li N, Zhang C, … Liang G (8 autores)
43083712.resumo: A queda de eIF3L se associou a menor suscetibilidade de Helicoverpa armigera a Cry1Ac e afeta a expressão dos receptores CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3.
43083712.resumo_original: Large-scale cultivation of transgenic Bt crops has led to target pest resistance to Bt proteins, especially Cry1Ac. Under persistent selection pressure, Helicoverpa armigera has evolved resistance to Bt proteins in both laboratory and field populations, highlighting an urgent need to comprehensively elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying pest Bt resistance. Previous studies have confirmed that the eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF2 plays a critical role in regulating Bt resistance. Our prior RNA-seq data showed significant differences in the expression level of eIF3L between susceptible and Cry1Ac-resistant strains of H. armigera. In this study, we further observed that the mRNA level of eIF3L was significantly reduced in larvae surviving Cry1Ac exposure. More importantly, heterologous expression of eIF3L increased the susceptibility of Sf9 cells to Cry1Ac. Consistently, knockdown of eIF3L was associated with reduced mortality in H. armigera larvae exposed to Cry1Ac. Together, our in vivo and in vitro results suggest that eIF3L is involved in Cry1Ac toxicity. Furthermore, eIF3L affects the expression of the Cry1Ac receptor genes CAD, ABCC2, and ABCC3. Collectively, these results indicate that down-regulation of eIF3L is associated with decreased susceptibility of H. armigera to Cry1Ac, providing novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying insect resistance to Bt proteins.

resumo_blocos.racional: O cultivo extensivo de culturas transgênicas Bt selecionou resistência à toxina Cry1Ac em populações de campo e laboratório de Helicoverpa armigera. Após identificar expressão diferencial do fator de iniciação traducional eIF3L em dados prévios de RNA-seq entre linhagens suscetíveis e resistentes, os autores investigaram o papel funcional de eIF3L na toxicidade de Cry1Ac.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Quantificação de mRNA de eIF3L em larvas de H. armigera sobreviventes à exposição a Cry1Ac, expressão heteróloga de eIF3L em células Sf9 (Spodoptera frugiperda) desafiadas com Cry1Ac, silenciamento gênico (knockdown) de eIF3L in vivo em larvas expostas à toxina e análise de expressão dos genes receptores CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Os transcritos de eIF3L mostraram-se significativamente reduzidos nas larvas sobreviventes ao tratamento com Cry1Ac. A expressão heteróloga de eIF3L aumentou a suscetibilidade das células Sf9 à Cry1Ac, enquanto o knockdown de eIF3L reduziu a mortalidade das larvas de H. armigera expostas à toxina. Adicionalmente, eIF3L modulou a expressão dos receptores de Cry1Ac CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3, ligando a maquinaria de tradução à densidade de receptores de toxina na membrana intestinal.

43082033.titulo: Trained immunity in sepsis from immune reprogramming to precision immunotherapy.
43082033.autores: Liu N, Gan T, … Wang Z (5 autores)
43082033.resumo: Revisão sobre imunidade treinada em sepse, da reprogramação imune à imunoterapia de precisão.
43082033.resumo_original: Sepsis represents a severe systemic inflammatory response to infection, with complex immune dysregulation at the core of its pathophysiology. Conventional therapies remain limited to effectively modulate immune status while controlling infection, contributing to high mortality rates and severe long-term complications.In recent years, trained immunity,a form of innate immune memory, has demonstrated novel potential for regulating immune responses through metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation. This narrative review integrates mechanistic and translational evidence on trained immunity in sepsis, with particular emphasis on key signalling pathways, their contributions to immune dysregulation, and potential biomarkers. It further discusses emerging precision immunotherapy strategies.Targeting trained immunity and assesses their opportunities and challenges in clinical translation, with particular emphasis on personalised treatment design and safety evaluation.Finally, we consider the application prospects of trained immunity in the long-term chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction associated with sepsis. However, direct clinical evidence remains limited, and validated biomarkers for identifying trained immune states in patients with sepsis are currently lacking. Future multidisciplinary studies are therefore needed to define clinically relevant trained immune states and establish reliable biomarkers for precision immune intervention in sepsis.

resumo_blocos.racional: A sepse caracteriza-se por resposta inflamatória sistêmica severa com desregulação imune complexa e elevada mortalidade mesmo sob terapias convencionais. Esta revisão narrativa examina como a imunidade treinada — memória imune inata sustentada por reprogramação metabólica e epigenética — pode explicar a disfunção imune crônica e orientar estratégias de imunoterapia de precisão.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Síntese crítica de evidências mecanísticas e translacionais sobre vias de sinalização da imunidade treinada, marcadores metabólicos e epigenéticos, biomarcadores potenciais e desafios de desenho personalizado e segurança clínica na sepse.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A revisão integra vias de reprogramação metabólica e remodelamento epigenético associadas tanto à hiperinflamação quanto à imunoparalisia pós-sepse e às sequelas inflamatórias de longo prazo. Contudo, ressalta que a evidência clínica direta ainda é limitada e que faltam biomarcadores validados para estratificar estados de imunidade treinada em pacientes sépticos antes da intervenção imune personalizada.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece referencial conceitual para interpretar reprogramação metabólica e epigenética de monócitos/macrófagos em quadros inflamatórios sistêmicos graves comparáveis à malária grave e à malária cerebral.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar se a exposição prévia a hemo livre ou hemozoína induz assinatura metabólica/epigenética de imunidade treinada ou tolerância em células mieloides e endotélio cerebral na infecção por Plasmodium.

43081668.titulo: Epigenetic Crosstalk Between BCG-Infected Macrophages and Naïve Monocytes: Potential Role of the Extracellular Vesicles.
43081668.autores: Ellinger L, Alipoor SD, … Lerm M (6 autores)
43081668.resumo: Fatores solúveis e vesículas extracelulares de macrófagos infectados com BCG alteram a metilação de DNA de monócitos naive, com tendência a menor carga de Mtb.
43081668.resumo_original: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of death from infectious disease. Infected cells secrete extracellular vesicles (EVs), nanosized membrane-bound particles containing bioactive molecules known to mediate intercellular communication and may contribute to immune regulation during infection. We hypothesized that factors released by Mycobacterium bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-infected macrophages (MΦs), including EVs, could contribute to epigenetic remodeling of naïve monocytes and influence their response to subsequent Mtb infection. A transwell co-culture system enabled communication via soluble factors and EVs between BCG-infected MΦs and naïve monocytes undergoing differentiation into recipient MΦs. The recipient MΦs exhibited altered DNA methylation patterns compared to those co-cultured with untreated, Staphylococcus aureus-infected or hydrogen peroxide-exposed MΦs. These DNA methylation changes were accompanied by a trend toward lower GFP-based Mtb burden in vitro. BCG-infected MΦs released EVs with a distinct proteomic profile enriched in tuberculosis-related pathways. Exploratory integration of the EV proteomic and DNA methylation datasets from the recipient MΦs identified potential molecular associations, including a TNF-centered network enriched in phagosome and tuberculosis pathways. These findings indicate that exposure to the intercellular environment generated by BCG-infected MΦs, including EVs and soluble factors, is associated with DNA methylation changes and modulation of antimycobacterial responses in recipient cells. Further studies using purified EVs and targeted mechanistic approaches are required to define the relative roles of EVs and other soluble mediators.

43078098.titulo: Flashing light modulates insect behavior in a species-specific manner.
43078098.autores: Ali MS, Luo X, … Holmes TC (4 autores)
43078098.resumo: Luz intermitente modula o comportamento de insetos de modo espécie-específico (Curr Biol). Só título e metadados lidos; abstract não consultado.
43078098.resumo_original: Light is a powerful tool to study animal behavior.1-3 In contrast to natural light, almost all artificial light exhibits flicker, but most work on insect behavioral responses to light flicker focuses on flicker perceptual detection. We tested photopreference light-choice behavior across a wide range of Drosophila species in response to rhythmically flickering light using custom FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues) instrumentation and find species-specific behavioral responses and altered time-of-day-ordered behaviors that are evoked by light frequencies far beyond perceptual flicker frequency. Mutant analysis shows that behavioral responses to FLASH rely on all known classes of phototransduction, including Cryptochrome and Rhodopsin-7 expressed directly in brain neurons and the eyes. FLASH behavioral responses are abolished following ablation of the pigment-dispersing factor (PDF)-positive lateral ventral neuron circadian light input hub and in circadian mutants. These results suggest means for designing ecologically friendly light devices for species-specific insect behavioral control.

resumo_blocos.racional: Diferentemente da luz solar natural, fontes artificiais exibem cintilação (flicker) rítmica, mas a resposta comportamental dos insetos além da frequência perceptiva de fusão permanecia pouco explorada. Os autores investigaram como luz cintilante espectralmente modulada altera a fotopreferência e ritmos comportamentais em múltiplas espécies de Drosophila.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios comportamentais de escolha luminosa em painel de espécies de Drosophila utilizando instrumentação customizada FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues), combinados a análise de mutantes de fotorrecepção (incluindo Cryptochrome e Rhodopsin-7) e ablação genética do centro circadiano de neurônios ventrais laterais positivos para PDF.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A luz cintilante evocou respostas de fotopreferência espécie-específicas e alterou comportamentos ordenados por hora do dia mesmo em frequências muito superiores ao limiar perceptivo de cintilação. Análise com mutantes mostrou dependência de todas as classes conhecidas de fototransdução — incluindo Cryptochrome e Rhodopsin-7 expressos em neurônios cerebrais e olhos — e abolição completa da resposta após ablação do hub circadiano PDF+ ou em mutantes circadianos.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Dialoga com os estudos de neurobiologia, ritmos circadianos e comportamento de dípteros do LUCHM, sugerindo que cintilação espectral acoplada a vias PDF/Cryptochrome permite modular comportamento vetorial de forma espécie-específica.

43081641.titulo: Dietary Hercynine Protects Intestinal Stem Cell Function During Epithelial Repair and Aging Through Insulin Signaling.
43081641.autores: Zhang Q, Fu F, … Chen H (10 autores)
43081641.resumo: A hercinina protege células-tronco intestinais de Drosophila no reparo e no envelhecimento via sinalização de insulina; a microbiota remodelada parece resposta acompanhante, não causa.
43081641.resumo_original: Intestinal stem cell (ISC) dysfunction compromises epithelial repair and contributes to intestinal aging, yet naturally derived metabolites that preserve ISC homeostasis remain incompletely defined. Through metabolomic profiling of a standardized edible mushroom extract, we identified hercynine (HER) as the most abundant detected metabolite and investigated its role in intestinal repair and aging. In Drosophila, HER accelerated post-injury epithelial repair by promoting timely restoration of ISC/progenitor dynamics and epithelial differentiation. During physiological aging, mid-life HER supplementation preferentially attenuated age-associated ISC/progenitor dysfunction, accompanied by improved intestinal homeostasis, enhanced organismal fitness, and extended lifespan. Mechanistically, HER shifted aged ISC/progenitor transcriptomes toward a more youth-associated state, with genetic and pharmacological pathway-perturbation experiments supporting the functional involvement of insulin signaling in HER-mediated improvements in aged ISC/progenitor homeostasis. HER was also associated with remodeling of the gut microbiota during injury repair and aging; microbiota perturbation experiments suggested that this remodeling represented an accompanying response to HER treatment rather than the primary driver of ISC protection. In aged human small intestinal organoids, HER improved budding capacity, ISC/progenitor-associated activity, and epithelial differentiation, while reducing p-AKT levels, supporting a conserved epithelial response in a mammalian model. Together, these findings identify HER as a mushroom-derived metabolite that supports ISC-centered intestinal epithelial repair and mitigates intestinal aging, highlighting dietary metabolites as potential modulators of stem cell-associated epithelial homeostasis during tissue repair and aging.

43077227.titulo: Krüppel regulates cell cycle exit and limits adult neurogenesis of mushroom body neural progenitors in Drosophila.
43077227.autores: Chen D, Man J, … Kimata Y (7 autores)
43077227.resumo: Em Drosophila, Krüppel regula a saída do ciclo celular e a eliminação dos neuroblastos do corpo pedunculado; sua depleção prolonga a vida dos neuroblastos e permite neurogênese adulta, via Imp, com Kr-h1 antagonizando Kr.
43077227.resumo_original: Neural progenitors typically exit the cell cycle during development, limiting adult neurogenesis. Here, we identify Krüppel (Kr) as a regulator of cell cycle exit and elimination of mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) in Drosophila. Neuroblast (NB)-specific Kr RNAi and the Irregular facet (KrIf-1) mutation prolong MBNB lifespan and enable continued adult neurogenesis. Despite low post-embryonic expression, pupal stage-specific Kr depletion or misexpression causes MBNB retention, revealing a role distinct from its established embryonic function. Persistent MBNBs retain the early temporal factor IGF2 mRNA-binding protein (Imp) and fail to fully induce the late temporal factors Syncrip (Syp) and Eip93F (E93). Imp co-depletion suppresses MBNB retention following Kr depletion, identifying Imp as a key downstream effector. Krüppel homolog 1 (Kr-h1), a hormone-responsive transcription factor, functionally antagonises Kr by suppressing E93 expression. Kr-h1 knockdown partially rescues MBNB retention caused by Kr depletion, whereas its overexpression drives tumour-like NB overgrowth. Together, these findings identify Kr as a lineage-specific regulator coordinating the Imp/Syp transition and E93 expression to promote timely MBNB termination. This work reveals how temporal regulators control neural progenitor lifespan and restrict adult neurogenesis, linking intrinsic developmental programmes with hormone-responsive pathways in the Drosophila brain.

resumo_blocos.racional: Progenitores neurais tipicamente encerram o ciclo celular durante o desenvolvimento para restringir a neurogênese adulta. Os autores investigaram como o fator transcricional Krüppel (Kr) coordena a saída do ciclo celular e a eliminação programada dos neuroblastos do corpo cogumelar (MBNBs) no cérebro de Drosophila.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Depleção por RNAi específica de neuroblastos, uso do mutante KrIf-1, manipulação temporal restrita à fase pupal, ensaios de co-depleção genética com Imp e análises de antagonismo funcional com o fator responsivo a hormônios Krüppel homolog 1 (Kr-h1) e expressão de Syncrip (Syp) e Eip93F (E93).
resumo_blocos.resultados: A perda de função de Kr (por RNAi, mutação KrIf-1 ou depleção pupal — distinta da função embrionária) prolongou a sobrevida dos MBNBs e manteve neurogênese adulta contínua. Neuroblastos persistentes retiveram o fator temporal precoce Imp (IGF2 mRNA-binding protein) e falharam em induzir plenamente os fatores tardios Syp e E93; a co-depleção de Imp suprimiu essa retenção. Além disso, Kr-h1 antagonizou funcionalmente Kr ao reprimir E93, sendo que o knockdown de Kr-h1 resgatou parcialmente a retenção de MBNBs enquanto sua superexpressão promoveu hiperproliferação tumoral.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Esclarece a integração entre fatores temporais intrínsecos (Imp/Syp/E93) e sinalização hormonal (Kr-h1) na plasticidade neural de dípteros, relevante para compreensão do neurodesenvolvimento e remodelamento cerebral de vetores.

43073441.titulo: Helical repeat protein mRSiC is required for rRNA fragment accumulation in T. gondii mitochondria.
43073441.autores: Drakoulis N, Maschmann S, … Tetzlaff S (12 autores)
43073441.resumo: A proteína de repetição helicoidal mRSiC é necessária para o acúmulo de fragmentos de rRNA na mitocôndria de Toxoplasma gondii (EMBO Rep).
43073441.resumo_original: Myzozoans, including apicomplexan parasites Plasmodium falciparum and Toxoplasma gondii, possess unusual mitochondrial genomes that only encode two to three respiratory chain subunits and extensively fragmented rRNAs forming a divergent mitoribosome. Heptatricopeptide repeat (HPR) proteins are expanded in myzozoans, with some functioning as mitoribosomal constituents. Additional HPR proteins have been proposed to function in post-transcriptional mitochondrial gene expression, though their specific roles remain unexplored. We present a phylogenetic analysis of HPR proteins that reveals extensive lineage-specific expansions, consistent with diversifications of mitochondrial gene expression systems within myzozoans. We further characterize mRSiC, a HPR found in T. gondii and its closest relatives. Using sRNA sequencing and RNA gel blot analyses, we show that mRSiC is required for the stabilization of two lineage-specific mitochondrial sRNAs, RNA33 and RNA42. Loss of mRSiC causes rapid depletion of these RNAs, followed by secondary reductions of rRNA fragments, defects in the respiratory chain, and impaired parasite proliferation. Together, these findings highlight the importance of HPRs in apicomplexan mitochondrial gene expression and illustrate how lineage-specific RNA-binding factors support highly derived mitochondrial expression systems.

resumo_blocos.racional: Parasitos apicomplexos como Plasmodium falciparum e Toxoplasma gondii mantêm genomas mitocondriais minimalistas que codificam apenas duas a três subunidades da cadeia respiratória e rRNAs extensivamente fragmentados montados em um mitorribossomo divergente. O trabalho investigou como proteínas com repetições heptatricopeptídicas (HPR) expandidas em myzozoários sustentam essa expressão gênica mitocondrial pós-transcricional.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise filogenômica comparativa de proteínas HPR em myzozoários seguida de caracterização funcional da proteína mRSiC em Toxoplasma gondii por sequenciamento de pequenos RNAs (sRNA-seq), Northern/gel blot de RNA, ensaios de cadeia respiratória e proliferação parasitária.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A filogenia revelou expansões linhagem-específicas de proteínas HPR acompanhando a diversificação dos sistemas de expressão mitocondrial em myzozoários. Em T. gondii, a perda de mRSiC provocou rápida depleção de dois pequenos RNAs mitocondriais linhagem-específicos (RNA33 e RNA42), seguida por redução secundária dos fragmentos de rRNA, defeitos na cadeia respiratória e comprometimento severo da proliferação do parasito.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Ilustra mecanismos altamente divergentes de estabilização de sRNAs e rRNAs fragmentados mitocondriais em apicomplexos, apontando vulnerabilidades moleculares conservadas em família HPR também expandida em Plasmodium.

43083739.titulo: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Remodeling of the Cockroach Brain Following Envenomation by Parasitoid Wasp Ampulex compressa.
43083739.autores: Miroliubov A, Lianguzova A, … Libersat F (6 autores)
43083739.resumo: Transcriptoma e metabolômica do cérebro de Periplaneta americana 24 h após envenenamento por Ampulex compressa: 331 genes diferenciais, sinalização aminérgica alterada e aumento de ácido fumárico e sorbitol.
43083739.resumo_original: The parasitoid jewel wasp Ampulex compressa induces prolonged hypokinesia in its cockroach host, Periplaneta americana, by injecting venom into the central nervous system. Although acute behavioral effects are well characterized, molecular processes associated with persistent hypokinesia remain poorly understood. We combined transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics to characterize brain changes 24 h after envenomation. RNA-seq of the central brain region containing the central complex and adjacent tissue identified 331 differentially expressed genes: 267 upregulated and 64 downregulated. Increased expression of tyrosine decarboxylase-like and arrestin-domain genes, together with reduced expression of a putative tyramine/octopamine receptor, suggests altered regulation of aminergic signaling. Changes in synaptic vesicle and innexin transcripts further implicate chemical and electrical synaptic function. Immune, detoxification, and extracellular-matrix genes were also affected. Independent metabolomic analyses revealed significant increases in fumaric acid and sorbitol, consistent with altered energy metabolism. Tyramine, octopamine, glutamate, and GABA showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction, although several showed greater inter-individual variation in stung cockroaches. Together, these findings identify changes in neuromodulatory signaling, synaptic organization, and metabolic support as candidate processes associated with persistent hypokinesia. Their contributions to behavioral suppression remain to be distinguished from downstream responses to reduced neural activity and tissue stress.

43078171.titulo: Beyond taste: internal nutrient sensing and endocrine roles of selected insect gustatory receptors.
43078171.autores: Zhang W, Sun J, Mang D (3 autores)
43078171.resumo: Revisão das funções fisiológicas de receptores gustativos em sensoriamento interno de nutrientes, como Gr43a em Drosophila e BmGr9 em Bombyx, incluindo sinalização endócrina e proliferação hematopoiética.
43078171.resumo_original: Gustatory receptors (GRs) are best known for detecting chemicals that influence insect feeding and behavior. Studies of selected receptors, predominantly sugar-responsive GRs, have also established roles in internal nutrient sensing and physiological regulation. Fructose-responsive receptors such as Drosophila melanogaster Gr43a and Bombyx mori BmGr9 illustrate how internal carbohydrate availability can influence feeding, endocrine signaling, and hematopoietic proliferation. Other sugar-responsive GRs have been implicated in gut peptide hormone signaling and metabolic regulation. Here, we examine the experimental evidence for these functions and distinguish established receptor-specific mechanisms from broader hypotheses concerning the GR family. We discuss how structural biology, single-cell approaches, and comparative functional studies can define the distribution and mechanisms of physiological GR functions. These findings motivate a framework connecting chemical sensing with internal physiological state, while their generality across GR lineages and contribution to ecological adaptation remain open questions.

43083678.titulo: Hybrid Epidemiological-Neural Modelling of Dengue Under Climate-Socioeconomic Influence.
43083678.autores: Adeniji A, Mahmood A, … He Z (4 autores)
43083678.resumo: Modelagem híbrida epidemiológico-neural de dengue sob influência climática e socioeconômica.
43083678.resumo_original: Dengue transmission in climate-sensitive and socioeconomically heterogeneous settings arises from nonlinear interactions between environmental suitability, mosquito ecology, and human behaviour. Classical SEIR-type models offer mechanistic interpretability but are often constrained by observational noise and incomplete data, while purely data-driven approaches typically fail to respect underlying transmission dynamics. In this study, we introduce a hybrid epidemiological framework that embeds a temperature-unemployment driven SEIR-SEI model within a Physics-Informed Neural Network (SEIR-PINN). Using weekly dengue incidence data from Medellín, Colombia, we incorporate unemployment as a socioeconomic proxy that modulates transmission alongside climatic suitability. The Model performance was evaluated in two ways; the prediction of observed incidence, the SEIR-PINN achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.05 and R2 of 0.975, compared with MAE of 43.57 and R2 of 0.870 for a mechanistic SEIR-SEI baseline fitted under identical climatic and socioeconomic assumptions. Shuffled five-fold cross-validation provided held-out prediction of observed incidence within the 2009-2011 period, with mean MAE of 14.87 and mean R2 of 0.977 (out-of-fold MAE 14.89, R2 0.978). These held-out results interpolate within the observed epidemic and are not an assessment of prospective forecasting performance Importantly, the SEIR-PINN reconstructs latent human and mosquito compartments that remain biologically consistent across epidemic phases. By fusing mechanistic structure with data-adaptive flexibility, the proposed SEIR-PINN provides an interpretable framework for analysing the joint climatic and socioeconomic modulation of dengue transmission in an urban endemic setting. Although using Medellín as a single-city methodological case study, application of this framework to other dengue endemic settings requires external validation using additional locations, longer time periods, and independent datasets. The results therefore support the potential use of physics-informed hybrid models as interpretable tools for dengue surveillance and transmission-dynamics research, while recognising the need for further external validation across longer time periods and additional geographical regions.

43077045.titulo: Mosquito Population Dynamics Across Successive Gonotrophic Cycles: A Structured Multiscale Mathematical Approach.
43077045.autores: Nforba GDY, Teboh-Ewungkem MI, Ngwa GA (3 autores)
43077045.resumo: Modelo multiescala estruturado da dinâmica populacional de mosquitos ao longo de ciclos gonotróficos sucessivos.
43077045.resumo_original: We develop a structured multiscale mathematical model for mosquito population dynamics that explicitly links gonotrophic-cycle processes to population-level demographic outcomes across multiple reproductive cycles. The model couples breeding-site movement, resting, oviposition, density-dependent recruitment, mortality, human biting, and repeated reproductive cycling, thereby quantifying contributions of mosquitoes that survive to complete multiple cycles. As a first step toward understanding the role of gonotrophic cycling in mosquito-borne disease transmission, we focus on mosquito demography, with the human population held at demographic equilibrium. We characterize the steady states of the model and their stability, derive a basic offspring number governing mosquito persistence, and investigate bifurcation behaviour and parameter sensitivity. The results show that incorporating additional gonotrophic cycles increases reproductive contributions and can qualitatively alter persistence predictions. Parameter regimes yielding extinction with one or two cycles can support persistence when a third cycle is included, while additional cycles can shift stable populations into oscillatory regimes at lower oviposition rates. Shortening the gonotrophic cycle can further promote persistence under low oviposition and modestly alter oscillation frequency and amplitude at higher oviposition. Sensitivity analysis identifies early gonotrophic-cycle processes, particularly first-cycle oviposition, successful blood feeding, and breeding-to-questing progression, as dominant regulators of the basic offspring number. More generally, oviposition, breeding-to-questing movement, biting, successful blood feeding, and return rates positively influence the basic offspring number, whereas stage-specific mortality acts negatively; the effects of later-cycle parameters are increasingly weighted by successful progression through preceding cycles. These results demonstrate that explicitly representing successive gonotrophic cycles can materially change predicted mosquito persistence, stability, and potential control targets.

43083672.titulo: Insecticide Resistance in Anopheles stephensi: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Native and Invasive Populations.
43083672.autores: Eshetu D, Gadisa E, … Yan G (10 autores)
43083672.resumo: Revisão sistemática e metanálise de resistência a inseticidas em Anopheles stephensi, em populações nativas e invasoras.
43083672.resumo_original:
The rapid spread of the invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi in Africa, coupled with increasing reports of insecticide resistance, presents an emerging challenge for malaria vector control. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare insecticide resistance profiles and underlying resistance mechanisms between native Asian and invasive African populations and assessed their implications for insecticide resistance management.
PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, WHO IRIS, and gray literature sources were searched using terms related to An. stephensi, insecticide susceptibility, and resistance mechanisms. Data were extracted into Excel, critically appraised using an adapted Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-analysis software. The protocol was registered in Prospero International Registrar for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis in April 2025 (ID: CRD420251007131).
Thirty-one studies published between 2000 and 2025 were included. Pooled mortality was lower in invasive than native populations for the pyrethroids assessed in both ranges, including deltamethrin (72.6% vs. 83.5%), permethrin (68.3% vs. 89.0%), and lambda-cyhalothrin (47.0% vs. 87.0%), as well as for DDT (36.0% vs. 47.7%). Mortality was also lower in invasive populations for bendiocarb and propoxur, although propoxur was assessed in only one native-range study. Between-study heterogeneity varied substantially. Target-site mutations were reported at low frequencies; L1014F ranged from 1.4% to 32.9% in native populations and was detected in one study in invasive-range (5.7%), while L1014S (21.4-35%) was reported only in native-range. Metabolic resistance mechanisms involved cytochrome P450s (CYP4 and CYP6 families), glutathione S-transferases (GSTe2 and GSTe4), and esterases, including esterase E4 and carboxylesterase-6. No acetylcholinesterase-1 (ace-1) mutations were reported.
Anopheles stephensi exhibits resistance to multiple insecticide classes across its native and invasive ranges, with lower pooled mortality observed in the invasive range. Available evidence indicates an important contribution of metabolic detoxification, while target-site resistance markers, including vgsc L1014F/L1014S, were detected at lower frequencies and remain poorly characterized in invasive populations. High between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation and highlights the need for standardized phenotypic and molecular surveillance to guide locally tailored insecticide resistance management as An. stephensi continues to spread in Africa.

Esta revisão sistemática com metanálise comparou perfis de resistência e mecanismos moleculares entre populações nativas asiáticas e populações invasoras africanas.

10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.titulo: Population genomics of the Anopheles farauti complex reveals a distinct regime of malaria vector evolution in the southwest Pacific
10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.resumo: Preprint de genômica populacional do complexo Anopheles farauti, com um regime distinto de evolução de vetor de malária (não revisado por pares; só título lido).
10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.resumo_original: Abstract: The southwest Pacific has one of the highest per-capita malaria burdens outside Africa, yet how its malaria mosquitoes evolve is largely unknown. In African vectors, insecticide resistance evolves rapidly in large, connected populations carrying abundant standing variation. Southwest Pacific vectors show little to no biochemical resistance despite decades of insecticide-based control. We analyse 495 genomes from six taxa of the Anopheles farauti complex, which includes the region's major vectors. The complex radiated rapidly in the late Pleistocene concomitant to the peopling of Near Oceania. Thereafter, post-glacial sea-level rise and climate change fragmented its populations into recently colonised island isolates. Successive environmental and colonisation bottlenecks left a legacy of extraordinary inbreeding, most marked in island populations of the coastal specialist An. farauti sensu stricto, where sustained low effective population size has allowed deleterious alleles to be purged effectively; the inland generalists An. hinesorum and An. oreios retain more variation. After five decades of chemical control we recover a single resistance sweep, at Gste2, alongside recent selection at species-specific chemosensory gene repertoires. Severe inbreeding and the loss of standing variation have not prevented ecological success, challenging assumptions about how much variation and connectivity a vector population needs to thrive. This work establishes the first genomic foundation for this major vector system of endemic species through a biogeographically diverse region of the world.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o Pacífico Sudoeste concentre algumas das maiores taxas per capita de malária fora da África, seus vetores do complexo Anopheles farauti exibiram pouca ou nenhuma resistência bioquímica após décadas de controle químico, em forte contraste com vetores africanos altamente polimórficos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise populacional genômica de 495 genomas abrangendo seis táxons do complexo Anopheles farauti, reconstruindo radiação biogeográfica, gargalos demográficos insulares, níveis de endogamia, purga de alelos deletérios e varreduras seletivas após cinco décadas de pressão por inseticidas.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O complexo radiou rapidamente no Pleistoceno tardio concomitantemente ao povoamento da Oceania Próxima, sofrendo fragmentação insular pela elevação pós-glacial do nível do mar. Gargalos sucessivos geraram endogamia extraordinária no especialista costeiro An. farauti s.s. — permitindo purga eficaz de alelos deletérios sob baixo tamanho populacional efetivo — enquanto os generalistas continentais An. hinesorum e An. oreios retiveram maior diversidade. Após cinco décadas de controle químico, emergiu apenas uma varredura de resistência em Gste2, ao lado de seleção recente em repertórios gênicos quimiossensoriais espécie-específicos.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Desafia o paradigma de que elevada variação genética e conectividade sejam pré-requisitos para o sucesso ecológico de vetores de malária, oferecendo marco genômico inédito sobre Gste2 e genes quimiossensoriais em Anopheles.

43083682.titulo: Overcoming Dengue Underreporting: A Machine Learning Framework for Automated Dengue Notification Based on Electronic Medical Records.
43083682.autores: Sornsurin W, Suwannik W, … Ingsrisawang L (5 autores)
43083682.resumo: Framework de aprendizado de máquina para notificação automatizada de dengue a partir de registros eletrônicos, contra a subnotificação.
43083682.resumo_original: Hospital notification of dengue cases is frequently delayed, contributing to underreporting. At Thai provincial hospitals the bottleneck is administrative, not diagnostic: delayed discharge coding and clerical steps mean notifications are submitted late or omitted. Existing machine learning (ML) studies require clinician-annotated features absent in passive electronic medical records (EMRs). We propose a dual-pathway EMR framework for ML-based pre-population of surveillance reports. We analyzed 1031 dengue-suspected encounters (508 notifiable) from Surin Hospital, Thailand (2019-2022). Pathway A combines EMR data with manually documented clinical features; Pathway B uses only passive EMR data. Using an 80/20 stratified split, we tested 7 ML methods across 11 feature sets (77 combinations) with SHAP-guided feature elimination and 10-fold cross-validation. On the primary split, Pathway A (CatBoost) achieved an F1 score of 96.62%, 95.10% sensitivity, and 98.10% specificity (10-seed mean F1 95.7% ± 1.4%). Pathway B (LightGBM) achieved an F1 score of 84.42%, 94.12% sensitivity, 75.24% specificity, and a projected negative predictive value of 99.1% at 10% prevalence; 10-seed performance was lower (F1 78.5% ± 4.3%; sensitivity 89.1%). An exploratory LSTM-16 stacking model (F1 83.99%; precision 79.49%) performed best in precision and specificity among Pathway B. Test F1 SD across 10 seeds was ≤5.0% in 75 of 77 combinations. Within this cohort, passive EMR modeling achieved 91-94% sensitivity on the primary split (85-89% across seeds) without additional data collection, supporting the feasibility of ML-based notification in resource-constrained hospitals. Whether this reduces dengue underreporting must be established in prospective, multi-center studies.

43083857.titulo: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India.
43083857.resumo: Febre Oropouche num mundo tropical em mudança: emergência, diagnóstico e preparo de vigilância na Índia.
43083857.resumo_original: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic.

43078151.titulo: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
43078151.autores: Chiu TJ, Lu TW, … Lee JC (8 autores)
43078151.resumo: A liraglutida inibiu ZIKV em cultura (IC50 5,5 ± 0,6 µM), prolongou a vida de camundongos AG129 e reduziu a viremia cerca de 15 vezes, via AMPK/TORC2 e redução de enzimas gliconeogênicas.
43078151.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. The antiviral activity of liraglutide was attenuated by both AMPK inhibitor Compound C and siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown, supporting the claim that AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis contributes to liraglutide's anti-ZIKV activity. Given its clinical availability, liraglutide represents a promising therapeutic option for immediate repurposing for managing patients infected with ZIKV.

43082073.titulo: Cyclotides Enable the Oral Activity of Neuroactive Peptides against Lepidopteran Pests.
43082073.autores: Huang YH, Wang CK, … Craik DJ (23 autores)
43082073.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082073.resumo: Os ciclotídeos kalata B1 e B2 aumentaram de 2 a 3 vezes, de forma sinérgica, a eficácia oral de neurotoxinas de veneno contra lepidópteros; o mecanismo proposto é a ruptura seletiva da barreira do intestino médio, confirmada por microscopia.
43082073.resumo_original: Farmers face shrinking crop-protection options due to climate change, resistance, regulations, and demand for residue-free food. Peptides and proteins are attractive solutions because they are potent, specific, and degrade into harmless amino acids. Venom-derived peptide neurotoxins show strong potential as bioinsecticides, but their poor oral activity limits use in sprayable formulations. We show that plant cyclotides, kalata B1 and B2, dramatically enhance the oral efficacy of venom-derived neurotoxins against major lepidopteran pests. Their effects are synergistic, increasing activity by two to 3-fold beyond additivity, and in some cases, enabling complete mortality at doses where either component alone is ineffective. The proposed mechanism involves cyclotides selectively disrupt the lepidopteran midgut barrier, allowing neurotoxins to cross into the hemocoel and act on the nervous system. Microscopy confirms midgut damage, and the D-form of kalata B1 retains activity, indicating an achiral, lipid-mediated interaction. These results establish cyclotides as enablers of peptide-based bioinsecticides against selected important crop pests.

43082071.titulo: Trypsin-Mediated Control of Metabolic Flux Sustains Detoxification and Reproduction under Chronic Thermal Stress.
43082071.autores: Miao X, Chen B, … You S (6 autores)
43082071.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082071.resumo: Em Plutella xylostella, tripsinas do intestino médio, via CRISPR, são essenciais sob estresse térmico crônico: sustentam detoxificação e reprodução ao suprir aminoácidos.
43082071.resumo_original: Global warming and intensive insecticide use impose concurrent demands on pests, yet mechanisms coordinating resource allocation between stress responses and life-history traits remain poorly understood. We identify midgut trypsins as key regulators of this coordination in the diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we show that two trypsin genes, PxTryCFT1-like and PxTry-like, are dispensable for acute thermal tolerance but essential under chronic stress. Mutant lines exhibit severe reproductive failure under prolonged high temperatures and display broad-spectrum hypersensitivity (2- to 22-fold) to multiple insecticides. Mechanistically, trypsin loss disrupts amino acid supply, suppressing major detoxification systems including cytochrome P450s, glutathione S-transferases, and carboxylesterases. By elucidating the noncanonical role of midgut trypsins in modulating trade-offs between growth and stress defense, we demonstrate how nutrient acquisition fuels stress-response networks.

43082084.titulo: FTZ-F1 Homologue Silencing Reveals Endocrine and Xenobiotic-Response Vulnerabilities Associated with RNAi-Insect Growth Regulator Co-Treatment in Heortia vitessoides.
43082084.autores: Wang H, Liu N, … Lin T (5 autores)
43082084.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082084.resumo: Em Heortia vitessoides, o silenciamento de dois homólogos de FTZ-F1 prejudicou ecdise, pupação e emergência; um se associou a menos triglicerídeo no corpo gorduroso, o outro a ruptura do epitélio do intestino médio. dsRNA em quitosana combinado a reguladores de crescimento reduziu a sobrevivência em algumas combinações.
43082084.resumo_original: Insect growth regulators disrupt endocrine signaling, but the molecular vulnerabilities underlying their effects remain incompletely understood. Here, two FTZ-F1 homologues in Heortia vitessoides were characterized and functionally analyzed. RNAi-mediated knockdown of either homologue impaired ecdysis, pupation, and adult emergence. HvFTZ-F1-1 knockdown was more strongly associated with reduced fat-body triglyceride content and lipid-metabolism-related transcription, whereas HvFTZ-F1-2 knockdown was more strongly associated with midgut epithelial disruption, reduced ELISA-derived 20E immunoreactive levels, and broader transcriptomic perturbation. Pyriproxyfen and tebufenozide induced opposite transcriptional responses of the two homologues. Chitosan-dsRNA cotreatment produced combination-dependent survival responses, with CS-dsF1+Teb and CS-dsF2+PPF showing reduced survival relative to the corresponding pesticide-control groups. These findings identify homologue-biased developmental vulnerabilities and support a laboratory framework for RNAi-insect growth regulator cotreatment in H. vitessoides.

43082872.titulo: Virulence of Conidiobolus coronatus Against the Fall Webworm, Hyphantria cunea, and the Effect of Silencing a Host Cuticular Protein Gene on Larval Susceptibility.
43082872.autores: Bai F, Yang T, … Zhou X (7 autores)
43082872.resumo: Conidiobolus coronatus (LC50 204 conídios/mm²) contra Hyphantria cunea; o silenciamento de um gene de proteína cuticular por dsRNA oral reduziu a muda e acelerou a mortalidade após exposição ao fungo.
43082872.resumo_original: Conidiobolus coronatus is an entomopathogenic fungus with a broad insect host range. We examined the virulence of strain 20220622F, isolated from a naturally infected gall midge, against the invasive forest pest Hyphantria cunea (fall webworm). Bioassays against final-instar larvae yielded a median lethal concentration (LC50) of 204 conidia/mm2 at 96 h post-inoculation, with cumulative mortality reaching 75% at the highest inoculum density tested (351.3 conidia/mm2). Infected larvae showed transient changes in polyphenol oxidase and catalase activities, reactive oxygen species levels, and circulating hemocyte counts, together with apoptosis-related fluorescence at 24 h. Transcriptomic analysis identified differentially expressed genes associated with immune and cuticle-related functions. In third-instar larvae, feeding on dsRNA targeting the cuticular protein gene Hc.10517 reduced its expression by approximately 55% at 48 and 72 h, and this silencing was associated with developmental abnormalities and reduced moulting success. Following inoculation with 150 conidia/mm2, the dsHc.10517 group reached 100% mortality within 60 h, with a median survival time of 42 h (95% CI, 36-48 h). These laboratory results identify strain 20220622F as a candidate for the biological control of H. cunea and indicate that silencing Hc.10517 is associated with faster mortality following fungal exposure.
