43081080.titulo: A larval salivary effector from a parasitoid wasp hijacks bacteria to kill host hemocytes.
43081080.autores: Song J, Yan Z, … Ye G (11 autores)
43081080.resumo: Uma proteína flagelar de origem bacteriana, transferida horizontalmente para vespas calcidoides, é expressa na saliva larval de Nasonia vitripennis, altera a microbiota do hospedeiro e, com Enterococcus faecalis, induz morte de hemócitos por perturbação do metabolismo da dopamina.
43081080.resumo_original: Salivary proteins are well characterized in herbivorous and blood-feeding insects but remain largely unexplored in parasitoid wasps. Here, we show that FlhE, a bacterial flagellar protein gene, was horizontally transferred from Herbaspirillum to chalcidoid wasps. The single-copy Nasonia vitripennis larval salivary flagellar protein FlhE (NvLSFlhE) is highly expressed in larval salivary glands and important for wasp development. Furthermore, we found that NvLSFlhE modulated the microbiota of host fly Sarcophaga peregrina, increased microbial diversity and specifically interacted with inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) from Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis). This cooperative effect of NvLSFlhE and E. faecalis induced host hemocyte death by perturbing dopamine metabolism, with decreased cellular adenosine triphosphate levels and accumulation of cytotoxic 7-ketolithocholic acid. These findings reveal how a parasitoid larval salivary effector remodels host microbiota and shapes parasitoid-microbe-host interactions.

43080506.titulo: Host Availability and Host Contacts of Mosquitoes Using Environmental DNA.
43080506.autores: Balvers C, Visser TM, … Koenraadt CJM (7 autores)
43080506.resumo: Combina DNA do repasto, eDNA em pernas e eDNA do ar para estimar disponibilidade e contato de hospedeiros por mosquitos; Culex pipiens pipiens se alimentou mais em aves que as demais espécies.
43080506.resumo_original: Host availability is an important parameter when studying vector-borne diseases, especially in the case of opportunistic mosquito vectors. To study host feeding patterns of mosquitoes in the field, we integrated three sources of information: (1) host feeding, by identifying the origin of DNA in bloodmeals; (2) host contact, inferred from eDNA detected on mosquito legs; and (3) host availability, estimated via airborne eDNA using the frequency of host detection via airborne eDNA as a proxy for their relative abundance. At four field locations, we deployed Burkard 7-day spore traps next to BG-sentinel 2 traps to capture airborne eDNA and blood-fed mosquitoes, respectively. We found that mosquitoes caught on dairy farms fed most on the animal species that were most frequently detected by airborne eDNA. However, Culex pipiens pipiens fed significantly more on birds compared to Cx. p. molestus, Anopheles daciae, An. messeae and Culiseta annulata (p < 0.01), which fed more on mammals. Animal DNA on mosquito legs via direct contact could be detected, but results were inconsistent and prone to contamination, thereby limiting the use of mosquito legs to study host contacts. This study shows that airborne eDNA is a promising method to assess the presence, and to a certain extent also the relative abundance of vertebrate animal species as potential available hosts for mosquitoes. This method could ultimately provide better insights into the context dependency of host preference of opportunistic mosquito vectors.

43081152.titulo: Chamber explosion synthesis of TiC-TiO_2_ hybrid nanostructures.
43081152.autores: Al Mayyahi A, Sigdel S, … Amama PB (8 autores)
43081152.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Chamber explosion synthesis of TiC-TiO_2_ hybrid nanostructures.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43081152.resumo_original: Hybrid nanomaterials with tailored properties are central to advances in catalysis, energy, and environmental applications. Chamber explosion synthesis is currently either unknown or rarely used for the synthesis of hybrid nanomaterials, despite offering unique advantages, particularly its rapid in situ generation of reaction heat through an exothermic process and formation of nanostructures on a millisecond timescale. Here, we demonstrate the explosion synthesis of carbon- and titanium-containing hybrids on a millisecond timescale in a constant-volume, closed chamber. The exothermic process involves the explosion of a mixture of combustible toluene (C7H8) and noncombustible titanium tetrachloride (TiCl4) in the presence of oxygen in a closed chamber. The results reveal that the chemical, morphological, and optical properties of the hybrids vary systematically with the molar ratio of the precursors. Synthesis using TiCl4/C7H8 ratios of 0, 0.38, 0.73, and 1.0 at a constant oxygen concentration yields graphene, sheet-like graphene-TiC, core-shell TiO2-TiC particles with visible-light sensitivity, and rod-like TiO2-TiC, respectively. TiO2-TiC core-shell particles exhibit high efficiency in NO x photocatalytic oxidation under visible light. To understand the hybrid formation mechanisms, the explosion reactions were simulated using thermochemical software to predict stable phases under the reaction conditions. This study is expected to advance chamber explosion synthesis of hybrid nanomaterials and provide a framework for producing other hybrids and tuning their properties.

43083814.titulo: Dengue Vaccination in Children and Adolescents: Current Evidence, Safety, and Future Directions.
43083814.autores: Masetti M, Zambelli G, Esposito S (3 autores)
43083814.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Dengue Vaccination in Children and Adolescents: Current Evidence, Safety, and Future Directions.», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43083814.resumo_original: Background: Dengue is an expanding mosquito-borne disease and a growing global health threat. Its four serotypes, changing epidemiology, and complex immune responses make vaccine development particularly challenging. This review examines dengue vaccines, with emphasis on children and adolescents. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 10 November 2026. Clinical trials, observational studies, reviews, surveillance reports, and guidelines addressing dengue immunopathogenesis, vaccine development, efficacy, immunogenicity, safety, effectiveness, or implementation were considered. Evidence was assessed with attention to pediatric populations, age, baseline serostatus, infecting serotype, and duration of protection. Results: CYD-TDV provides moderate protection, but long-term follow-up identified an increased risk of hospitalized or severe dengue in seronegative recipients, making pre-vaccination screening central to its use. TAK-003 protects children and adolescents against virologically confirmed and hospitalized dengue, although efficacy varies by serotype and serostatus; protection against DENV-3 and DENV-4 in seronegative recipients remains uncertain. Butantan-DV showed efficacy across pediatric age groups and baseline serostatus, although the absence of DENV-3 and DENV-4 cases precluded serotype-specific estimates. Over five years, phase III rates of unsolicited vaccine-related adverse events, including serious events, were comparable with placebo. After ANVISA registered the vaccine for ages 12-59 on 8 December 2025, Brazil paused its vaccination strategy in June 2026 while investigating 42 reports following approximately 500,000 doses, including three severe cases and two deaths. Causality has not been established. TV003/TV005 and other platforms broaden the pipeline, though pediatric efficacy evidence remains limited. No validated correlate of protection is available. Affordability, equitable access, surveillance, and caregiver confidence remain important implementation challenges. Conclusions: Dengue vaccines mark important progress, but their benefits and risks depend on age, serostatus, and circulating serotypes. Long-term, serotype-specific evaluation and post-marketing surveillance are needed. Next-generation vaccines, clear communication, and sustainable access will be essential to achieve durable, equitable protection for children.

43070414.titulo: FGF23 in chronic kidney disease progression: biomarker or mediator?
43070414.autores: Chandrakar K, Shet Shirodkar SN, … Rao IR (5 autores)
43070414.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «FGF23 in chronic kidney disease progression: biomarker or mediator?», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43070414.resumo_original: Fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23) is an important regulator of phosphate balance that rises early in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Evidence suggests that elevated FGF23 is associated with adverse renal outcomes. However, whether FGF23 is merely a biomarker or a direct mediator of CKD progression remains unresolved. In this narrative review, we synthesize current knowledge on the biology of FGF23, evaluate mechanistic and clinical evidence linking FGF23 to CKD progression, and highlight key areas for future research. We included observational and experimental studies indexed in PubMed from inception to March 2026 that examined the relationships between FGF23 and renal outcomes, as well as the underlying biological pathways. Available evidence suggests that elevated FGF23 levels are associated with an accelerated decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate, increased albuminuria, and a higher risk of kidney failure across diverse populations. Longitudinal data further demonstrate that rising FGF23 trajectories are associated with adverse renal outcomes. Experimental studies suggest that FGF23 may contribute to inflammation, oxidative stress, renin-angiotensin system activation, and tubulointerstitial fibrosis. However, the close interplay between FGF23, α-Klotho, phosphate load, and calciprotein particles complicates causal inference. Therefore, the pathogenic role of FGF23 in CKD progression remains unclear, underscoring the need for further research.

43083636.titulo: Neonicotinoids and Mental Health: Mechanistic, Preclinical and Epidemiological Evidence for a Transdiagnostic Neurodevelopmental Risk.
43083636.autores: Rosas-Sánchez GU, Soria-Fregozo C, … Soriano-Hernández AD (11 autores)
43083636.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Neonicotinoids and Mental Health: Mechanistic, Preclinical and Epidemiological Evidence for a Transdiagnostic Neurodevelopmental Risk.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43083636.resumo_original: Neonicotinoid insecticides (imidacloprid, clothianidin, thiacloprid, acetamiprid, thiamethoxam, nitenpyram, dinotefuran) were developed as insect-selective nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) agonists and have long been regarded as safe for vertebrates. However, parent compounds and, more potently, desnitro metabolites such as DN-imidacloprid act on mammalian α4β2 and α7 nAChRs with nicotine-like potency, implicating cholinergic circuits central to cognition, mood, and reward. This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, preclinical, and epidemiological evidence linking neonicotinoid exposure to neuropsychiatric risk. Mechanistically, these compounds promote glial activation, oxidative stress, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, and gut microbiota alterations that converge on hippocampal and limbic dysfunction. Rodent and invertebrate studies show sex-, dose-, and exposure-window-dependent effects on anxiety-, depression-, and cognition-like behaviors, with developmental exposure mirroring prenatal nicotine effects. Human data, although limited, are convergent: poisoning case series document acute neuropsychiatric symptoms; biomonitoring studies in China, Japan, and Sri Lanka associate urinary metabolites with depression, anxiety, and a recognizable "neo-nicotinic" symptom cluster; in Mexico, studies of agricultural populations link pesticide mixtures to psychological distress, although neonicotinoid biomarkers have not yet been measured in that setting; and pediatric cohorts in China and Ecuador link prenatal and childhood exposure to impaired neurodevelopment, emotional symptoms, and hyperactivity. Collectively, this evidence is consistent with neonicotinoids being an underrecognized environmental risk factor for neuropsychiatric disorders, although the human data remain too fragmented to support causal inference and underscores the need for dedicated cohorts, expanded biomonitoring, and mechanistic research to inform regulatory assessment.

43073825.titulo: An international multicentre observational cohort study of the clinical presentation of acute arboviral infection (ARIA): a study protocol.
43073825.autores: Bourner J, Duarte G, … Bozza FA (17 autores)
43073825.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «An international multicentre observational cohort study of the clinical presentation of acute arboviral infection (ARIA): a study protocol.», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43073825.resumo_original:
Despite the growing global burden of diseases caused by arboviruses, there remain substantial gaps in our understanding of the clinical presentation and natural history of arboviral infections, especially in the acute phase. There is a critical need for robust, multicentre, and internationally harmonised data to characterise the clinical features of arboviral infections, identify early predictors of severe disease, and inform the development of diagnostic algorithms, case definitions and research study design. This study aims to address these gaps by establishing an international multicentre observational cohort focused on the clinical presentation and evolution of acute arboviral infections.
The study will be conducted across primary, secondary, and tertiary healthcare settings in multiple countries. Participating countries have the flexibility to implement the protocol at any level of their health system, depending on local context and infrastructure, and adapt the protocol according to local research interests. The protocol uses a tiered approach to sample and data collection to support implementation according to site capacity. Tier 1 is the core protocol described in this article and sites can define additional data (Tier 2) and sample (Tier 3) collection according to local resource capacity and research interest. The study will enrol patients with clinically suspected or confirmed arboviral infection who present to a participating healthcare facility within seven days of symptom onset. Participants will be enrolled for a maximum of 10 days, during which data on signs and symptoms, interventions, routine laboratory results will be collected daily. Outcome information will be collected on D10.
The systematic collection of comparable, and contextually-adaptable data on arboviral illnesses aims to generate a harmonised data set of global presentations of acute arbovirus infection and map the patient journey through their illness. The resulting dataset aims to provide evidence to support improvements in patient management, feasible research study design, and accelerate the development of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Ultimately, this collaborative effort aims to contribute towards a coordinated global response to arboviral diseases.
Not applicable.

43075328.titulo: Potential role of exercise-associated glucose metabolic reprogramming of immune cells in ameliorating chronic low-grade inflammation in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
43075328.autores: Yang Q, Pang X, … Han Y (6 autores)
43075328.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Potential role of exercise-associated glucose metabolic reprogramming of immune cells in ameliorating chronic low-grade inflammation in type 2 diabetes mellitus.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43075328.resumo_original: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is often accompanied by chronic low-grade inflammation, an important driver of the development and progression of insulin resistance. The functional phenotypes of monocytes/macrophages and T cells involved in inflammatory responses are highly dependent on their intracellular glucose metabolic patterns. Immunometabolic research indicates that, in specific cell types and under particular activation conditions, some pro-inflammatory immune cells exhibit enhanced aerobic glycolysis, whereas some immune cells with anti-inflammatory or regulatory functions rely relatively more on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. However, these metabolic-functional relationships are context-dependent and cannot serve as a universal basis for classifying all immune cells. This gives rise to an integrative hypothesis: beyond glucose-lowering and fat-loss effects, exercise may ameliorate chronic inflammation in T2DM by reshaping the functional profile of immune cells via reprogramming their glucose metabolic programmes. Whether such metabolic shifts serve as a direct mediator of the anti-inflammatory effects of exercise remains to be verified by metabolic flux measurements and mechanism-focused investigations. Centered on the cascade "exercise stimulation → altered immune-cell metabolic flux → remodelled inflammatory signalling → improved glycaemic control", this review summarises the features of disrupted glucose metabolism in immune cells and their proinflammatory mechanisms in T2DM. This review summarises the plausible molecular bases through which acute exercise and chronic training regulate immune cell metabolism via lactate signalling, the AMPK-mTOR-HIF-1α axis, epigenetic modifications and myokines. It distinguishes evidence obtained from human studies, animal experiments and in vitro cellular investigations, and discusses the effects of aerobic exercise, resistance training and high-intensity interval training, alongside limitations in head-to-head comparative evidence. Acute exercise triggers transient metabolic and signalling perturbations. Whether repeated bouts of exercise induce sustained immunometabolic adaptations through epigenetic regulation and mitochondrial remodelling constitutes the working model advanced herein; its stability and mediating role in patients with T2DM remain unconfirmed. We further perform an evidence-level appraisal of available data and identify critical gaps supporting this hypothesis, including the scarcity of direct metabolic flux measurements, limited accessibility of tissue-resident immune cell samples, and a lack of formal mediation analyses. Future work integrating stable-isotope tracing, single-cell multi-omics and mechanism-driven randomised controlled trials may help clarify whether glucose metabolic reprogramming mediates the anti-inflammatory effects of exercise. Such findings could lay a theoretical foundation for developing personalised exercise prescriptions for T2DM based on immunometabolic subtyping.

43072559.titulo: PagGAPB2 enhances salt tolerance by improving ROS scavenging in Populus alba × Populus tremula var. glandulosa.
43072559.autores: Liao S, Zhang Z, … Jiang T (5 autores)
43072559.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «PagGAPB2 enhances salt tolerance by improving ROS scavenging in Populus alba × Populus tremula var. glandulosa.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43072559.resumo_original: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) is a key enzyme in carbon metabolism and is also involved in plant responses to abiotic stress. However, the function of GAPB subfamily members under salt stress remains unclear in woody plants. In this study, 13 PagGAPDH genes were identified in 84K poplar (Populus alba × Populus tremula var. glandulosa) and classified into four subgroups: GAPA, GAPB, GAPC, and GAPCp. Structure analysis showed that PagGAPDH proteins were generally conserved, although subgroup-specific features were observed. Expression analysis revealed that PagGAPB2 was significantly induced by NaCl treatment. To investigate its function, PagGAPB2 overexpressing poplar lines were generated. Under salt stress, the overexpression lines exhibited enhanced salt tolerance compared with wild-type plants, with reduced leaf wilting, chlorosis, and plant damage. Histochemical staining and physiological measurements showed that overexpression of PagGAPB2 decreased the accumulation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), superoxide anion (O2-), and malondialdehyde (MDA), while increasing the activities of superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT). STRING-based interaction prediction and AlphaFold3-based structural modeling suggested a potential association between PagGAPB2 and phosphoglycerate kinase proteins, providing clues for further investigation of the possible relationship between carbon metabolism and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. These findings indicate that PagGAPB2 positively regulates salt tolerance in poplar by enhancing ROS scavenging capacity and may serve as a candidate gene for molecular breeding of salt tolerant forest trees.

43083713.titulo: Helicoverpa zea Boddie (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) Remains Susceptible to Vip3A Across the Southeastern USA: Eight Years of Diet-Overlay Monitoring Highlight the Need for Annual Benchmarking.
43083713.autores: Reisig D, Abdelgaffar H, … Jurat-Fuentes JL (17 autores)
43083713.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Helicoverpa zea Boddie (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae) Remains Susceptible to Vip3A Across the Southeastern USA: Eight Years of Diet-Overlay Monitoring Highlight the Need for Annual Benchmarking.», no contexto de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas.
43083713.resumo_original: Helicoverpa zea Boddie (corn earworm or bollworm) is a primary target of transgenic crops expressing insecticidal Cry and Vip3Aa proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt). Widespread resistance to Cry toxins has increased reliance on Vip3Aa. We evaluated Vip3Aa susceptibility in 71 field populations of H. zea collected across the southeastern USA from 2018 through 2025 using diet-overlay bioassays of F1 progeny. Vip3Aa1 was used in 2018 and Vip3Aa39 from 2019 through 2025. Median lethal concentrations (LC50) were estimated and resistance ratios calculated relative to two susceptible laboratory colonies, a field-collected susceptible and the commercially available Benzon colony. Resistance ratios depended strongly on the susceptible reference used. Three populations evaluated in 2018 had resistance ratios ≥ 10 relative to the field-collected susceptible colony, whereas all Benzon-referenced resistance ratios were <1.3. Benzon-referenced resistance ratios increased significantly over time, whereas field-collected-susceptible-referenced resistance ratios decreased. In contrast, field-population LC50 values showed no temporal trend from 2019 through 2025, when all populations were evaluated with Vip3Aa39. These results provide no evidence of a sustained regional decline in Vip3Aa susceptibility in this region, but they highlight the importance of stable susceptible benchmarks, protein quality control, and complementary approaches for long-term resistance monitoring.

43072584.titulo: Comparison of anti-hyperuricemic activity of berberine and metformin: Insight from de novo purine biosynthesis and purine metabolism and intestinal microbiome.
43072584.autores: Yu Q, Fu H, … Xie J (15 autores)
43072584.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Comparison of anti-hyperuricemic activity of berberine and metformin: Insight from de novo purine biosynthesis and purine metabolism and intestinal microbiome.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43072584.resumo_original: Increasing evidence has shown that the worldwide epidemic of metabolic disease including hyperuricemia (HUA) correlates with an elevation in serum uric acid (UA) as well as a marked increase in total fructose intake. Phellodendri Chinensis Cortex (PC) is a traditional medicinal material used to treat metabolic diseases including gout and HUA. Berberine (BBR), the main component of PC, possesses anti-HUA and anti-gout effects. Metformin is widely used for the treatment of metabolic syndrome. However, their effect on HUA induced by high-fructose remained unexplored. The present work endeavored to explore the anti-HUA potential of BBR and metformin on high-fructose-induced hyperuricemic rats focusing on intestinal microbiota, de novo purine biosynthesis (DNPB) of endogenous purine, purine cycle and metabolism and intestinal microbiota. Results indicated that BBR and metformin remarkably decreased the high levels of UA, creatinine, and urea induced by a long-term high-fructose diet. BBR and metformin activated the expression of ketohexokinase (KHK) and suppressed the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) to regulate fructose metabolism. Following that, BBR and metformin suppressed the activated DNPB induced by high-fructose, through which a great number of purine synthesis was inhibited. Besides, BBR promoted the purine salvage pathway (PSP) and suppressed the expression of xanthine oxidase (XOD) to inhibit the purine metabolism, resulting in the increase of inosine and decrease of IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, and accelerating the purine cycle. Metformin decreased the levels of inosine, IMP, hypoxanthine and xanthine, inhibiting purine cycle and metabolism. Additionally, BBR and metformin favorably modulated the species of gut microbiota, regulated intestinal purine absorption and excretion, decreased the intestinal purine contents and increased the fecal uricase and allantoinase concentration to recover UA catabolism. Our study revealed that BBR and metformin had outstanding anti-HUA effect, which was intimately associated with suppression of PPP, DNPB and XOD in the liver and modulation of the intestinal microbiota. BBR and metformin deserved to provide a preclinical basis for further investigation for the treatment of HUA.

43074010.titulo: Diagnostic utility of peripheral blood smear in fatal hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating severe falciparum malaria in pregnancy: a case report and review of the literature.
43074010.autores: Hagos BT, Alem GM, … Yayna AA (6 autores)
43074010.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Diagnostic utility of peripheral blood smear in fatal hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis complicating severe falciparum malaria in pregnancy: a case report and review of the literature.», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43074010.resumo_original:
Malaria, a common public health concern in endemic regions, poses significant risks during pregnancy and can rarely trigger secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH), a life-threatening hyperinflammatory condition. It is characterized by a cytokine storm and hyperactive macrophage-mediated phagocytosis of blood cells. To our knowledge, only one case of malaria-associated sHLH in pregnancy has been reported, where malaria was an incidental finding in an HIV-confounded presentation. We describe the first case of sHLH in pregnancy primarily triggered by malaria. This case was uniquely diagnosed via peripheral blood morphology, without bone marrow biopsy, and was accompanied by a leukoerythroblastic reaction on smear examination.
A 20-year-old primigravida Ethiopian woman presented in her third trimester with intermittent high-grade fever, tachycardia, tachypnea, and splenomegaly. Laboratory findings revealed bicytopenia (anemia and thrombocytopenia), leukocytosis, and Plasmodium falciparum on peripheral smear. Despite resuscitation, intravenous artesunate, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, her condition deteriorated rapidly, culminating in fatal cardiac arrest within hours. Postmortem reevaluation of the peripheral smear demonstrated definitive hemophagocytic features, including phagocytosed erythrocytes, suggesting the diagnosis of sHLH.
sHLH in pregnancy is often overlooked due to nonspecific symptoms mimicking common conditions and limited access to diagnostic criteria in resource-limited settings. In this case, delayed recognition likely contributed to mortality. While rare, identifying hemophagocytic histiocytes on peripheral smears is critical. Laboratory personnel play a vital role in flagging these morphological anomalies. Strengthening this collaboration, combined with heightened clinical suspicion, is essential to reducing diagnostic delays and facilitating life-saving intervention.

43072339.titulo: GhOAT1 mediates ornithine metabolism to promote proline under salt stress in cotton.
43072339.autores: Zhu J, Chen X, … Ye W (20 autores)
43072339.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «GhOAT1 mediates ornithine metabolism to promote proline under salt stress in cotton.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43072339.resumo_original: Salt stress is the major abiotic constraints on plant growth and development. Proline (PRO) is an important osmoregulatory substance that can enhance plant salt tolerance by maintaining cellular osmotic balance and through other mechanisms. Ornithine δ-aminotransferase (OAT) is pyridoxal 5'-phosphate-dependent aminotransferase that converts ornithine into glutamate-γ-semialdehyde, linking ornithine metabolism to PRO metabolism. However, the role of OAT in cotton salt tolerance remains unclear. In this study, OAT genes were identified at the genome-wide level in four cotton species, including Gossypium hirsutum, G. arboreum, G. raimondii and G. barbadense. Promoter cis-acting element analysis revealed that the promoter regions of most OAT family members were predominantly enriched with stress-responsive elements (salt- and drought-related) and multiple hormone-related elements. GhOAT1 was the most salt-responsive OAT family gene, as confirmed by qRT-PCR. Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of GhOAT1 aggravated wilting under salt stress, reduced OAT activity and the contents of PRO and soluble sugars, decreased peroxidase (POD) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activities, increased the accumulation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and malondialdehyde (MDA), and caused more severe disruption of leaf tissue structure than in control plants. Under salt stress, ornithine content was significantly higher in GhOAT1-silenced plants than in control plants. Collectively, GhOAT1 may improve cotton salt tolerance by regulating ornithine metabolism to promote PRO accumulation, enhancing osmotic adjustment, and maintaining cellular redox homeostasis. This study provides a theoretical basis and candidate genetic resource for elucidating OAT-mediated salt-tolerance mechanisms and for the molecular breeding of salt-tolerant cotton.

43074007.titulo: The role of lipid metabolism in immune thrombocytopenia: new perspectives from immune inflammation and thrombopoiesis.
43074007.autores: Li D, Qiu L, … Feng W (6 autores)
43074007.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «The role of lipid metabolism in immune thrombocytopenia: new perspectives from immune inflammation and thrombopoiesis.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43074007.resumo_original:
Primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune condition defined by increased immune-driven platelet destruction and inadequate platelet generation. Emerging research highlights that global alterations in lipid metabolism are closely associated with immune dysfunction and suppressed thrombopoiesis in ITP, offering a new metabolic framework for understanding disease mechanisms.
This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the pivotal role played by lipid metabolic pathways in the development and progression of ITP. Dysregulated lipid metabolism-characterized by upregulated fatty acid biosynthesis and diminished oxidative metabolism-promotes the expansion of pro-inflammatory T helper cells (Th1/Th17), activates B cells and M1 macrophages, and simultaneously undermines the suppressive activity of regulatory T cells (Tregs) and anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages. Such metabolic imbalances lead to chronic inflammation and accelerate platelet elimination. In addition, disturbances in lipid homeostasis negatively affect megakaryocyte differentiation and compromise platelet membrane stability, thereby further inhibiting platelet production. We also examine potential therapeutic interventions targeting lipid-related pathways, such as boosting the synthesis of specialized pro-resolving mediators, modulating immune cell metabolic programming, utilizing existing lipid-lowering drugs (e.g., statins) for new indications, and applying dietary modifications to influence disease outcomes.
Altered lipid metabolism may represent a central immunometabolic axis linking immune dysregulation and impaired thrombopoiesis in ITP. Combining lipid-targeted approaches with standard immunomodulatory treatments may open new avenues for treating patients with refractory ITP. Further research into lipidomic signatures and underlying molecular mechanisms is needed to advance these findings toward clinical application.

43079498.titulo: INPP5E interactome reveals novel connections to growth factor signaling.
43079498.autores: Martin-Morales R, Barbeito P, … Garcia-Gonzalo FR (16 autores)
43079498.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «INPP5E interactome reveals novel connections to growth factor signaling.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43079498.resumo_original: Primary cilia are sensory cell membrane protrusions whose malfunction causes diseases known as ciliopathies. Joubert syndrome (JBTS) is a rare recessive ciliopathy causing brain malformations and kidney cysts, among other manifestations. A key player in JBTS is INPP5E, a ciliary phosphoinositide lipid phosphatase. Although INPP5E regulates ciliary growth factor signaling, the molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, we show that a constitutively active growth factor receptor (PDGFRα-D842V) stimulates INPP5E tyrosine phosphorylation, as does the SRC tyrosine kinase. INPP5E tyrosine phosphorylation did not affect its enzyme activity but was associated with stronger binding to SH3GL1, an endocytic regulator, and SNX9, a phosphoinositide-binding protein involved, like INPP5E, in growth factor-induced ciliary ectovesicle release. Our INPP5E interactomic studies identified other growth factor signaling regulators, including among others: SIN1 (the phosphoinositide-binding subunit of the mTORC2 complex), STRAP (a TGFβ and PI3K/AKT signaling regulator), GRB2 (a growth factor receptor adaptor) and the JBTS-associated proteins AHI1 and NPHP1. Moreover, INPP5E strongly interacted with the phosphopeptide-binding 14-3-3 proteins, and did so only in presence of serine-85, a phosphorylated INPP5E residue. Lastly, we found that INPP5E differentially regulates two cilium-dependent growth factor signaling pathways in fibroblasts. Thus, while INPP5E downregulated PDGFRα levels and PDGF-induced AKT and ERK phosphorylations, it upregulated TGFBR1 levels and TGFβ-induced SMAD2 and ERK phosphorylations. Altogether, our work provides important clues on the cilia-dependent actions of growth factors, with implications for ciliopathies like JBTS.

43072066.titulo: TALDO1 inhibition suppresses glioblastoma via ROS-JNK-dependent apoptosis and promotes pro-inflammatory remodeling of glioma-associated myeloid cells.
43072066.autores: Qiu Z, Guo C, … Yin L (10 autores)
43072066.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «TALDO1 inhibition suppresses glioblastoma via ROS-JNK-dependent apoptosis and promotes pro-inflammatory remodeling of glioma-associated myeloid cells.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43072066.resumo_original: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains difficult to control because of its aggressive growth, metabolic plasticity, and complex immune microenvironment. Transaldolase 1 (TALDO1) is a key enzyme in the pentose phosphate pathway, but its role in GBM remains unclear. We integrated multistage Mendelian randomization, pan-cancer analysis, and experimental validation to prioritize TALDO1 as a candidate therapeutic target. We then investigated its function using genetic and pharmacological perturbation, RNA sequencing, rescue assays, conditioned medium experiments, and an orthotopic GL261 model. TALDO1 promoted GBM cell migration, proliferation, and tumor growth. TALDO1 depletion induced G1/S arrest, accompanied by p53 and p21 upregulation and cyclin D1 suppression. It also reduced the NADPH/NADP+ ratio, increased reactive oxygen species (ROS), activated JNK, and induced apoptosis. Pharmacological inhibition of TALDO1 with AO-022 reproduced these effects. Conditioned medium from TALDO1-depleted or AO-022-treated glioma cells induced pro-inflammatory changes in myeloid cells. NAC attenuated these changes, whereas direct AO-022 treatment had no comparable effect, indicating that myeloid remodeling was mediated primarily by glioma cell derived signals. In the orthotopic GL261 model, AO-022 suppressed tumor progression, prolonged survival, increased tumor cell apoptosis, and promoted pro-inflammatory remodeling of glioma-associated myeloid cells (GAMs). Together, these findings identify TALDO1 as a potential therapeutic target that connects cell cycle progression and redox homeostasis with myeloid remodeling in GBM.

43078774.titulo: Lactobacillus Fermentation-Derived γ-Aminobutyric Acid Improves Sleep Parameters in Invertebrate and Vertebrate Models.
43078774.autores: Ha YJ, Kim MJ, … Hong KB (7 autores)
43078774.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Lactobacillus Fermentation-Derived γ-Aminobutyric Acid Improves Sleep Parameters in Invertebrate and Vertebrate Models.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43078774.resumo_original: This study aimed to evaluate the sleep-promoting effects of Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) produced by Lactobacillus fermentation using invertebrate and vertebral models. The activity of GABA derived from lactic acid bacteria (GABArelax®) was analyzed through subjective day-night movement and sleep-related parameters in fruit flies (Drosophila melanogaster) and sleep duration, neurotransmitter-related factors, and brain waves in ICR mice and SD-rats. In Drosophila, GABArelax® increased total sleep time and reduced nighttime and daytime locomotor activity, with the 3% treatment producing effects comparable to those of benzodiazepine. Video-tracking analysis further demonstrated that 2% and 3% GABArelax® reduced the total distance traveled, locomotor velocity, and overall mobility, while exerting relatively limited effects on the total duration of active and inactive behavior. In ICR mice, GABArelax® increased the mRNA expression of GABAergic and serotonergic receptors, including GABAA-R, GABAB-R1, GABAB-R2, and Htr1a. These transcriptional changes were accompanied by elevated brain concentrations of GABA and 5-hydroxytryptamine and enhanced expression of antioxidant defense-related genes, including SOD, Gpx1, and CAT. Electroencephalographic analysis in SD-rats showed that GABArelax® reduced wakefulness and prolonged total sleep duration. This increase was predominantly attributable to an extension of non-rapid eye movement sleep, whereas high-dose administration reduced REM sleep and enhanced δ-wave activity, an electrophysiological marker of deep sleep. Overall, these findings demonstrate that GABArelax® promotes sleep through coordinated regulation of GABAergic and serotonergic neurotransmission, reinforcement of antioxidant defense, and improvement of sleep architecture. GABArelax® therefore represents a promising food-derived functional ingredient for the management of sleep disturbances and the improvement of sleep quality.

43075447.titulo: Pathological mechanisms of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline.
43075447.autores: Yan M, Wang Z, … Luo J (6 autores)
43075447.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Pathological mechanisms of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43075447.resumo_original: Chronic low-grade systemic inflammation serves as a pivotal pathological link coupling unhealthy lifestyles with malignant remodeling of body composition. This review systematically constructs and elucidates the molecular mechanisms and pathological progression of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline. Upstream multidimensional lifestyle stressors-including unhealthy diets, sleep deprivation, psychological stress, and sedentary behavior-disrupt the gut barrier, endocrine barriers, and mechanical contractile strain, thereby initiating immunometabolic reprogramming and triggering systemic chronic low-grade sterile inflammation. Acting as a core pathological driver, this low-grade inflammation impairs lipid and protein homeostasis, propels lipotoxic spillover and intramyocellular fat infiltration, and ultimately leads to the progressive decline of skeletal muscle mass and function. Concurrently, age-related neuroendocrine axis decline and dwindling sex hormone levels function as endogenous amplifiers, synergistically accelerating tissue microenvironmental remodeling and body composition imbalance in a distinctly dimorphic manner (e.g., postmenopausal estrogen deficiency accelerates muscle deterioration by inducing autophagy dysfunction in muscle stem cells). A deep mechanistic parsing of the regulatory nodes within this multidimensional network provides substantial academic value for deciphering the onset and progression of lifestyle-driven chronic inflammatory disorders.

43073701.titulo: Genomic characterization of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from the National Clinical Bacteriology Reference Laboratory, Ethiopia.
43073701.autores: Negeri AA, Getu M, … Tollera G (23 autores)
43073701.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Genomic characterization of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates from the National Clinical Bacteriology Reference Laboratory, Ethiopia.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43073701.resumo_original:
Acinetobacter baumannii is a major cause of healthcare-associated infections, and carbapenem-resistant strains pose a critical public health threat owing to limited treatment options and the dissemination of AMR determinants. However, genomic data on carbapenem-resistant A baumannii(CRAB) in Ethiopia are limited. This study characterized 30 A. baumannii isolates from the National Clinical Bacteriology Reference Laboratory (NRL) using phenotypic and whole-genome sequencing (WGS).
All 30 A. baumannii isolates exhibited multidrug-resistant (MDR) phenotypes, and 29/30 (96.7%) were phenotypically resistant to carbapenems. WGS identified acquired carbapenemase genes in 28/29 (96.6%) carbapenem-resistant isolates, predominantly blaNDM-1(20/29) and blaOXA-23 (17/29), together with diverse AMR determinants. Population structure analysis using the Pasteur multilocus sequence typing (MLST) scheme identified ST2 (International Clone 2) as the predominant lineage (14/30, 46.7%), followed by ST85 (5/30, 16.7%) and ST1 (3/30, 10.0%). The Oxford MLST scheme further resolved the isolates into ST1697 (9/30, 30.0%), ST1089 (5/30, 16.7%), ST451 (5/30, 16.7%), and ST405 (3/30, 10.0%), while three isolates had unassigned MLST profiles that were not matched to existing sequence types in the MLST database. The core-genome SNP phylogeny showed that isolates generally clustered according to their MLST sequence types, while also revealing genetic diversity within individual sequence types. Closely related clusters were consistent with clonal relatedness, whereas genetically distinct isolates within the same sequence type suggested diversification among isolates. Capsular typing identified nine KL types, with KL152 predominating (14/30, 46.7%), and three major Outer Core Locus (OCL) types, OCL1 (15/30, 50.0%), OCL16 (6/30, 20.0%), and OCL15 (5/30, 16.7%). All isolates carried conserved virulence determinants associated with biofilm formation, quorum sensing, iron acquisition, secretion systems, and type IV pili, and harbored Rep_3 superfamily plasmids representing 14 distinct plasmid types.
Genomic characterization of MDR clinical isolates A. baumannii revealed the predominance of international high-risk lineages carrying clinically relevant carbapenemase genes, diverse virulence determinants and plasmid replicons. WGS provides high-resolution insights into population structure and genetic diversity, highlighting its value for strengthening antimicrobial resistance surveillance and informing infection prevention and control strategies.

43075477.titulo: Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Dengue Fever in the Chaoshan Region, China: Two Epidemic Years (2019 vs 2025).
43075477.autores: Liu DK, Wu YF, … Liu YH (5 autores)
43075477.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Epidemiological and Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Dengue Fever in the Chaoshan Region, China: Two Epidemic Years (2019 vs 2025).», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43075477.resumo_original:
Compare the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of patients in the Chaoshan region of Guangdong who had dengue fever during two epidemic years, 2019 and 2025.
This retrospective study analyzed patients who were diagnosed with dengue fever in 2019 (n=200) and 2025 (n=161) at the First Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College. The epidemiological characteristics, geographic distributions, clinical presentations, laboratory findings, and clinical outcomes of the two cohorts were compared.
Comparison of the two epidemic years indicated the 2025 cohort was older (52.14±20.36 vs 42.37±18.42 years, P<0.01) and had higher prevalences of morbidities and multimorbidities (24.2% vs 6.0%, P<0.01). DENV-1 was the predominant serotype in both cohorts and accounted for 142 of the 200 patients tested in 2019 (71.0%) and 118 of the 141 patients tested in 2025 (83.7%). The maximum number of cases was in August during 2019 and in October during 2025. Geographical analysis indicated a concentration of cases in the urban districts of Shantou during 2019 and in the Chao'an district of Chaozhou during 2025. After propensity score matching, the 2025 cohort had a lower rate of fever; higher rates of weakness, nausea, and vomiting; a higher white blood cell nadir; and a higher rate of liver dysfunction (elevated LDH, AST, ALT, and TBIL, all P<0.05). ICU admission was also more frequent in the 2025 cohort after matching (16/142 vs 0/142; exact McNemar P<0.001; risk difference 11.3%, 95% CI 6.1-16.5), although the matched odds ratio was not estimable because no patient in the 2019 cohort was admitted to the ICU; comparisons of severe dengue and in-hospital mortality were inconclusive because of the small number of events. The 2025 cohort had greater hospital costs (P<0.001).
The 2025 cohort was older and had a higher prevalence of morbidities, a distinct clinical and laboratory profile, and a different geographic distribution. These findings may help improve the preparedness and management of future dengue epidemics.

43082195.titulo: Effects of heat stress on honey bee physiology and gut microbiome under laboratory conditions.
43082195.autores: Baugus L, Walt HK, … Chakrabarti P (5 autores)
43082195.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Effects of heat stress on honey bee physiology and gut microbiome under laboratory conditions.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43082195.resumo_original: Heat stress affects individual honey bees, and this may compromise overall colony performance and health. As the frequency, intensity, and duration of heat waves increase due to climate change, it is crucial to understand the impacts of heat on honey bees. This study investigates how heat stress impacts honey bee physiology and gut microbiome. Honey bees were subjected to three temperature conditions (control, heat stress and heat shock) for two weeks. Half of all experimental cages received multifloral pollen supplementation. The acute heat shock group, both with and without pollen, exhibited the highest mortality, followed by control groups (with and without pollen) and chronic heat stress groups (with and without pollen). The honey bee microbiome adapted to the effects of heat stress, with temperature stress exerting selective, taxon-specific effects on gut microbiome rather than broad community disruption. Specifically, changes occurred in Bombella intestini, Bifidobacterium asteroides, Lactobacillus apis, and Gilliamella apicola. Additionally, there was an absence of a strong effect of heat stress on the honey bee proteome, suggesting that the honey bee proteome adequately adapts to heat stress in the measured temperature range. This study highlights the value of focusing on individual taxon and specific protein functions when evaluating environmental stressor impacts.

43079531.titulo: Streamlined durability monitoring of DuraNet® Plus and Interceptor® G2 insecticide-treated nets in Northern Region, Cameroon: assessment results in two sites from 2022 to 2025.
43079531.autores: Esch K, Fotso-Toguem YG, … Poyer S (15 autores)
43079531.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Streamlined durability monitoring of DuraNet® Plus and Interceptor® G2 insecticide-treated nets in Northern Region, Cameroon: assessment results in two sites from 2022 to 2025.», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43079531.resumo_original:
Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) are a critical vector control and malaria prevention tool. Routine monitoring of ITN physical and chemical durability is key to assessing their performance under real-world conditions. A streamlined ITN durability (SDM) monitoring methodology was deployed in Northern Region, Cameroon from 2022 to 2025. SDM can be  less expensive than standard durability monitoring and focus primarily on insecticidal efficacy. The primary assessment objective was to measure the insecticidal efficacy of pyrethroid (pyr) + piperonyl butoxide (PBO) DuraNet Plus (DNP) and pry + chlorfenapyr (CFP) Interceptor G2 (IG2) ITNs through mosquito mortality and chemical retention testing. Secondary objectives were to monitor ITN physical integrity and estimate ITN attrition. This work seeks to generate data that informs future ITN procurement and deploy decisions in Cameroon.
This was a prospective assessment using repeat cross-sectional cluster surveys of ITNs randomly sampled from a primary sampling frame after annual assessment timepoints. Two study districts, Lagdo and Pitoa, were selected for their proximity and similarities in climate, demographics and malaria burden. Questionnaires captured information on ITN use in households from which ITNs were sampled. Sampled ITNs underwent physical hole inspection, as well as bioassay and chemical residue analyses. Insecticidal efficacy, assessed as pyr-resistant mosquito mortality (24-h mortality for DNP ITNs and 72-h mortality for IG2 ITNs) and mean chemical content were evaluated, as were ITN attrition and potential associations between ITN use factors and chemical content retention.
Mean PBO content of DNP ITNs and mean CFP content of IG2 ITNs fell outside the manufacturers' target doses across the 12-, 24- and 36-month survey rounds. Pry-resistant strain 24-h mortality 36 months post-distribution of DNP ITNs was just 5%, corresponding with an 82% decrease in PBO content compared to the manufacturer's target dose. IG2 pyr-resistant strain 72-h mortality after 36 months was 55%, corresponding with a 79% decrease in CFP content compared to the manufacturer's target dose. Ever washing an ITN (p = 0.017) and the use of a detergent or bleach (p = 0.007) were significantly associated with reductions in mean chemical content in IG2 ITNs. All cause attrition was estimated at 51% for DNP ITNs and 32% for IG2 ITNs after 36 months.
These are the first published SDM results. IG2 ITNs in Lagdo outperformed DNP ITNs in Pitoa on measures of pyr-resistant strain mortality and chemical retention. Durability monitoring data from other sites is necessary to identify trends in DNP performance under real-world conditions. However, our findings support the procurement and deployment of IG2 ITNs over DNP ITNs in Northern Region, Cameroon.

43078954.titulo: Microbiota of Polistine Wasps: A Comparison of Four Species From India.
43078954.autores: Rana A, Nain D, … Sen R (6 autores)
43078954.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Microbiota of Polistine Wasps: A Comparison of Four Species From India.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43078954.resumo_original: Studying the microbiota of closely related species can provide important insights into the essential roles of symbiotic microbes in the physiology of organisms. We have studied the bacterial microbiota of four polistine species (Vespidae: Polistinae), from India, using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore platform. Many polistine species have been studied from behavioural, genetic, physiological and ecological perspectives. However, few of them were used for studying their microbiota. A recent study on the microbiota of Polistes wattii revealed that its microbiota is similar to Vespa (Vespidae: Vespinae). However, the microbiota of a single species from a single geographic location did not provide a holistic assessment of the genus's microbiota. Therefore, here we studied and compared the microbial community of four polistine species. We used P. wattii and P. indicus from northern India and P. wattii, P. olivaceous, and Ropalidia spatulata from eastern India to compare the microbiota of different polistine species. We show that the microbiota of P. wattii from different geographic locations were more similar to each other than the other three species. Contrary to our expectation, sympatric species showed more distinct bacterial community profiles while P. wattii samples from two different locations were more similar to each other. We further conducted a multivariate analysis to assess the gut microbiota of different hymenopteran species. We show that the gut microbial communities of polistine wasps are more similar to those of Asian Vespine wasps (both carnivorous) than to those of omnivorous ants and herbivorous bees, indicating that diet is an important determinant of their bacterial microbiota.

43082836.titulo: Recent Research on Trichoderma in Biological Control and Plant Growth Promotion: A Descriptive Review of Taxonomic Reporting, Species-Target Networks, and Field-Validation Gaps.
43082836.autores: Handte VG, Ramos RF, … Jacques RJS (10 autores)
43082836.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Recent Research on Trichoderma in Biological Control and Plant Growth Promotion: A Descriptive Review of Taxonomic Reporting, Species-Target Networks, and Field-Validation Gaps.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43082836.resumo_original: Trichoderma is among the most extensively studied fungal genera for biological control and plant growth promotion. We conducted a descriptive quantitative review of English-language original articles published from January 2021 to July 2025 to describe application categories, taxonomic representation, species-target networks, geographical patterns, and experimental settings. Searches in Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect retrieved 4643 records, of which 335 met the eligibility criteria. Biofungicide studies predominated among the included articles (219/335; 65.4%), while T. harzianum (110/335; 32.8%) and T. asperellum (65/335; 19.4%) were the most frequently reported taxa. Fifty-six articles (16.7%) reported the agent only as Trichoderma spp., limiting species-level comparisons across studies. A field component was reported in 98 studies (29.3%), whereas 237 (70.7%) were restricted to laboratory and/or greenhouse conditions. A limited subset also examined non-crop targets, including mosquito vectors. The findings support improved taxonomic reporting and further field validation, while formulation stability and input compatibility, not systematically assessed here, are proposed as additional research priorities. In the Brazilian case study, products containing Trichoderma accounted for 15.1% of the biological-product registrations in the analyzed AGROFIT dataset. This descriptive synthesis provides a basis for prioritizing research toward the integration of Trichoderma-based products into sustainable crop-management programs.

43072563.titulo: Timing of exposure affects transmission of a gut parasite in bumblebee colonies.
43072563.autores: Wolmuth-Gordon H, Fenton A, Brown MJ (3 autores)
43072563.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Timing of exposure affects transmission of a gut parasite in bumblebee colonies.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43072563.resumo_original: Parasite transmission speed affects parasite impact on a population and is influenced by population size, sex and age structure. The eusocial bumblebee, Bombus terrestris, and its gut parasite, Crithidia bombi, provide a model system to test the effects of population demographics on parasite transmission. We investigated whether the timing of colony parasite exposure influences its transmission. Colonies were inoculated at the start, middle or end of their lifecycle. The basic reproduction number (Ro) was estimated as 8.48 (±6.38) and did not differ between colonies of different lifecycle stages. For the remainder of their lifecycle, colonies were screened biweekly to determine infection prevalence. We constructed an epidemiological model to further understand the relationship between colony demography and C. bombi transmission. Colonies exposed to the parasite earlier experienced a higher, and more prolonged period of transmission. Surprisingly, by the end of their lifecycle parasitaemia had died out in 88% of colonies. Modelling suggests that transmission is frequency-dependent and therefore, observed patterns are not due to colony size differences. The model indicates per capita net transmission rates declined over time, irrespective of inoculation timing. These results provide insight into disease dynamics in social insects and more broadly, epidemics in populations of social species.

43081711.titulo: Individual differences: when probabilities shape brain development.
43081711.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Individual differences: when probabilities shape brain development.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43081711.resumo_original: Brains are stereotyped, yet no two brains are strictly identical. Structural differences between hemispheres and among individuals sharing the same genetic and environmental background can contribute to behavioral individuality. In addition to genetic and environmental influences, the stochastic nature of brain development represents a third source of individual variation.Here, we report a developmental sequence of events that generates individual neural circuits in the Drosophila visual system. Variation in the wiring of the dorsal cluster neurons (DCNs), a population of visual interneurons, contributes to non-heritable individual object-orientation behaviors. This variation relies on a differential innervation of proximal versus distal neuropils by DCN axons. Using 4D live imaging of developing brains, we found that alternative axon-targeting outcomes result from two sequential and independent genetically encoded stochastic processes, through which DCNs gradually lose their capacity to target distally. First, a postmitotic Notch-mediated lateral inhibition event restricts a pool of NotchON axons to proximal neuropils, whereas remaining NotchOFF axons adopt a bi-potential transitory state. Subsequently, a subset of NotchOFF axons accumulates stable microtubules in a probabilistic manner, enabling distal target innervation, while axons that fail to stabilize innervate proximally.Together, these sequential targeting decisions generate stochastic variation in the number of distal-projecting axons across individuals. Our findings provide a conceptual and mechanistic framework for understanding how neural circuits can preserve an overall robust structure while displaying individual-specific wiring patterns.

43070992.titulo: From chimpanzee faeces to emerging seedlings: How dung beetle communities drive secondary seed dispersal in Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire.
43070992.autores: Koffi KKS, Dosso K, … Wittig RM (8 autores)
43070992.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «From chimpanzee faeces to emerging seedlings: How dung beetle communities drive secondary seed dispersal in Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43070992.resumo_original: Seed dispersal is a major force shaping plant recruitment and forest regeneration in tropical ecosystems. We looked at how dung beetles (Scarabaeidae) contribute to secondary seed dispersal from chimpanzee faeces in three territories (Northern, Southern, and Eastern) of Taï National Park, Côte d'Ivoire. Four fruiting tree species commonly eaten by chimpanzees were selected-Dacryodes klaineana, Diospyros mannii, Pycnanthus angolensis, and Uapaca guineensis-because their seeds regularly occurred in chimpanzee faeces and survived gut passage. Each experimental faecal sample contained all four seed species simultaneously, with seven seeds per species (28 seeds in total), allowing us to assess species-specific patterns of secondary seed dispersal under the same faecal deposition conditions. To mimic natural conditions, we exposed chimpanzee faeces containing seeds for 48 h and then tracked seed fate. Germination and seedling establishment were tested in controlled conditions at five burial depths (0-15 cm). Over the course of the study we recorded 7,946 dung beetles from 49 species, with communities strongly dominated by paracoprid (burrowing) species. Just over half of the seeds (51.94%) were moved by beetles; among the dispersed seeds, 87.73% (2,679 seeds) remained on the soil surface, whereas only 12.28% (375 seeds) were buried. Seed species mainly affected vertical dispersal (burial), with weaker effects on horizontal dispersal, but not on total dispersal. Burial depth was a key ecological filter. Germination was highest at intermediate depths (2-5 cm), while seeds left on the surface or buried deeper showed much lower recruitment. Where seeds came from also mattered: for some species, seeds that passed through chimpanzees survived better, probably because faecal material improves local nutrient conditions and aids seedling establishment. In short, dung beetles shape seed fate mostly by changing seeds' vertical position in the soil rather than by increasing the total number moved. By influencing burial depth, these beetles play an important role in early plant recruitment and thus in forest regeneration.

43073738.titulo: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of phosphate-solubilizing strain YNK-FB0058, which potentially represents a novel species within the genus Phyllobacterium.
43073738.autores: Wang Y, Jia J, … Yang P (15 autores)
43073738.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Genomic and phenotypic characterization of phosphate-solubilizing strain YNK-FB0058, which potentially represents a novel species within the genus Phyllobacterium.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43073738.resumo_original:
Phosphate-solubilizing bacteria are soil-dwelling probiotics that promote plant growth and convert unavailable phosphorus into absorbable forms for plants. A phosphate-solubilizing strain, YNK-FB0058, which potentially represents a novel species within the genus Phyllobacterium, was isolated from the rhizosphere of safflower in a tobacco-safflower rotation field. Whole-genome sequencing and in vitro verification tests were conducted to explore its genetic basis and functional traits.
Phylogenetic analysis based on the 16 S rRNA gene, together with comprehensive ANIm and dDDH comparisons against the available Phyllobacterium type-strain genomes and genome-scale taxonomic analysis using TYGS, suggested that strain YNK-FB0058 may represent a novel species within the genus Phyllobacterium. Its draft genome assembly size is 4,694,147 bp with a GC content of 61.14%, and a total of 4,459 CDSs were annotated. The genome harbors gene clusters involved in inorganic phosphorus solubilization, organic phosphorus mineralization, phosphorus transport and regulation. It also carries growth-promoting genes related to indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) synthesis, nitrogen-related functions, a putative nonribosomal peptide metallophore/nonribosomal peptide synthetase biosynthetic gene cluster, iron acquisition and homeostasis, and zinc solubilization. The strain exhibited high efficiency in solubilizing organic and inorganic phosphorus, with solubilization capacities of 566.3 mg/L- 1 and 474.46 mg/L- 1, respectively, and showed a maximum IAA-equivalent concentration of 19.319 µg/mL. It also grew under the tested nitrogen-free-medium conditions, exhibited zinc-solubilizing activity, and showed CAS-detectable siderophore production. Inoculation with this strain significantly increased plant height, stem diameter, leaf area and biomass of flue-cured tobacco, elevated nitrogen and phosphorus contents and enzyme activities in rhizosphere soil, and promoted phosphorus accumulation in tobacco plants.
Strain YNK-FB0058 may represent a novel species within the genus Phyllobacterium and exhibits efficient phosphate-solubilizing activity and multiple plant growth-promoting traits. This strain provides a high-quality microbial resource and theoretical basis for reducing chemical phosphorus fertilizer application and developing high-efficiency microbial inoculants in green agriculture.

43082688.titulo: Connectomes as Structural Priors for Embodied Control: Lessons from Digital Drosophila.
43082688.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Connectomes as Structural Priors for Embodied Control: Lessons from Digital Drosophila.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43082688.resumo_original: Synapse-resolved connectomes of Drosophila melanogaster now map the entire adult brain and ventral nerve cord, but behavior also depends on synaptic strengths, neural dynamics, and the body. A connectome is therefore better used as a testable structural prior than as a blueprint to copy. This review examines how digital Drosophila (connectomes plus the models and body simulators built on them) can serve this role in embodied control. We trace how electron-microscopy images become a connectivity graph, where errors enter, and how heterogeneous datasets can be combined reproducibly. We then compare three uses of the graph (extracting a circuit principle, embedding a reconstructed module, or adopting the whole connectome as controller topology) with one another and with conventional controllers, separating experimentally validated findings from computational predictions. Connectome-constrained models can predict neural activity and sensorimotor pathways, but simulated success does not by itself establish biological accuracy, and sensory encoding, motor decoding, and body mechanics are as much part of the controller as the wiring. From this synthesis we derive five candidate design principles (sparse modular communication, recurrent state estimation, hierarchical motor control, selective plasticity, and body-controller co-design) and one methodological principle (anatomically indexed intervention), each paired with falsifiable predictions, matched baselines, and sim-to-real stress tests.

43078196.titulo: Orientation-invariant morphometry of dendritic spines: A landmark-based method applied to layer II pyramidal neurons of the petavoxel human connectome.
43078196.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Orientation-invariant morphometry of dendritic spines: A landmark-based method applied to layer II pyramidal neurons of the petavoxel human connectome.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43078196.resumo_original: The classification of cortical dendritic spines into stubby, thin and mushroom subtypes has been shown to be unstable under rotation, so the structure of spine morphology cannot be read from measurements that depend on the viewing angle. We developed the Spine Morphometry Hub (SMH), a 12-point anatomical landmark framework that characterizes each spine in all three orthogonal planes, independently of the viewing angle, and extracts geometric, voxel-based, and mesh-based metrics. We applied it to 228 spines from five layer II pyramidal neurons in the H01 nanometer-resolution reconstruction of human temporal cortex. No morphometric distribution departed from unimodality, and all were right-skewed. Density-based clustering assigned most spines to noise, and a Monte Carlo test showed that this pattern is incompatible with a null model of two compact discrete types. Spines at the extremes of the distribution were clearly distinct in form, yet no boundary between classes emerged. Two explicit classification rules applied to the same three-dimensional measurements assigned the same name to only 33.3% of the spines, and because no viewing angle is involved, this disagreement arises from the classification rules themselves. Apical and basal spines did not differ in the six core morphometric variables. Although a continuum of spine forms has been reported in rodent and human cortex, this framework is original in applying an orientation-invariant, landmark-based measurement method to dendritic spines reconstructed at nanometer resolution in the H01 petavoxel dataset. We propose that it can serve as a common reference for studies of spine remodeling in neurological disorders.

43073997.titulo: Quality assessment of malaria microscopy in Ouagadougou laboratories, Burkina Faso: accuracy of thick and thin blood smears.
43073997.autores: Sawadogo PM, Kaboré JAT, … Zida A (7 autores)
43073997.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Quality assessment of malaria microscopy in Ouagadougou laboratories, Burkina Faso: accuracy of thick and thin blood smears.», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43073997.resumo_original:
Malaria microscopy remains the reference method for parasite detection in many low-resource settings, but its accuracy depends on slide preparation, staining quality, and reader performance.
This study aimed to assess the accuracy of routine malaria microscopy in selected laboratories in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
We conducted a cross-sectional study in four laboratories in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, and re-examined 1000 malaria blood smears initially read by 29 laboratory providers using independent expert microscopy. The slides examined were the same as those used for routine diagnosis to ensure no bias remains in the interpretation of the results.-Routine microscopy was performed using single reading, while expert microscopy was performed using double reading to comply with the WHO standard.
Twenty-nine microscopy providers participated, of whom 79.3% (23/29) were biomedical technicians, 17.2% (5/29) trainees, and 3.4% (1/29) biologists. Routine microscopy classified 184/1000 slides (18.4%) as positive and 816/1000 (81.6%) as negative, whereas expert re-reading identified 115/1000 (11.5%) as positive and 885/1000 (88.5%) as negative. Overall concordance was 88.1% (95% CI 85.9-90.0%), with a sensitivity of 78.3% (95% CI 69.9-84.8%), specificity of 89.4% (95% CI 87.2-91.2%), positive predictive value of 48.9% (95% CI 41.8-56.1%), and negative predictive value of 96.9% (95% CI 95.5-97.9%). Inter-reader agreement between routine and expert classification was moderate (Cohen's kappa = 0.54). Inaccurate routine readings were significantly associated with lack of refresher training and shorter slide-reading time.
Routine malaria microscopy performance in the participating laboratories was limited by false-positive readings, highlighting the need for strengthened quality assurance and continuous competency-based training.

43080126.titulo: From Emerging Vectors to Missed Fevers: Why Fragile Health Systems Need Integrated Fever-Vector Preparedness.
43080126.autores: Abdi DA, Abdi Yusuf A, … Ahmed Mohamed A (5 autores)
43080126.revista: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
43080126.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «From Emerging Vectors to Missed Fevers: Why Fragile Health Systems Need Integrated Fever-Vector Preparedness.», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43080126.resumo_original: Climate change, urbanization, population mobility, and expanding mosquito vectors are reshaping infectious-disease risks in fragile health systems, where surveillance, diagnosis, and response often remain fragmented. This Policy Analysis argues that preparedness should move beyond isolated pathogen- or vector-specific programs toward an integrated fever-vector model. Undifferentiated fever should serve as the clinical entry point linking environmental intelligence, entomological surveillance, sentinel fever surveillance, tiered laboratory testing, and public health response. Such integration could improve recognition of arboviral infections overlooked in malaria-centered systems, support earlier outbreak detection, and guide targeted vector control and diagnostic preparedness. Somalia and the wider Horn of Africa illustrate the urgency of this shift because climate shocks, displacement, weak laboratory systems, and emerging urban vector-borne risks increasingly converge. The priority is not a more technologically complex system, but a connected and sustainable preparedness architecture capable of linking emerging vectors with febrile illnesses presenting in routine care.

43070712.titulo: Evolutionary relatedness is a partially reliable predictor of host-associated microbiome composition.
43070712.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Evolutionary relatedness is a partially reliable predictor of host-associated microbiome composition.», no contexto de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas.
43070712.resumo_original: Multicellular animals emerged into a microbial world, and they continue to be influenced by sympatric bacterial species. Host-associated microbiomes are recognized as critical contributors to their living domicile's success. Detailing how microbiomes are assembled and maintained by their hosts has important implications for animal health, agricultural productivity, and biodiversity interventions across the tree of life. Tens to 100s of bacterial genera are frequently detected in animal microbiomes, with some being uniquely and consistently detected in specific host species. Such discoveries have informed theories like phylosymbiosis that assert that host-associated microbiomes often reflect host species relatedness. We explored the predictive limits of this theory by performing a multi-scale dissimilarity-based comparative analyses using publicly available microbiomes drawn from 113 insect species spanning 14 insect orders. We detected a moderate inter-order phylosymbiotic signal (Mantel test: r = 0.392, P < 0.001) that was weakened (r = 0.173, P < 0.001) when the Blattodea were excluded from the analysis. Intra-order level phylosymbiotic signals varied widely for lepidopteran, hymenopteran, hemipteran, and blattodean host species microbiomes. Strong signals were often explained by obligate endosymbionts and/or nestmate-acquired gut bacteria, rather than by the total microbiomes. In short, host species-defining bacterial genera often represented a small fraction of the total observed microbial diversity in their respective insect host species, and these genera were well-integrated into host behaviors and/or physiologies that facilitated reliable intra- and inter-generational transmission. In contrast, microbiome compositional variability was so high in some insect orders that attempts to reflect host speciation events using their microbiomes were impossible.IMPORTANCEWhile all animals have microbiomes, the principles determining their composition remain an incomplete story. We leveraged the diversity of Insecta, arisen from 400 My of evolution, to evaluate if microbiome evolution is synchronized with the evolutionary history of their associated hosts. We found that host evolution plays a limited role in predicting microbiome composition, particularly due to the non-uniformity of host-microbial symbioses across insects. This result is in stark contrast to studies of similar scope in vertebrate organisms that spanned much less evolutionary time (i.e., up to 50 My). While insects of the order Blattodea, in particular, harbor exceptionally diverse microbiomes, many insect microbiomes are characterized by few bacterial genera. Our results suggest that host evolutionary history is but one of many factors, including differences in microbiome transmission modality, influencing insect microbiome evolution.
