43075215.titulo: Circadian rhythm regulates immune cell function and participates in the development and progression of metabolic diseases.
43075215.autores: Yang Y, Zheng S, … Zhu J (8 autores)
43075215.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Circadian rhythm regulates immune cell function and participates in the development and progression of metabolic diseases.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43075215.resumo_original: The circadian rhythm is an intrinsic ~24-hour timing system that plays a crucial role in regulating immune functions and maintaining metabolic homeostasis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how the circadian clock influences five key immune cell types-macrophages, dendritic cells, B cells, T cells, and natural killer cells-affecting processes such as phagocytosis, antigen presentation, cytokine secretion, cell migration, antibody production, and cytotoxicity, along with their underlying molecular mechanisms. This review also examines the effects of circadian disruption on metabolic disorders-including obesity, insulin resistance/type 2 diabetes, and atherosclerosis-mediated by immune cell pathways. Key mechanisms include adipose tissue macrophage polarization, rhythmic IL-17A secretion by γδ T cells, and the temporal regulation of the Th17/Treg cell balance. Additionally, we address current challenges in fully elucidating these mechanisms and translating them into clinical applications, emphasizing promising avenues such as multi-omics integration, biomarker identification, and chrono-immunotherapy, while noting that the latter remains supported primarily by retrospective and hypothesis-generating evidence. Overall, this review seeks to provide a comprehensive framework for the emerging field of circadian immunometabolism and to facilitate the development of time-based precision strategies for managing metabolic diseases.

43075377.titulo: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in the tumor host macroenvironment: organ crosstalk, treatment trajectories, and net clinical benefit.
43075377.autores: Jia MJ, Zhou J, … Liang FQ (5 autores)
43075377.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in the tumor host macroenvironment: organ crosstalk, treatment trajectories, and net clinical benefit.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43075377.resumo_original: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome links metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease, yet oncology commonly treats these conditions as separate comorbidities. This review examines CKM as a measurable component of the tumor host macroenvironment that may influence treatment tolerance and competing mortality. We integrate adipose, cardiorenal, and immune-metabolic pathways; clonal hematopoiesis is considered as a candidate link between inflammation, vascular injury, and treatment exposure, rather than a CKM staging criterion. Cancer and its treatment can also alter CKM status through organ injury and catabolism. Population studies associate higher CKM stages with cancer incidence and adverse host outcomes, but evidence for cancer-specific mortality and treatment efficacy remains inconsistent or limited. The central question is therefore whether CKM captures biologically meaningful host variation that changes tumor natural history, treatment tolerance, or both. Our oncology-adapted phenotyping framework retains the original American Heart Association CKM stages and adds organ reserve and activity, tumor and treatment context, and longitudinal change. It applies to both patients with active cancer and survivors, without introducing a new stage or stage-specific treatment recommendation. We outline assessment from pretreatment to survivorship and distinguish established cardiorenal indications from exploratory anticancer effects of CKM therapies. Net clinical benefit requires joint assessment of tumor control, treatment delivery, cardiorenal events, function, and patient priorities. Prospective validation is needed before the added phenotypes can guide cancer-treatment selection.

43077455.titulo: Electrical, mechanical, and morphological properties of nano-filled HTV-SR/EPDM blends under AC corona aging.
43077455.autores: Saleem MZ, Noorden ZA, … Algamili AS (5 autores)
43077455.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Electrical, mechanical, and morphological properties of nano-filled HTV-SR/EPDM blends under AC corona aging.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43077455.resumo_original: Among the various factors, corona discharge is recognized as one of the most threatening to degrade polymeric insulators. Over time, corona-induced deterioration has become a more dominant phenomenon in extra- and ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines. Therefore, this study investigates the aging effects on optimally balanced weight-percentage samples of high-temperature-vulcanized silicone rubber/ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (HTV-SR/EPDM) incorporating boron nitride (BN) and silicon carbide (SiC) fillers to identify the most desirable composition for resistance to degradation. The nano-sized fillers were loaded at 1, 3, and 5 wt.%. The test samples were subjected to an AC corona discharge for 72 h, utilizing a multi-needle high-voltage electrode and a plane-grounded electrode arrangement. The deterioration characteristics of the blend materials, both before and after aging, were evaluated through electrical, morphological, and mechanical analyses encompassing volume conductivity, dielectric response, scanning electron microscopy, tensile strength, and hardness measurements. The results revealed that at 8 kV stress across 30-60 °C, corona exposure increased the volume conductivity of 3 wt.% BN nanocomposites by only 25.8%-36.5%, whereas the unfilled blend experienced a much higher increase of 45.3%-88.3%. After corona exposure, high-loading nanocomposites retained up to 42.4% greater tensile strength than the degraded unfilled blend. The surface roughness was relatively lower for the filled blend samples following the corona discharge. Overall, the blend sample with 3 wt.% of BN demonstrated consistent behavior under all investigated conditions, indicating better corona-aging retardation. It has been shown that the incorporation of nano-sized fillers retards material degradation, thereby enhancing the performance of polymeric insulation.

43082261.titulo: Cortisol-Producing Adrenocortical Adenomas Drive a Unique Cytokine and Steroid Profile that Suppress Macrophage Immunity.
43082261.autores: Crastin A, David Onesimu EL, … Ronchi CL (11 autores)
43082261.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Cortisol-Producing Adrenocortical Adenomas Drive a Unique Cytokine and Steroid Profile that Suppress Macrophage Immunity.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43082261.resumo_original:
Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) in patients with adrenocortical adenoma is associated with increased infection-related morbidity and mortality, although the mechanisms underpinning immunity dysfunction remain poorly defined. Given the central role of macrophages in innate immunity and immune-metabolic coordination, we investigated whether circulating factors in overt Cushing's syndrome (CS) and MACS alter macrophage inflammatory and metabolic function.
Primary human macrophages were polarised toward an inflammatory M1-like phenotype and treated with serum from patients with CS (n=6), MACS (n=10), or inactive endocrine adenoma. Cytokine secretion, polarisation markers, phagocytic capacity, mitochondrial viability, oxidative phosphorylation, and glycolysis were assessed and correlated with clinical and biochemical characteristics.
CS serum significantly reduced TNF-α and IL-6 secretion, and increased mitochondrial viability while promoting features consistent with anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization. CS serum also markedly suppressed oxidative phosphorylation, glycolysis, and ATP production. MACS serum elicited a similar but attenuated profile, characterized by trends toward suppression of inflammatory and metabolic activation, consistent with early glucocorticoid-driven immune remodelling. Across all samples, serum-free cortisol concentrations correlated negatively with macrophage inflammatory cytokine production and positively with anti-inflammatory markers.
Patients with CS and MACS possess unique glucocorticoid and cytokine profiles that drive suppression of macrophage inflammatory and metabolic function. These findings provide mechanistic evidence that even mild cortisol excess in MACS may contribute to early innate immune remodelling that predisposes to infection and impaired inflammatory resilience.

43081773.titulo: Schwann Cells Mount an Early Injury Response in Sarm1 Knockout Nerves, and Glial Sarm1 Loss Delays Axon Degeneration.
43081773.autores: Stepanova E, Hunter-Chang S, … Deppmann C (14 autores)
43081773.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Schwann Cells Mount an Early Injury Response in Sarm1 Knockout Nerves, and Glial Sarm1 Loss Delays Axon Degeneration.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43081773.resumo_original: Schwann cells (SCs) transition into a Repair state after peripheral nerve injury, but their early injury response remains poorly understood. To characterize SC injury responses before axon fragmentation and in the absence of axonal SARM1 activity, we profiled WT and global Sarm1-knockout nerves within the first day after transection by single-nucleus RNA sequencing. We observed a substantial transcriptional injury response, enrichment of a putative intermediate SC state, and increased oxidative phosphorylation gene expression across injured SC states. These genotype-associated differences may reflect the absence of SARM1-dependent axonal signals, Sarm1 loss within SCs, or contributions from other cell types; they do not establish cell-autonomous control of the repair-state transition. We then asked whether glial Sarm1 influences axon degeneration when neuronal SARM1 is intact. We detect Sarm1 transcripts in SCs that increase after nerve injury. Reducing SC or glial Sarm1 delayed axon degeneration in co-cultures of Sarm1-knockout SCs with wild-type neurons, Sarm1 conditional knockout in Sox10 positive cells in mice, and Drosophila with pan-glial dSarm knockdown. Together, our findings characterize early SC injury states in nerves lacking SARM1-dependent axon degeneration and support a glial contribution to axon degeneration kinetics.

43074420.titulo: miR-493 and miR-995-3p negatively regulate TSSK1 and affect male fertility in Zeugodacus cucurbitae.
43074420.autores: Han HL, Zhai XD, … Wei D (7 autores)
43074420.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «miR-493 and miR-995-3p negatively regulate TSSK1 and affect male fertility in Zeugodacus cucurbitae.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43074420.resumo_original: MicroRNAs are crucial upstream regulators of reproductive development across insect species. In this study, we identified two testis-highly expressed miRNAs, the novel miR-493 and the known miR-995-3p, that directly target the testis-specific serine/threonine kinase 1 (ZcTSSK1) in Zeugodacus cucurbitae (Coquillett). Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) assays showed that miR-493, miR-995-3p, and ZcTSSK1 co-localized in the testicular transformation region. Overexpression of miR-493 and miR-995-3p significantly reduced the total sperm count and sperm viability, and decreased the offspring hatching rate. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of ZcTSSK1 reduced sperm count and sperm viability, decreased total bound phosphate groups in testes, elevated the proportion of apoptotic cells, and induced abnormal sperm morphology. These phenotypes closely mirrored those induced by miRNA overexpression. Collectively, these results indicate that miR-493 and miR-995-3p regulate ZcTSSK1 to modulate global protein phosphorylation in the testis and the differentiation of spermatids into mature sperm, thereby playing a crucial role in spermatogenesis in Z. cucurbitae. This study clarifies the essential role of the miR-493/miR-995-3p-ZcTSSK1 regulatory module in spermatogenesis and male fertility of Z. cucurbitae, and provides a molecular basis for exploring reproduction-targeted genetic control strategies against tephritid pests.

43071006.titulo: Structural and biochemical characterization of ligand binding, oxidative modulation and inhibitory mechanisms of human inorganic pyrophosphatase 1.
43071006.autores: Mawani JS, Gnann AD, … Dowling DP (6 autores)
43071006.revista: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
43071006.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Structural and biochemical characterization of ligand binding, oxidative modulation and inhibitory mechanisms of human inorganic pyrophosphatase 1.», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43071006.resumo_original: Human inorganic pyrophosphatase 1 (hsPPA1) is a ubiquitous metalloenzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of cytoplasmic inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) into inorganic phosphate (Pi). hsPPA1 maintains cellular phosphorus homeostasis by removing the PPi released during the synthesis of biomolecules, thus making biosynthetic reactions thermodynamically favorable. Therefore, hsPPA1 is critical to cellular metabolism, and its upregulation and overexpression in cancer-cell proliferation and metastasis make hsPPA1 a promising enzyme target for the development of anticancer drugs. Here, we report X-ray crystal structures of hsPPA1 in multiple liganded states: with magnesium ions, with lithium ions and a fluoride-inhibited structure complexed with magnesium and pyrophosphate ions. These structures show that hsPPA1 adopts the conserved oligonucleotide/oligosaccharide (OB) fold, and substrate binding induces subtle conformational changes in the active-site residues. The structure of hsPPA1 with lithium ions bound, combined with functional studies, showed that Li+ can bind in the same sites as the M1 and M2 magnesium ions and inhibit the enzyme. In addition, functional assays on the variants of the proposed catalytic base residue (Asp118) and phosphate ions revealed details of the chemical mechanism of hsPPA1 and the dual effects of phosphate on hsPPA1 activity. Finally, we report on the effect of magnesium concentrations and reducing agent on hsPPA1 activity. These findings reveal a deeper understanding of hsPPA1 at the molecular level and establish a framework for structure-based inhibitor design.

43075439.titulo: Microbiota-associated post-translational remodeling of immune cell states in gastrointestinal cancer.
43075439.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Microbiota-associated post-translational remodeling of immune cell states in gastrointestinal cancer.», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43075439.resumo_original: Microbial communities influence gastrointestinal (GI) cancer through metabolic exchange and immune regulation. Post-translational modifications (PTMs) can connect these signals to changes in chromatin, protein function and immune-cell states. This narrative review examines histone and non-histone modifications to explore how microbial inputs and host metabolism intersect in the regulation of immune-cell states and tumor immunity. Microbial metabolites can influence acyl-donor availability and PTM enzyme activity, while microbial sensing can reprogram host metabolism and downstream modification states. These routes provide a framework for understanding changes in lymphoid and myeloid cell function, whose consequences for tumor immunity depend on cellular and disease context. Among the studies assessed, evidence linking microbial interventions to immune-cell PTM changes in GI cancer is concentrated in colorectal cancer and its metastatic models. Findings from nonmalignant models, other cancers and host metabolic studies provide complementary insights into potentially relevant mechanisms. Their extension to microbiota-immune interactions in GI tumors requires attention to both microbial involvement and the functional contribution of specific modifications. Understanding how microbial inputs converge with host metabolism at the level of PTM regulation may reveal opportunities to modulate tumor immunity. Defining metabolite sources and cellular exposure, resolving the functions of individual modifications, and validating pathways in relevant anatomical and therapeutic settings will be important for identifying mechanisms that can inform biomarker and therapeutic development.

43073749.titulo: Mechanism study on the toxicity-reducing effect of processing on Xanthii Fructus based on transcriptomics and metabolomics.
43073749.autores: Geng Y, Mu C, … Han Y (6 autores)
43073749.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Mechanism study on the toxicity-reducing effect of processing on Xanthii Fructus based on transcriptomics and metabolomics.», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43073749.resumo_original: Xanthii Fructus, a commonly used traditional Chinese medicine in clinical practice, has hepatotoxicity in its raw form. Our previous studies have confirmed its liver injury-inducing effect and reduced toxicity after processing, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the alleviating effect of processing on the hepatotoxicity of Xanthii Fructus from the perspectives of transcriptomics and metabolomics. Rats were divided into control (CON), raw Xanthii Fructus (RXF), and processed Xanthii Fructus (PXF) groups. HE staining and serum ALT/AST measurement showed that PXF significantly alleviated liver pathological damage and decreased ALT/AST levels (P < 0.05). Transcriptomics revealed 283 core differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in bile secretion, FoxO, PI3K-Akt, and MAPK pathways. Metabolomics identified 354 core differential metabolites (DMs), mainly fatty acyls, carboxylic acids, and steroids, enriched in D-amino acid, histidine, arachidonic acid, retinol, beta-alanine, and sphingolipid metabolism. Integrated KEGG analysis showed that calcium signaling, Fc gamma R-mediated phagocytosis, and phospholipase D signaling were commonly enriched. The gene-metabolite network identified core metabolites sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) and 3-aminopropanoic acid (β-alanine, β-Ala), and key genes Adcy10, Pde1b, and Ugt2a1. qRT-PCR validation showed Adcy10, Pde1b, and Ugt2a1 were upregulated in RXF and reversed after processing, consistent with transcriptomics. These results indicate that processing alleviates hepatotoxicity by reversing disrupted gene expression and metabolic pathways, partially restoring hepatic homeostasis.

43083690.titulo: Travelers and Human-Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases.
43083690.autores: Charoensakulchai S, Nuntanajaroenkul N, … Onwan M (4 autores)
43083690.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Travelers and Human-Animal Pathogen Transmission: A One Health Review of Zoonotic and Reverse Zoonotic Diseases.», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43083690.resumo_original:
International travel can accelerate the geographic spread of zoonotic pathogens and, under certain circumstances, contribute to epidemic or pandemic dissemination. Travelers may also transmit human pathogens to wildlife at tourism interfaces, acting as intermediaries in zoonotic and reverse zoonotic transmission.
Archived WHO and ECDC reports were screened for major zoonotic outbreaks in which international travel contributed to cross-border spread. PubMed and Scopus were searched for studies of human-to-wildlife transmission involving tourists, visitors, or travelers and traveler behaviors that could facilitate transmission.
Among 14 major zoonotic outbreaks, travelers commonly acted as spreaders following initial animal-to-human spillover by importing infections into new regions, sometimes resulting in onward transmission. This pattern was prominent with respiratory infections such as SARS, MERS, influenza, and COVID-19 and vector-borne infections such as Oropouche and Zika. Twenty-one studies reported possible or confirmed reverse zoonotic transmission at human-wildlife tourism interfaces. Pathogens included respiratory viruses, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, enteric pathogens, and antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. Affected wildlife included great apes, primates, elephants, felines, carnivorans, ungulates, avians, reptiles, and urban-adapted wildlife in national parks, zoological parks, rehabilitation centers, and semi-urban parks. Five additional studies documented risky tourist behaviors, including close approach to, physical contact with, and feeding and visiting wildlife while having respiratory symptoms, and inadequate vaccination against measles, influenza, and polio.
Travelers can influence transmission bidirectionally by disseminating zoonotic pathogens and exposing wildlife to human pathogens. Travel medicine should incorporate wildlife-protective counseling on distancing, hygiene, waste disposal, and immunization alongside conventional traveler protection.

43081802.titulo: Assessing the role of single human chromosome 21 gene orthologues on amyloid-β toxicity in fly models.
43081802.autores: Wenz K, Lau H, … Niccoli T (4 autores)
43081802.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Assessing the role of single human chromosome 21 gene orthologues on amyloid-β toxicity in fly models.», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43081802.resumo_original: Individuals with Down syndrome face a high risk of early-onset Alzheimer's disease. While an additional copy of the amyloid beta precursor protein gene (APP) is a primary trigger, other human chromosome 21 (Hsa21) genes are known to modulate amyloid-β1-42 (Aβ42) pathology and response. However, the relative impact of single genes during early neurodevelopment or in adult neurons remains unclear. To systematically evaluate the contribution of single gene effects, we overexpressed conserved Hsa21 Drosophila orthologues in an adult-restricted model of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity and found no single gene was able to modulate this biology. To evaluate developmental effects, we expressed these Hsa21 orthologues in the developing fly eye. We found that overexpression of the Hsa21 orthologues Pten/TPTE, Sik2/SIK1, plp/PCNT, pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 significantly exacerbated Aβ42-induced rough eye phenotypes. Crucially, overexpression of pnt and O-fut2 was sufficient to drive severe neurodegeneration even in the absence of Aβ42. Our findings suggest that direct modulation of Aβ42 adult locomotor toxicity downstream of APP by single Hsa21 orthologues in adult neurons is limited in our model. Instead, overexpression of genes such as pnt/ETS2 and O-fut2/POFUT2 can disrupt early neurodevelopment, which may establish long-lasting vulnerabilities that impact on the later effect of Aβ42, underscoring the critical role of early brain development in later Down Syndrome Alzheimer's disease progression.

43063265.titulo: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
43063265.autores: Su T, Liu S, … Zhou ZH (5 autores)
43063265.resumo: Estrutura por crio-EM do complexo Saglin–SGS4 de Anopheles gambiae: SGS4 e SGS5 ligam Saglin e outras proteínas SG1 em extratos de glândula salivar; Saglin forma homodímero por coiled-coil e pontes dissulfeto.
43063265.resumo_original: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

resumo_blocos.racional: A transmissão bem-sucedida da malária por mosquitos Anopheles exige o desenvolvimento do Plasmodium no intestino médio seguido pela invasão das glândulas salivares pelos esporozoítos. Embora proteínas salivares como Saglin e as proteínas de superfície de glândula salivar SGS4 e SGS5 já fossem implicadas nessa etapa, a ausência completa de estruturas tridimensionais nativas impedia decifrar a mecânica molecular dessa interação.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores realizaram fracionamento bioquímico e análises por espectrometria de massas diretamente a partir de extratos nativos de glândulas salivares de Anopheles gambiae para mapear parceiros de ligação endógenos. Em seguida, resolveram por criomicroscopia eletrônica (cryo-EM) a estrutura em alta resolução do complexo nativo Saglin-SGS4 e conduziram análises estruturais comparativas entre diferentes complexos da família SG1 (salivary gland 1) com proteínas SGS.
resumo_blocos.resultados: As análises proteômicas demonstraram que SGS4 e SGS5 de Anopheles gambiae associam-se diretamente a Saglin e a outros membros da família SG1 nos extratos salivares. A estrutura por cryo-EM revelou que a Saglin forma homodímeros estabilizados por interações coiled-coil e pontes dissulfeto, acoplando-se longitudinalmente à subunidade SGS4. A comparação entre complexos SG1-SGS evidenciou uma arquitetura conservada nas proteínas SG1 combinada à plasticidade conformacional das proteínas SGS para acomodar parceiros SG1 de comprimentos distintos.

43072377.titulo: A gut-brain axis for aversive interoception drives innate and anticipatory emesis in Drosophila
43072377.autores: Karunakaran R, Choudhary P, … Das G (9 autores)
43072377.resumo: Em Drosophila, toxina ingerida lesa enterócitos do intestino médio, que geram ROS; o canal TrpA1 de células enteroendócrinas detecta o ROS e libera neuropeptídeos, que atuam em neurônios serotoninérgicos e dopaminérgicos e chegam aos corpos pedunculados. O circuito produz êmese inata e memória aversiva que antecipa a êmese.
43072377.resumo_original: The gut-brain pathways that transmit negative signals to the brain, influencing bodily functions and behavior, are not fully understood. We have identified a gut-brain axis in Drosophila that detects toxin-induced gut damage and triggers innate and learned, anticipatory emesis. Ingested toxins induce the midgut enterocytes to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS are detected by TrpA1 channels in enteroendocrine cells, resulting in the release of neuropeptides that signal gastric malaise. We also find evidence for midgut and ROS-independent mechanisms of toxin detection. Gut-derived neuropeptides act on brain serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons, which then communicate with the brain's sensory integration and memory centers, the mushroom bodies (MBs). This circuit enables vomiting and facilitates the formation of aversive memories. We find that the persistent activity of dopaminergic neurons mediates aversive reinforcement. Such activity lends itself to pairing the gut-derived malaise signal with odor representations in the MBs, enabling the flies to learn that the paired odor predicts toxin ingestion and to exhibit anticipatory emesis. Many components of this interoceptive pathway are likely conserved, providing a genetic model for exploring how aversive gut-brain communication influences metabolism, feeding, stress responses, and neurodegeneration.

resumo_blocos.racional: Os circuitos enteroceptivos do eixo intestino-cérebro capazes de detectar dano epitelial agudo induzido por toxinas ingeridas e convertê-lo em respostas comportamentais defensivas imediatas e memória aversiva permaneciam pouco elucidados em insetos. O estudo buscou mapear como o estresse oxidativo intestinal se traduz em comando neuroendócrino central e aprendizado antecipatório.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Utilizando linhagens genéticas de Drosophila melanogaster submetidas à ingestão controlada de toxinas luminais, os autores combinaram ensaios comportamentais de êmese inata e condicionamento olfativo antecipatório com manipulação genética de enterócitos, células enteroendócrinas expressando canais TrpA1 e circuitos aminérgicos centrais. A sinalização de espécies reativas de oxigênio (ROS), liberação de neuropeptídeos intestinais e atividade persistente de neurônios serotonérgicos e dopaminérgicos conectados aos corpos pedunculados (mushroom bodies) foram dissecadas funcionalmente.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Toxinas ingeridas induzem enterócitos do intestino médio a produzir espécies reativas de oxigênio (ROS), que são detectadas por canais TrpA1 em células enteroendócrinas — paralelamente a vias independentes de ROS — disparando a secreção de neuropeptídeos sinalizadores de mal-estar gástrico. Esses neuropeptídeos ativam neurônios serotonérgicos e dopaminérgicos cerebrais projetados aos corpos pedunculados, promovendo êmese defensiva imediata. A atividade persistente dos neurônios dopaminérgicos atua como reforço aversivo que associa o sinal visceral a odores pareados, gerando êmese antecipatória aprendida.

43066088.titulo: Metabolic profiling of brain and cerebrospinal fluid in cerebral malaria
43066088.autores: Sachdeva C, Forster R, … Daily JP (12 autores)
43066088.resumo: Metabolômica não direcionada de cérebro de camundongos com malária cerebral experimental e de cérebro e LCR de crianças com CM e coma não malárico: ECM altera energia e aminoácidos (ácidos pipecólico e lático); cérebro humano CM×NMC difere pouco; ácido glicérico sobe no LCR de CM.
43066088.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria (CM), a severe neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, is a common cause of pediatric mortality and long-term cognitive impairment in endemic regions. The mechanisms driving CM-associated coma and neuropathology are not fully understood. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of brain tissue from experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) mouse models and brain autopsy tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from children with CM and non-malarial coma (NMC). ECM brain samples exhibited significant metabolic alterations, including differences in energy metabolism and amino acids and elevated pipecolic and lactic acids. In contrast, CM and NMC brain metabolomes showed limited differences. CSF metabolomes from cohorts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Malawi showed elevated glyceric acid in CM compared with NMC. Together, these findings highlight metabolic perturbations in CM across species and sample types and identify glyceric acid as a potential CSF biomarker.

resumo_blocos.racional: A malária cerebral causada por Plasmodium falciparum permanece entre as principais causas de letalidade pediátrica e sequelas neurocognitivas duradouras, mas os distúrbios metabólicos neuroquímicos que sustentam o coma malárico em comparação a comas não maláricos e ao modelo murino ainda eram pouco caracterizados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores executaram perfilamento metabolômico não direcionado (untargeted metabolomics) comparando parênquima cerebral de camundongos com malária cerebral experimental (ECM) frente a tecido cerebral de autópsia e amostras pareadas de líquido cefalorraquidiano (LCR) obtidas de coortes pediátricas com malária cerebral (CM) versus coma não malárico (NMC) na República Democrática do Congo e no Maláui.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O tecido cerebral murino na ECM apresentou remodelamento metabólico pronunciado em vias bioenergéticas e de aminoácidos, destacando-se o acúmulo significativo de ácido pipecólico e ácido lático. Em contraste, o metaboloma post-mortem do parênquima cerebral humano diferiu pouco entre CM e NMC, mas o metaboloma do líquor nas duas coortes africanas revelou elevação consistente de ácido glicérico nos pacientes com malária cerebral em relação ao coma não malárico.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece um mapa comparativo direto entre o modelo murino de malária cerebral experimental (como o sistema PbA/C57BL/6J operado no LUCHM) e a doença pediátrica humana, posicionando os ácidos pipecólico, lático e especialmente o ácido glicérico liquórico como marcadores translacionais de disfunção bioenergética e barreira hematoencefálica.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Dosar lactato, ácido pipecólico e ácido glicérico no córtex e no líquor cisternal de camundongos C57BL/6J infectados com PbA nos dias 4 a 6 pós-infecção, correlacionando seus níveis à quebra de claudina-5 e ativação microglial.

43063246.titulo: Biostable insect kinin mimetics in either blood or sugar meals deter feeding in the mosquito Aedes aegypti (L.)
43063246.resumo: Seis miméticos biostáveis de cinina reduzem o comportamento alimentar de fêmeas de Ae. aegypti; 1728, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20 cortam o volume de sangue ingerido em 95%, 51% e 63%; antagonista de receptor reverte parcialmente o efeito.
43063246.resumo_original: In insects, kinins (leucokinins) regulate diverse physiological processes. Previously we found kinin mimetic 1728 elicits aversive behavioral responses in Aedes aegypti female mosquitoes of flying-, walking- or jumping away when offered in sucrose. The feeding effects of six insect kinin analogues with different EC50 on the recombinant mosquito kinin receptor, and containing aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) (1728, 1729, IK-Aib-12, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20) or β3-Pro (1460) for increased biostability, were investigated when offered in sugar or blood meals. We used a high-resolution, high-throughput feeding behaviors analysis device, the flyPAD, adapted for mosquitoes. Analogues 1728, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20 (1 mM) decreased the feeding behaviors towards both meals resulting in a reduction in sucrose volume ingested of 95%, 92%, and 33%, respectively, and reduced the volume of blood ingested by 95, 51 and 63%, respectively. Analogue IK-Aib-12 reduced blood volume ingested by 78%, having no effect on feeding behaviors towards sugar. Mimetics1728 and 1729 (1 mM) reduced the feeding behaviors towards blood, and the blood volume ingested by 95% and 91%, respectively. Analogues modulated feeding behaviors by mainly reducing the number of sips, feeding bursts, and activity bouts. Analogue 1728 reduced sugar volume ingested by 95% and its aversive behavioral effects were partially reversed by co-administration of a synthetic small molecule kinin receptor antagonist (SACC-0048555) that we discovered, as expected. However, the sugar volume ingested was still reduced by 73%. Co-administration of 1728 with suramin, a G protein decoupler, in contrast, restored both normal feeding behaviors and volume ingested. These results agreed with our previous finding that 1728 directly shuts down the sugar sensory neuron in the labella signaling through the kinin receptor, a GPCR.

resumo_blocos.racional: As cininas de insetos (leucocininas) regulam balanço hidrossalino e comportamento alimentar via receptores acoplados à proteína G (GPCRs), mas peptídeos nativos sofrem degradação proteolítica rápida. O estudo avaliou se análogos sintéticos biostáveis de cinina adicionados a refeições açucaradas ou sanguíneas bloqueiam a ingestão em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Seis análogos biostáveis de cinina com diferentes valores de EC50 frente ao receptor recombinante de cinina de mosquito — contendo ácido aminoisobutírico (Aib: 1728, 1729, IK-Aib-12, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20) ou β3-prolina (1460) — foram ofertados a 1 mM em sacarose ou repasto sanguíneo para fêmeas de Aedes aegypti. A microestrutura fina da alimentação (número de goles/sips, rajadas de alimentação e surtos de atividade) foi quantificada na plataforma de alta resolução flyPAD adaptada para mosquitos, seguida de ensaios farmacológicos de resgate com o antagonista sintético SACC-0048555 e com suramina (desacoplador de proteína G).
resumo_blocos.resultados: A 1 mM, os análogos 1728, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20 reduziram o volume ingerido de sacarose em 95%, 92% e 33% e cortaram o volume de sangue ingerido em 95%, 51% e 63%, respectivamente, enquanto o análogo 1729 reduziu o repasto sanguíneo em 91% e o IK-Aib-12 inibiu seletivamente a ingestão de sangue em 78% sem afetar o açúcar. A inibição decorreu da queda acentuada no número de goles e rajadas alimentares. Enquanto o antagonista do receptor de cinina SACC-0048555 reverteu parcialmente a aversão ao 1728 (mantendo 73% de redução de volume), a co-administração com suramina restaurou integralmente o comportamento e o volume ingerido, confirmando silenciamento de neurônios gustativos da labela via GPCR.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Traz ferramentas farmacológicas seletivas (como IK-Aib-12, específico para repasto sanguíneo, e 1728/1729) e métricas comportamentais de alta resolução para dissecar regulação pós-ingestão e sinalização por leucocininas em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti no insetário do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Utilizar análogos seletivos da via de cininas ou modulação de Lkr para testar se o fracionamento forçado do volume de repasto sanguíneo atenua o pico de hemo livre e a peroxidação lipídica intestinal em Aedes alimentadas com sangue HFHS.

43062890.titulo: Blood-derived dietary protein promotes sleep in the mosquito Aedes aegypti
43062890.autores: Zhang J, Tsujimoto H, … Keene AC (5 autores)
43062890.resumo: Proteína dietética do sangue (BSA sozinho reproduz o efeito) aumenta o sono de Aedes aegypti por vários dias após o repasto, além da fase de busca de hospedeiro; o receptor de leucocinina (Lkr) também foi testado por RNAi.
43062890.resumo_original: Sleep is a ubiquitous, yet highly variable, behavior across species. The duration and timing of sleep are influenced by ecological demands and dietary context. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, a blood-feeding insect with specialized nutritional requirements, the relationship between feeding and sleep remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how blood-derived dietary protein influences sleep regulation. Using postural analysis, videography, and arousal-threshold assays, we established that immobility bouts of ≥10 min reliably define sleep in A. aegypti. Mosquitoes lacking the circadian clock gene cycle still maintained daily sleep rhythms but exhibited reduced sleep duration and heightened overall activity. Infrared activity monitoring revealed that blood-fed females showed a marked increase in sleep beginning immediately after feeding and persisting for several days, accompanied by reduced locomotor activity. Notably, this sleep elevation lasted well beyond the cessation of previously reported host-seeking phases, raising the possibility of distinct phases of opportunistic vs. targeted host pursuit. To determine the dietary basis of this effect, we tested mosquitoes fed a bovine serum albumin (BSA)-based diet. BSA feeding alone was sufficient to mimic the sleep-promoting and activity-reducing effects of blood, suggesting dietary protein is a major nutritional regulator. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of the leucokinin receptor (Lkr), which has previously been associated with fluid homeostasis and feeding behavior, resulted in enhanced sleep and reduced activity, implicating mosquito LK signaling in the modulation of postprandial sleep. Together, these findings demonstrate that blood-derived proteins drive sustained increases in sleep and reductions in locomotor activity in A. aegypti. This work positions A. aegypti as a model for dissecting nutrient-specific regulation of sleep and highlights potential adaptive functions of protein-induced quiescence, such as energy conservation and predator avoidance. More broadly, it provides insight into how specialized diets shape the neural and behavioral architecture of sleep.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o sono seja profundamente moldado pelo contexto ecológico e nutricional, a relação entre hematofagia e regulação do sono em Aedes aegypti permanecia indefinida. Os autores investigaram se o repasto sanguíneo e especificamente seu componente proteico induzem estados prolongados de sono pós-prandial no vetor.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Combinando análise postural, videografia, ensaios de limiar de despertar (arousal-threshold) e monitoramento infravermelho contínuo de atividade locomotora em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti (incluindo mutantes do gene de relógio circadiano cycle), os autores validaram episódios de imobilidade ≥ 10 minutos como critério operacional de sono. Para isolar o gatilho nutricional e molecular, compararam sangue total a uma dieta artificial purificada de albumina sérica bovina (BSA) e realizaram silenciamento por RNAi do receptor de leucocinina (Lkr).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Mutantes de cycle mantiveram ritmos diários de sono, porém com menor duração total e hiperatividade basal. Em fêmeas selvagens, o repasto sanguíneo disparou aumento acentuado do sono e queda locomotora imediatamente após a alimentação, persistindo por vários dias — muito além da janela clássica de supressão de busca por hospedeiro. A ingestão isolada de BSA reproduziu integralmente o aumento sustentado de sono induzido pelo sangue, demonstrando que a proteína dietética é o regulador nutricional primário, enquanto o knockdown por RNAi de Lkr elevou o sono e reduziu a locomoção, implicando a via da leucocinina na modulação pós-prandial.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente nutrição pós-repasto, sinalização do receptor de leucocinina (Lkr) via RNAi e conservação energética em Aedes aegypti, abrindo uma variável comportamental inédita para os estudos de dieta HFHS (rica em lipídios/glicose versus proteína) conduzidos no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Monitorar em actímetros infravermelhos se fêmeas de Aedes aegypti alimentadas com sangue de camundongos obesos (HFHS) exibem alteração na duração da quiescência pós-prandial de ≥ 10 min e na expressão de Lkr em relação ao repasto controle.

43072483.titulo: Convergent evolution of bt resistance in insects: Receptor mutations, non-receptor mechanisms and polygenic adaptation
43072483.autores: Balaji A, Balakrishnan N, … Raghu R (5 autores)
43072483.resumo: Revisão que reúne mecanismos de resistência a Bt em insetos-praga: mutações em receptores (ABC, caderina, APN, ALP), mecanismos fora do receptor (ativação e sequestro da toxina, efeitos da microbiota) e arquitetura poligênica (variação de número de cópias em Helicoverpa zea), mais resistência a Vip3.
43072483.resumo_original: The extensive cultivation of transgenic Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) crops has constituted one of the largest human-mediated evolutionary selection experiments in modern agriculture. Although resistance is often attributed to specific management failures, accumulating global evidence shows that Bt-resistant populations repeatedly emerge across diverse agroecosystems and unrelated insect taxa, through comparable ecological conditions and a constrained set of adaptive mechanisms, indicating a central role for convergent evolution. This review integrates ecological, molecular and genomic perspectives into a single evolutionary framework. It argues that Bt resistance evolves through partially predictable trajectories shaped by convergent ecological pressures and constrained molecular pathways. At the ecological level, recurrent pressures such as prolonged Bt exposure, suboptimal toxin expression, inadequate refuge implementation and continuous host availability generate similar selection regimes in unrelated insect taxa. At the molecular level, convergence is most evident in receptor-gene modifications within ATP-binding cassette transporters, cadherins, aminopeptidases N and alkaline phosphatases, alongside non-receptor processes affecting toxin activation, sequestration and Bt susceptibility, including microbiota-associated effects. Genomic studies further demonstrate that resistance is not always explained by single major-effect mutations but can involve multilocus and polygenic architectures, as demonstrated by copy-number variation and standing quantitative-trait variation in Helicoverpa zea. The review also examines resistance to Vip3 toxins, considering reported genetic mechanisms and implications for Bt pyramids. These findings show how ecological pressures channel adaptation into a constrained set of molecular pathways, while diverse genetic architectures expand the evolutionary routes available to pest populations. We also discuss what molecular convergence means for resistance monitoring and management, and where the constraint may fail.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o surgimento de populações de insetos resistentes a culturas transgênicas expressando toxinas de Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) seja frequentemente atribuído a falhas isoladas de manejo local, evidências globais mostram evolução repetida da resistência em táxons distantes sob pressões seletivas equivalentes. O trabalho sintetiza um modelo evolutivo unificado integrando ecologia, vias moleculares restritas e arquitetura genômica poligênica.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão integrativa de estudos ecológicos, bioquímicos e genômicos populacionais sobre evolução convergente de resistência a toxinas Cry e Vip3 de Bacillus thuringiensis em lepidópteros e coleópteros-praga (incluindo Helicoverpa zea). Foram comparados regimes de seleção em campo (exposição prolongada, subdosagem tecidual e refúgio insuficiente), alterações em famílias de receptores de borda em escova, vias não ligadas a receptores e mapeamentos genômicos de variação de número de cópias (CNV) e locos quantitativos.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A síntese demonstra forte convergência molecular em quatro classes canônicas de receptores do intestino médio — transportadores ABC (como ABCC2), caderinas, aminopeptidases N (APN) e fosfatases alcalinas (ALP) — coexistindo com mecanismos não receptores de ativação proteolítica alterada, sequestro luminal de toxina e modulação pela microbiota intestinal. Revela ainda que, além de mutações monogênicas de grande efeito, a resistência em campo envolve arquiteturas poligênicas e variação de número de cópias (como documentado em Helicoverpa zea), além de mecanismos genéticos distintos frente a toxinas Vip3 em pirâmides Bt.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Incide diretamente no programa de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas do LUCHM em Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis, reforçando a necessidade de monitorar simultaneamente receptores ABCC2/APN/ALP, integridade da matriz peritrófica, proteases luminais e contribuição de simbiontes bacterianos como Enterococcus mundtii.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Cruzar ensaios de susceptibilidade a toxinas Cry em larvas de Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis com depleção/reconstituição de simbiontes intestinais para separar resistência mediada por receptores ABCC2 de mecanismos luminais dependentes da microbiota.

10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.titulo: A standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay with spatially defined bite areas
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.autores: Miot EF, Medkour H, … Pompon J (10 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.resumo: Preprint: ensaio padronizado de transmissão mosquito-camundongo com áreas de picada definidas (Miot, Pompon); abstract não lido, só o título.
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne viruses initiate infection in the skin, where interactions between viral particles, host cells, and mosquito saliva can influence early infection and subsequent viral dissemination. Investigating these events requires methods that link mosquito exposure to the precise site of inoculation. However, identifying individual bite sites during subsequent tissue collection remains a practical challenge in mosquito-to-mouse transmission models. Here, we describe a standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay that facilitates the localization of mosquito bite sites and targeted tissue sampling. The method combines a custom 3D-printed feeding device, individual mosquito exposure, and perforated adhesive tape to define the biting area and mark identified bite sites for subsequent collection. We demonstrate the application of this protocol using West Nile virus (WNV) and Dengue virus (DENV)-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes with C57BL/6J mice and A129 Ifnar1-/- mice, respectively. All infected mosquitoes successfully blood-fed within 20 min of exposure. After three infected-mosquito bites, mice developed clinical signs from approximately day 6 post-bite, with mortality occurring between days 8 and 10 for WNV, while disease onset occurred at 4 days post bite and most of the mice recovered by day 10 for DENV. To investigate early WNV viral kinetics in skin, WNV genomic RNA was quantified in biopsies collected at marked bite sites and the draining inguinal lymph nodes. Viral RNA was detected in both tissues as early as 1 h post-bite, and RNA levels increased significantly at 24 h post-bite. This protocol provides a practical approach for identifying mosquito bite sites and investigating early tissue-level events following vector-mediated transmission. With appropriate validation, the protocol can be adapted to other vector pathogen host systems and downstream analyses.

resumo_blocos.racional: A transmissão de arbovírus inicia-se na derme, onde partículas virais, células residentes do hospedeiro e fatores salivares do mosquito interagem nos primeiros minutos pós-picada. Contudo, localizar com precisão milimétrica o ponto exato de inoculação individual para biópsia tecidual precoce seguia sendo um entrave técnico nos modelos mosquito-camundongo.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Desenvolveu-se um protocolo padronizado de transmissão mosquito-para-camundongo combinando um dispositivo de alimentação impresso em 3D, exposição individualizada de mosquitos e fita adesiva perfurada que delimita a janela cutânea de picada e marca cada ponto de repasto. O método foi validado expondo camundongos C57BL/6J e A129 Ifnar1-/- a três fêmeas de Aedes aegypti infectadas respectivamente com vírus do Nilo Ocidental (WNV) ou Dengue (DENV), seguido de quantificação de RNA genômico viral em biópsias cutâneas demarcadas e linfonodos inguinais drenantes em 1 h e 24 h pós-picada.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Todas as fêmeas infectadas realizaram repasto sanguíneo completo em até 20 minutos de exposição controlada. Após três picadas infectantes, camundongos C57BL/6J desenvolveram sinais clínicos de WNV por volta do dia 6 e mortalidade entre os dias 8 e 10, enquanto camundongos A129 Ifnar1-/- apresentaram início clínico de DENV no dia 4 com recuperação majoritária até o dia 10. O RNA genômico de WNV já foi detectado tanto na biópsia cutânea demarcada quanto no linfonodo inguinal drenante em apenas 1 hora pós-picada, elevando-se significativamente em 24 horas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Protocolo de baixo custo (impressão 3D + máscara adesiva perfurada) imediatamente adaptável ao biotério C57BL/6J e insetário do LUCHM tanto para arbovírus quanto para rastrear a deposição dérmica de esporozoítos de Plasmodium berghei ANKA e proteínas salivares.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Fabricar em impressora 3D o adaptador de área delimitada para comparar a cinética cutânea (1 h vs 24 h) e o infiltrado inflamatório dérmico após picada de fêmeas de Aedes criadas sob dieta padrão versus HFHS.

43069274.titulo: A synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
43069274.autores: Wang F, Zhao W, … Zhang J (13 autores)
43069274.resumo: FIB-SEM e eletrofisiologia revelam complexos mitocôndria–fita–vesícula sináptica em fotorreceptores: rodopsina de bastonete com par 1:1 megamitocôndria–fita; desmonte do complexo precede a perda funcional na degeneração (Nat Commun).
43069274.resumo_original: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural-metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

resumo_blocos.racional: Sinapses de fotorreceptores dependem da cooperação estreita entre mitocôndrias, fitas sinápticas (synaptic ribbons) e vesículas para sustentar liberação contínua de neurotransmissores, mas a organização tridimensional nanoscópica desses elementos em módulos bioenergéticos funcionais entre bastonetes e cones permanecia obscura.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores empregaram microscopia eletrônica de varredura com feixe de íons focalizado (FIB-SEM) combinada a registros eletrofisiológicos em retina de mamíferos, reconstruindo em 3D terminais de bastonetes (rod spherules) e pedículos de cones. Avaliaram ainda a perturbação genética da proteína de ancoragem mitocondrial sintafilina (syntaphilin) e acompanharam a integridade ultraestrutural do complexo em um modelo de degeneração retiniana antes do declínio funcional.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A reconstrução por FIB-SEM revelou complexos sinápticos mitocôndria-fita-vesícula (sMRVcs) com arquiteturas subtipo-específicas: esférulas de bastonetes exibem pareamento estrito 1:1 entre uma única megamitocôndria e uma fita sináptica para sustentar liberação contínua de glutamato no escuro, ao passo que pedículos de cones abrigam múltiplos sMRVcs distribuídos, além de sítios de liberação não associados à fita voltados a células horizontais. A deleção de sintafilina alterou a razão para 2:1 nos bastonetes ao recrutar mitocôndrias extras junto à fita e potencializou a transmissão sináptica, enquanto na degeneração retiniana a desmontagem do sMRVc (fragmentação mitocondrial e destacamento da fita) precedeu a perda funcional.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Exemplifica o poder analítico do FIB-SEM para quantificar acoplamento físico-metabólico e estequiometria organelar em escala nanométrica, servindo de referência metodológica direta para os projetos de contactoma mitocôndria-organela no CENABIO/LUCHM.

10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.titulo: The ACDC domains of AP2-O3 and FD3 contribute to protein interactions and ookinete development
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.autores: Tang J, Liu B, … Li Z (7 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.resumo: Preprint: domínios ACDC de AP2-O3 e FD3 e o desenvolvimento do oocineto de Plasmodium.
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.resumo_original: The Apicomplexan AP2 (ApiAP2) family of transcription factors are key regulators of Plasmodium spp. parasite development. In addition to containing AP2 DNA-binding domains, nine ApiAP2 proteins also encode an apicomplexan-specific ACDC domain whose function remains largely unknown. Here, we dissect the biological role of the ACDC domain from two female-specific regulators, AP2-O3 and FD3, using the rodent malaria model Plasmodium yoelii and the human malaria parasite P. falciparum. In Plasmodium yoelii, deletion of the ACDC domain preserved AP2-O3 and FD3 protein presence and nuclear localization without significantly affecting asexual growth or gametocyte production. However, deletion of these domains impaired the gametocyte-to-ookinete transition, reducing ookinete conversion efficiency. Proteomic and biochemical studies indicate that the AP2-O3 ACDC domain interacts with FD3, while the FD3 ACDC domain preferentially associates with full-length FD3. Transcriptomic data showed that over 80% of transcripts that increased after FD3 ACDC deletion were also higher following AP2-O3 loss, with female gametocyte marker expression largely unchanged. In Plasmodium falciparum, removing the FD3 ACDC domain did not affect female lineage-specific expression of FD3, nuclear localization of FD3, or the asexual growth and gametocyte maturation of parasites. Leveraging the high sequence conservation of ACDC domains across the Plasmodium genus, we conducted structure-based virtual screening of 283 compounds targeting the predicted PfAP2-O3 and PfFD3 ACDC interaction interface. Seven compounds ranked among the top candidate inhibitors for both domains, and the highest-priority ligand for each domain was further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Collectively, our findings support a role for ACDC domains in ApiAP2 protein interactions and identify candidate compounds for future experimental evaluation as potential transmission-blocking leads.

resumo_blocos.racional: Fatores de transcrição da família ApiAP2 governam transições críticas do ciclo de Plasmodium, e nove deles possuem na extremidade um domínio exclusivo de apicomplexas denominado ACDC cuja função bioquímica era desconhecida. O estudo investigou o papel do domínio ACDC nos reguladores específicos da linhagem feminina AP2-O3 e FD3 durante o desenvolvimento sexual e formação de oocinetos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Utilizando edição genética nos modelos murino Plasmodium yoelii e humano Plasmodium falciparum, os autores deletaram seletivamente os domínios ACDC de AP2-O3 e FD3 avaliando expressão, localização nuclear, crescimento assexuado, gametocitogênese e eficiência de conversão de gametócitos em oocinetos. Complementaram a análise com ensaios proteômicos/bioquímicos de interação proteica, RNA-seq comparativo e triagem virtual baseada em estrutura de 283 compostos contra a interface predita PfAP2-O3/PfFD3 seguida de dinâmica molecular.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Em P. yoelii e P. falciparum, a deleção do domínio ACDC preservou a expressão e a localização nuclear de AP2-O3 e FD3 sem afetar a replicação sanguínea assexuada nem a produção de gametócitos, mas bloqueou severamente a transição gametócito-oocineto em P. yoelii. Ensaios bioquímicos mostraram que o domínio ACDC de AP2-O3 interage com FD3 e o ACDC de FD3 promove autoassociação, com mais de 80% de sobreposição nos transcritos desregulados após perda de ambos. A triagem virtual de 283 moléculas identificou sete candidatos prioritários capazes de alvejar ambos os domínios ACDC conservados.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Identifica uma interface proteína-proteína altamente conservada (domínio ACDC em AP2-O3/FD3) indispensável para a maturação do oocineto no intestino do mosquito, oferecendo novos alvos químicos de bloqueio de transmissão alinhados à frente de Plasmodium do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar experimentalmente se inibidores candidatos da interface ACDC bloqueiam a conversão ex vivo de gametócitos em oocinetos de Plasmodium berghei ANKA e impedem a travessia do epitélio intestinal do vetor.

43074085.titulo: Assessment of natural filariae infections in the mosquitoes of Karen state, Myanmar: a cross-sectional PCR survey in six villages
43074085.autores: Rongthong P, Kularbkeeree T, … Nosten F (8 autores)
43074085.resumo: Em seis vilas de Karen (Mianmar), 5,2% (40/772) dos mosquitos tiveram PCR positivo para filárias; W. bancrofti em metade, incluindo Anopheles barbirostris e Aedes albopictus/pseudoalbopictus; estimativa de taxa de inoculação entomológica de 0,094 picada infectante por pessoa-dia.
43074085.resumo_original:
Filarial nematodes transmitted by mosquitos cause significant burdens and important stigma in the affected communities. Focal transmission of Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi was detected incidentally during blood surveys conducted for a program of malaria elimination in Karen state, Myanmar. The objective of this study was to assess filariae infections in selected mosquito species collected in these villages striving to identify the potential vectors, characterise their biting behaviours and estimate the entomological indices of transmission.
Cross-sectional entomological surveys were conducted in September 2019 in six villages. Mosquitos were captured over 24-h diel cycles using the human-landing catch and cow-baited trap collection methods, and identified with dichotomic morphological identification keys. A subset of the specimens of potential vector species was randomly selected and tested with a filariasis PCR assay targeting the parasites 5S rRNA gene. For positive Aedes specimens, correct identification of the filariae and vector species was confirmed with DNA sequencing of the filariasis and mosquito cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 PCR products.
Overall 5.2% (40/772) mosquito specimens had a positive filariasis PCR result. W. bancrofti DNA was found in half of the positive specimens. Three other zoonotic Brugia and Dirofilaria filariae species were also identified. W. bancrofti DNA was detected in known vector species including Anopheles barbirostris, An. hyrcanus, Downsiomyia harinasutai, Finlaya poicilia and Culex sitiens. Furthermore, it was also found in Aedes albopictus/pseudoalbopictus and Armigeres flavus. W. bancrofti entomological inoculation rate estimate was 0.094 infective bites/person-day (95%CI 0.049 to 0.164). Only 7.5% (3/40) of the positive specimens were captured indoors with the human-landing catch collection method between 9 PM and 5 AM. Specimens infected with zoonotic filariae were captured with the human-landing catch collection method highlighting the potential for zoonotic filariasis transmission in this area. Furthermore, infected specimens were collected in the cow-baited trap suggesting veterinary-based vector control interventions targeting livestock could be used to tackle filariasis transmission in this setting.
This study identified potential vectors of Wuchereria bancrofti and three zoonotic filariae species in Karen state. Mosquito bed nets may have only a limited efficacy against filariasis vectors in this area. Trials of vector control interventions preventing outdoor and early transmission are warranted.

43068115.titulo: From reactive control to precision environmental health: a One Health-based scoping review of vector management strategies in China
43068115.autores: Guo X, Lin Q, … Guo L (8 autores)
43068115.resumo: Revisão de escopo One Health sobre manejo de vetores, do controle reativo à saúde ambiental de precisão (Sci One Health).
43068115.resumo_original: Climate change, urbanization, and global travel have accelerated the resurgence of Aedes-borne diseases, posing growing public health threats. Conventional vector control remains largely reactive and chemical-dependent and is increasingly challenged by climate-driven changes in vector habitats. Using China as a case study, this scoping review examines the shift toward precision environmental health under a One Health framework. We trace surveillance advances from manual vector indices to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled ecological sensing and examine multisource early-warning approaches integrating meteorological, biological, and human-related data for dynamic risk classification. We also consider how technological interventions, including drone-assisted precision control and biological control, can be integrated with social governance to support climate-resilient health systems. Drawing on these experiences, we propose a Layered Technology framework intended to support adaptable, environmentally sustainable vector management in resource-constrained settings, particularly in the Global South. Finally, we call for coordinated international data sharing and collaboration to address cross-border environmental and public health threats.

43069404.titulo: Antimicrobial peptides are differentially regulated in blood and visceral adipose tissue in obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction and linked to NLRP3-related signaling
43069404.autores: Casado M, Gómez-Ambrosi J, … Catalán V (13 autores)
43069404.resumo: Em 108 participantes, obesidade se associa a perfil circulante de peptídeos antimicrobianos (catelicidina, calprotectina, entre outros); adipócitos viscerais humanos e macrófagos THP-1 ligam esses peptídeos à sinalização de NLRP3.
43069404.resumo_original: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation in which visceral adipose tissue (VAT) plays a central immunometabolic role. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) integrate host defense and inflammatory signaling, but their regulation across metabolic compartments in human obesity remains incompletely defined. We evaluated circulating AMP concentrations and gene expression levels in VAT and circulating leukocytes from 108 participants classified according to obesity and glycemic status. These analyses were complemented with mechanistic studies in human visceral adipocytes evaluating inflammatory and microbiota-related stimuli, effects of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)related modulation, and crosstalk with PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Obesity was associated with a selective circulating AMP profile characterized by higher cathelicidin, calprotectin, lipocalin-2 and neutrophil elastase together with lower α-defensin 6 and β-defensin 1. In VAT, obesity was accompanied by increased expression of several inflammatory AMP-related genes together with higher NLRP3 and NLRP6 expression and reduced DEFB1, with additional differences emerging across glycemic groups. Circulating leukocytes displayed a partially overlapping but distinct transcriptional profile, consistent with compartment-specific regulation rather than a generalized AMP response. In vitro, visceral adipocytes showed gene- and stimulus-dependent AMP responses to inflammatory and microbiota-related signals. NLRP3 silencing attenuated selected LPS-induced inflammatory and antimicrobial responses, whereas the glucose-lowering medication glibenclamide promoted complementary stimulus-dependent effects. Adipocyte-conditioned medium modified AMP expression in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Collectively, these findings identify a selective, compartment-dependent remodeling of antimicrobial pathways in obesity and obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, with NLRP3-related mechanisms emerging as a potential contributor to the regulation of selected antimicrobial responses in visceral adipocytes.

43074418.titulo: Itaconate: An Emerging Metabolic Regulator Linking Immunity and Ferroptosis
43074418.autores: Li S, Chen Y, … Nan Y (8 autores)
43074418.resumo: Revisão crítica do itaconato (ACOD1/IRG1) na ligação entre imunometabolismo, sinalização redox e ferroptose; aponta confusão frequente entre itaconato endógeno e derivados administrados (4-octil e dimetil itaconato).
43074418.resumo_original:
Itaconate, generated in activated myeloid cells by aconitate decarboxylase 1 (historically termed immune-responsive gene 1), coordinates immunometabolism, redox signalling and regulated cell death. Emerging evidence links this pathway to ferroptosis; however, interpretation is complicated by the frequent conflation of endogenous itaconate with exogenously administered native itaconate and electrophilic derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate and dimethyl itaconate.
This review critically integrates the biosynthesis, transport and intercellular signalling of itaconate with its effects on ferroptosis. Evidence is examined across solute carrier family 7 member 11-dependent cystine uptake, glutathione supply, glutathione peroxidase 4 expression, stability and catalytic activity, iron-sulfur clusters, ferritinophagy, phospholipid remodelling, mitochondrial redox signalling and selective autophagy, distinguishing cell-autonomous effects in myeloid cells from cell-nonautonomous transfer to parenchymal and tumour cells.
The available evidence supports a context-dependent model: itaconate-related signalling can suppress ferroptosis and limit acute tissue injury, but may also preserve immunosuppressive myeloid populations or confer ferroptosis resistance on tumours; at high pharmacological exposures, selected compounds can instead promote ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
Clinical translation requires compound-resolved terminology, validated ferroptosis endpoints, cell-specific delivery, quantitative exposure and target-engagement biomarkers and careful assessment of infection- and tumour-related risks.

resumo_blocos.racional: O itaconato, sintetizado em células mieloides ativadas pela enzima aconitato descarboxilase 1 (ACOD1/IRG1), conecta reprogramação imunometabólica, sinalização redox e ferroptose. Contudo, a literatura recente confunde efeitos do itaconato endógeno com derivados eletrofílicos exógenos como 4-octil-itaconato (4-OI) e dimetil-itaconato (DMI).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão mecanística crítica que disseca comparativamente a biossíntese, o transporte e a sinalização intercelular do itaconato nativo versus seus derivados alquilados/eletrofílicos sobre os eixos centrais da ferroptose: captação de cistina dependente de SLC7A11, síntese de glutationa, expressão e estabilidade catalítica de GPX4, centros ferro-enxofre, ferritinofagia, remodelamento de fosfolipídios poli-insaturados e autofagia seletiva em células mieloides e parenquimatosas.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A análise estabelece um modelo estritamente dependente de contexto e composto: em doses fisiológicas ou moderadas, o eixo do itaconato sustenta SLC7A11/GPX4 e defesas antioxidantes que suprimem a ferroptose e limitam a lesão tecidual aguda, distinguindo ações célula-autônomas em macrófagos/micróglia da transferência parácrina para células endoteliais e parenquimatosas. Em contrapartida, exposições farmacológicas elevadas a derivados eletrofílicos específicos podem inverter o fenótipo e disparar ferroptose dependente de ferritinofagia.

43075943.titulo: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster
43075943.autores: Okuno T, Woodward A, … Hata J (4 autores)
43075943.resumo: Aplica pré-processamento de fMRI a dados de cálcio de cérebro inteiro de Drosophila e os cruza com conectomas FlyEM/FlyWire; a correlação conectividade funcional × estrutural cai com o número de regiões e neurônios com sinapses não segregadas contribuem mais para a conectividade funcional.
43075943.resumo_original: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster, FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC-SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC-SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC-SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

43065052.titulo: Advancing a tool for Aedes aegypti breeding-site surveillance: validation of manual identification of trash and tires on unmanned aerial imaging
43065052.autores: Woo KE, Tarpenning MS, … Rosser JI (13 autores)
43065052.resumo: Validação de identificação manual de lixo e criadouros para vigilância de Aedes aegypti.
43065052.resumo_original:
Trash accumulations and discarded tires can retain water and may provide habitat for Aedes aegypti, but the reproducibility of identifying and classifying these features from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery has not been established.
We evaluated manual trash mapping in two Kenyan settings, Ukunda and Kisumu. Raters delineated visible trash polygons on high-resolution UAV orthomosaics and assigned categories using a seven-category scheme and a collapsed three-group scheme (low-risk trash, high-risk trash, and tires). Classification agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha. Spatial inter-rater and intra-rater consistency were evaluated from polygon overlap and unique area metrics.
Pairwise inter-rater agreement for classification was strong (mean unweighted Cohen's kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.75-0.86; mean weighted kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.61-0.97). Three-rater Fleiss' kappa was 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.83) and increased to 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.93) for the collapsed risk groups. Standard and fuzzy Krippendorff's alpha values were 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) and 0.94 (95% CI 0.91-0.96), respectively. Spatial analyses showed overlap in major trash areas but meaningful differences in detection and boundary placement. Intra-rater feature-specific unique area ranged from 4.7 to 18.5%; pooled across all seven features, unique area was 31.1% (95% CI 29.8-32.4).
Manual interpretation of UAV imagery is reproducible for image-based identification and classification of visible trash and tires, particularly for visually distinctive features such as tires. The method measures potential habitat proxies rather than confirmed Aedes aegypti breeding productivity; entomological ground validation remains necessary. Standardized annotations may also support future automated image classification approaches.
