43037379.titulo: Evolutionary Events Underlying Vector Competence and Epidemiological Variation in Hematophagous Diptera with Special Reference to Sand Flies and Mosquitoes.
43037379.autores: Sinha S, Pandey R, … Mishra N (5 autores)
43037379.resumo: Revisão sobre a evolução da hematofagia e dos traços de competência vetorial em dípteros, sem dados novos.
43037379.resumo_original:
Order Diptera includes house flies, blow flies, horse flies, midges, mosquitoes, sand flies, etc. Among these, mosquitoes and sand flies play a central role in the transmission of diseases affecting man and animals. They are typically characterised by a single pair of functional wings and a reduced, modified pair of halteres. Dipterans have evolved over 200 million years, undergoing extensive diversification shaped by adaptations in flight, sensory biology, feeding behaviour, and life history traits. Hematophagy is independently evolved in mosquitoes and sand flies, has been a key trait linked to reproductive success, while also facilitating pathogen transmission.
The ability of this order of insects to transmit diseases/pathogens is referred as vector competence. It depends on complex interactions between vector genetics, microbiota, immune responses and environmental factors. It also involves multiple physiological barriers within the insect/vector. More than 150,000 species described are distributed across numerous genera and evolutionary lineages. Dipterans have well-defined synapomorphies, which include specialised mouthparts and complete metamorphosis, which have helped them to exploit diverse ecological niches.
Understanding their evolutionary history and important biological traits underlying vector competence is crucial for explaining why only certain species efficiently transmit pathogens, parasites, bacteria and viruses. This kind of knowledge is crucial for improving vector surveillance, designing new control strategies, and targeted intervention for reducing the global burden of vector-borne diseases. Although many arthropods can carry pathogens incidentally, a limited number of these hematophagous insects act as consistent and efficient disease vectors. Hence, play a crucial role in the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases.
Successful transmission of the pathogen depends predominantly on vector competence. This reflects the genetic compatibility between the pathogen and the arthropod vector, as most ingested pathogens are killed during blood meal digestion. The broader concept of vectorial capacity and vectorial competence is shaped largely by complex interactions with the vector, host, pathogen, environment, and the arthropod-associated microbiota. This significantly influences host morphology and transmission efficiency. Notably, vectorial capacity is not a static phenomenon; it varies across time and space, thereby altering host-pathogen transmission dynamics/cycles. Feeding behaviour is attributed to transmission dynamics, like anthropophilic mosquitoes, e.g. Aedes spp. exhibit more susceptibility to viral infections as they predominantly feed on humans. Hematophagy/blood feeding occurs at different life stages across insect/vector taxa, with only female mosquitoes now requiring blood meals. In addition to blood, mosquitoes also rely heavily on plant sap sugars for survival. Contemporary climate change and biological invasions are expanding vector distributions. Thus, increasing disease risk in previously unaffected areas/populations, underscoring the critical need for a deeper understanding of the triad of vector-pathogen-environment interactions. This review addresses this triad and the evolution of this character in dipterans.

43024828.titulo: Variation in the composition of nutrients in the blood of vertebrate hosts affect gonotrophic cycle velocity and the reproductive output of Culex pipiens.
43024828.autores: Yassin MT, El Kholy S, … Seif A (4 autores)
43024828.resumo: Culex pipiens alimentadas em pombo, galinha, camundongo e humano: o sangue aviário tem mais aminoácidos livres e as fêmeas têm ciclo gonotrófico mais curto e desenvolvimento ovariano maior.
43024828.resumo_original: Deep understanding of vector biology is essential for improving disease control strategies. Most female mosquitoes are anautogenous, requiring a blood meal from vertebrate host for egg development. However, the impact of host blood nutritional composition such as red and white blood cell counts, hemoglobin percentage, total protein, and free amino acids on the gonotrophic cycle remains unclear. In this study, female Culex pipiens were allowed to feed on 4 vertebrate hosts (pigeon, chicken, mice, and human), and the nutritional profiles of the blood meals were quantified. Results revealed that avian blood meals contained higher levels of free amino acids compared to mammalian blood. Females fed on avian hosts exhibited a significantly shorter gonotrophic cycle and enhanced ovarian development. These findings suggest that variation in blood nutritional composition may influence reproductive timing in Cx. pipiens and could contribute to host-associated differences in feeding preference.

43061583.titulo: A Standardized Rearing Procedure for Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae): Implications for Laboratory-Based Vector Competence and Control Studies.
43061583.autores: Asgarian TS, Moosa-Kazemi SH, … Sedaghat MM (5 autores)
43061583.resumo: Procedimento padronizado de criação de Ae. aegypti em insectário (Irã): secar o papel de ovos gradualmente por dois dias dá eclosão acima de 90% sem estimulante (r de Pearson -0,818 entre tempo de secagem e eclosão).
43061583.resumo_original:
Aedes aegypti is a major vector of numerous arboviruses, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever. This study aimed to establish a standardized and practical procedure for maintaining and propagating an Ae. aegypti colony under controlled insectary conditions in Bandar Abbas, Iran.
Environmental parameters were routinely monitored. Larvae were reared with an appropriate diet under a regular feeding schedule, while adult mosquitoes were provided with a sucrose solution and blood meals. The correlation between the duration of egg paper drying and the hatching percentage was evaluated. Hatching rates were compared across three media: cooled boiled water, yeast and larval food.
A strong negative correlation was observed between drying duration and hatching percentage, with a Pearson correlation of -0.818 (p< 0.001). Gradual drying of egg papers over a period of two days resulted in a hatching rate of over 90% without any hatching stimulant. No significant differences in hatching rates were found among the three media, as indicated by F= 0.601 (p= 0.578). In a novel observation, female mosquitoes were found to deposit approximately 20-30% of their eggs directly on the water surface inside ovitraps under insectary conditions in Iran.
This study provides a reliable, low-cost model for rearing Ae. aegypti in research insectaries and facilitates future studies on vector control.

resumo_blocos.racional: A confiabilidade dos ensaios de competência vetorial e controle de Aedes aegypti depende de colônias de insetário padronizadas, mas variações no tempo de secagem dos papéis de ovos e nos meios de estímulo à eclosão geram oscilações acentuadas na viabilidade larval.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Em insetário controlado em Bandar Abbas (Irã), parâmetros ambientais foram monitorados continuamente durante a criação larval sob dieta programada e manutenção de adultos com solução de sacarose e repasto sanguíneo. Avaliaram-se a correlação entre a duração da secagem do papel de postura e a porcentagem de eclosão, além da comparação da taxa de eclosão em três meios: água fervida resfriada, levedura e ração larval.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Detectou-se forte correlação negativa entre o tempo de secagem dos papéis de ovos e a taxa de eclosão (Pearson r = -0,818; p < 0,001), com a secagem gradual por dois dias atingindo mais de 90% de eclosão sem necessidade de estimulantes. Não houve diferença significativa entre os três meios de eclosão testados (F = 0,601; p = 0,578), e observou-se que 20% a 30% dos ovos foram depositados diretamente sobre a superfície da água nas ovitrampas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece parâmetros operacionais imediatos para o insetário de Aedes aegypti do LUCHM, validando a secagem gradual de dois dias para eclosão acima de 90% e alertando para a postura direta na água ao quantificar fecundidade em fêmeas submetidas a diferentes dietas.

43009960.titulo: Escalating pyrethroid resistance in Anopheles funestus increases Plasmodium transmission.
43009960.autores: Natchema Soh Fonkou B, Tchouakui M, … Wondji CS (5 autores)
43009960.resumo: Em Anopheles funestus coletados em Camarões, a resistência a piretroides é intensa (33% de mortalidade na dose diagnóstica em Mibellon) e a infecção por esporozoítos é alta (8,8% e 6%); mosquitos mortos por piretroides tipo II estavam mais infectados por Plasmodium que os sobreviventes.
43009960.resumo_original:
The swift rise in pyrethroid resistance among malaria vectors poses a significant challenge to global malaria control. Although vector control tools have advanced, limited understanding of the vectorial capacity of highly pyrethroid-resistant mosquitoes hinders accurate predictions of how new interventions will affect malaria transmission in these resilient populations. Consequently, further research is needed to elucidate how escalating resistance influences mosquito vectorial capacity and shapes malaria transmission dynamics.
Wild Anopheles funestus s.l. mosquitoes were sampled from households in Adamaoua and Centre regions of Cameroon between February and September 2021 using a Prokopack aspirator. Phenotypic resistance to pyrethroids (permethrin, deltamethrin, alphacypermethrin) was assessed using WHO tube bioassays at diagnostic dose (DD), as well as at 5 × and 10 × DD. Plasmodium sporozoite infections were detected using TaqMan and nested PCR assays, and key resistance markers were genotyped by allele-specific PCR. Pearson's chi-squared tests and odds ratio were applied to examine the associations between resistance phenotypes, genotypes, and infection status.
Mosquitoes from Cameroon displayed low mortality rates in Mibellon, with only 33% mortality at the diagnostic dose (DD) and less than 95% mortality at 5 × and 10 × DD. In contrast, Elende populations exhibited lower resistance intensity. Sporozoite infection rates were very high in both collection sites (8.8% and 6% in Mibellon and Elende, respectively). Mosquitoes killed by elevated doses of type II pyrethroids were significantly more infected with Plasmodium than survivors (p < 0.05). Additionally, those surviving the highest deltamethrin doses showed reduced vectorial capacity compared to those surviving the 1 × diagnostic dose (OR = 2.8; 95% CI 1.1-7.3; p = 0.041). The persistence of elevated Plasmodium infection rates in mosquitoes surviving the highest permethrin concentrations underscores the direct impact of pyrethroid resistance escalation in driving malaria transmission. Genotypic analysis identified the L119F-GSTe2 mutation as associated with both resistance escalation and increased Plasmodium transmission whereas an opposite effect was observed for the P450 CYP9K1 with homozygote resistant 454A-CYP9K1 less infected than susceptible.
These findings highlight the urgent need for effective resistance management strategies to combat escalating pyrethroid resistance, while supporting the sustained use of type II pyrethroids, which remain effective against key Plasmodium-transmitting populations.

43010056.titulo: Fitness traits and genetic characterization of a new laboratory colony of Anopheles funestus established in Ifakara, Tanzania.
43010056.autores: Hape EE, Njalambaha RM, … Okumu FO (28 autores)
43010056.resumo: Colônia nova de Anopheles funestus (FUTAZ) estabelecida na Tanzânia: sucesso de acasalamento e tamanho corporal das fêmeas caem de F1 a F6 e se recuperam a partir de F7, igualando a colônia FUMOZ em F9; a fecundidade é similar entre colônias e o acasalamento leva mais de 10 dias para 50% das fêmeas.
43010056.resumo_original:
Anopheles funestus, a major vector of malaria in Africa, has proven difficult to colonize in laboratory settings, impeding research on its biology and control. After several attempts, our team recently succeeded in colonizing a strain of An. funestus from Tanzania (FUTAZ). The objective of this study was to analyze the key fitness and genotypic characteristics of these mosquitoes during multiple filial generations of laboratory adaptation and compare them to wild An. funestus from Tanzania and a pre-existing colony of An. funestus from Mozambique (FUMOZ).
Measures of mating success, body size, fecundity, and insecticide resistance were compared between the newly established FUTAZ colonies, the long-established FUMOZ colonies, and a colony of Anopheles arabiensis maintained in the same laboratory. The maternal lineages of the An. funestus mosquitoes were investigated through a hydrolysis probe analysis of their mitochondrial DNA to identify distinct clades. Other intragenomic variations were examined by D3-RFLP genotyping of 28S ribosomal DNA. These molecular markers were used to compare the FUTAZ colonies, FUMOZ colonies in Tanzania (TZ) and South African (SA) laboratories, and the wild-collected Tanzanian An. funestus.
The mating success and body size of FUTAZ females declined significantly from filial generations F1 to F6 relative to the founder population (F0) then increased from F7 onwards, eventually matching FUMOZ by F9. Fecundity was similar across all colonies tested. However, it took significantly longer for 50% of the females in the FUTAZ and FUMOZ colonies (> 10 days) to mate compared to females in the An. arabiensis colony (~ 5 days). Resistance appeared to be lost during colonization, but this varied with insecticide classes. Majority of FUTAZ mosquitoes, and the wild-caught Tanzanian An. funestus belonged to Clade I (80.4-89.4%) and RFLP type "Y" (90.5-91.4%), while FUMOZ colonies in TZ and SA were mostly Clade II (65.5-88.5%) and RFLP type "MW" (90.5-91.5%).
This study demonstrates that certain fitness traits of An. funestus, notably mating success and body size, declined during the initial phases of laboratory colonization but recovered as the population adapted to laboratory conditions. Having large founder populations is critical to survive these early-generation bottlenecks. Clade-specific and RFLP genotyping confirmed FUTAZ colony as genetically representative of wild-caught Tanzanian An. funestus. This newly established colony constitutes a valuable and reliable resource for malaria vector research.

43008025.titulo: N-terminal integrity governs heptamer assembly and maturation in a mosquito innexin hemichannel.
43008025.autores: Kawaguchi S, Nakano T, … Oshima A (8 autores)
43008025.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
43008025.resumo: Estruturas por crio-ME de uma inexina da malária (AGAP001487) em nanodiscos: heptâmero simétrico com anel N-terminal ordenado; a perda de dois ou mais resíduos N-terminais colapsa o poro e abole a função, e há uma população hexamérica minoritária interpretada como intermediário de montagem.
43008025.resumo_original: Nonchordate gap junction channels are formed by innexins, yet the structures and subunit assembly mechanisms of insect innexins remain unknown. We determined cryoelectron microscopy structures of AGAP001487, an innexin from the malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae, reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs. The wild-type protein forms a rotationally symmetric heptameric hemichannel with an ordered N-terminal ring stabilized by intersubunit hydrogen bonds. Whereas deletion of a single N-terminal residue preserves channel activity, removal of two or more residues markedly impairs function. Consistent with these functional defects, the structure lacking two N-terminal residues exhibits disrupted rotational symmetry, extensive N-terminal disorder, pore collapse, and altered pore-lipid interactions. In addition, two-dimensional class averages revealed a minor population of hexameric particles, consistent with a potential assembly intermediate. Together, these structures support a stepwise assembly pathway in which intersubunit hydrogen bonding stabilizes N-terminal ring formation as a maturation step leading to a fully symmetric heptameric channel. Our findings identify N-terminal integrity as a critical determinant of oligomer maturation and channel function and provide mechanistic insight into how defined oligomeric assemblies are established in large-pore channel families.

10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.titulo: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.autores: Vijayakumar P, Cauwenberghs K, … Su C-Y (7 autores)
10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.resumo: Atlas de partículas extracelulares e vesículas em 352 sensilos olfativos da antena de Drosophila (cerca de 70% do total) por SBF-SEM após criofixação; mais de 7.800 partículas segmentadas separam populações por morfologia, tamanho, densidade eletrônica e classe de sensilo. Corpos multivesiculares e brotamento de membrana em células auxiliares apontam sítios de biogênese; sensilos com neurônios em degeneração têm mais vesículas e partículas.
10.64898/2026.05.30.728996.resumo_original: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis. Together, these findings provide a large-scale ultrastructural characterization of extracellular particles in native sensory tissues and establish a foundation for understanding how extracellular particles are distributed, generated, and function during sensory signaling and degeneration.

43015880.titulo: Optimizing bacterial enrichment procedures to improve mosquito midgut microbiome research
43015880.autores: Schrieke H, Trouche B, … Reveillaud J (5 autores)
43015880.resumo: Comparação de três extrações de DNA em pools de intestino médio de Aedes aegypti: o kit QIAamp Microbiome deu o maior enriquecimento bacteriano e recuperou mais de 85% dos táxons dos outros kits; a filtração a 5 µm reduziu o DNA do hospedeiro, mas também o bacteriano; cada método detectou táxons exclusivos, o que sugere combinar métodos.
43015880.resumo_original: Mosquitoes are major vectors of infectious diseases, with their midgut microbiota playing a crucial role in host development, reproduction, and pathogen interactions. However, characterizing midgut microbial communities remains challenging because host DNA often dominates metagenomic libraries, reducing the resolution of bacterial community profiling and hindering the recovery of microbial genomes. To evaluate strategies for bacterial DNA enrichment in this context, we compared three DNA extraction protocols applied to pooled Aedes aegypti midguts: (i) the QIAGEN DNeasy Blood and Tissue kit without filtration (DNeasy NF), (ii) the same kit preceded by a 5 μm filtration step to reduce eukaryotic material (DNeasy F), and (iii) the QIAGEN QIAamp Microbiome kit, which combines differential host cell lysis and enzymatic DNA depletion. Each method was assessed using qPCR-based quantification of bacterial and host DNA, SSU rRNA-based taxonomic profiling of metagenomic reads, and Metagenome-Assembled Genomes (MAGs) reconstruction using advanced binning approaches. Our results show that while the Microbiome kit provided the highest bacterial enrichment and captured a large fraction (> 85%) of the bacterial taxa detected with the other kits, it yielded a higher relative abundance of Gammaproteobacteria. This occurred without a loss of overall diversity, suggesting improved recovery of microbial taxa rather than a compositional bias. The filtration step associated with the DNeasy kit significantly reduced host DNA but also lowered bacterial material, allowing MAG reconstruction, though less efficiently than the Microbiome kit. Despite this, the DNeasy methods allowed recovering a broader range of bacterial phyla with a more even distribution across taxa, while each extraction method also detected a unique set of NTUs. Overall, a combination of DNA extraction methods may be necessary to optimize microbiome analysis in mosquito midguts, facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of microbial diversity and its potential applications in vector control strategies.

resumo_blocos.racional: O microbioma do intestino médio de Aedes aegypti governa desenvolvimento, ovogênese e competência vetorial, mas o excesso de DNA eucariótico do hospedeiro satura bibliotecas metagenômicas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Comparação sistemática de três protocolos de extração em pools de intestinos médios de Aedes aegypti — DNeasy Blood & Tissue com/sem filtração em 5 μm e QIAamp Microbiome (lise diferencial + depleção enzimática de DNA do hospedeiro) — com qPCR, perfil taxonômico SSU rRNA e reconstrução de MAGs.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O kit QIAamp Microbiome alcançou o maior enriquecimento bacteriano e reconstrução de MAGs preservando >85% dos táxons (com maior recuperação de Gammaproteobacteria sem perda de diversidade global), enquanto os métodos DNeasy recuperaram maior amplitude de filos raros e NTUs exclusivas.

43017112.titulo: Individual variation in food odor sensitivity is related to neuropeptide signaling and starvation in
43017112.autores: Okumura M, Shibukawa Y, … Chihara T (6 autores)
43017112.resumo: Em Drosophila de um mesmo estoque, a sensibilidade a odores de alimento varia entre indivíduos: as sensíveis têm menos triacilglicerol, são mais vulneráveis à inanição e expressam mais um receptor de neuropeptídeo induzido por inanição; alimentar reduz a atração. O transcriptoma aponta genes de quimiossensação e de metabolismo e transporte de lipídios.
43017112.resumo_original: Olfaction is fundamental for animal survival, and individual variation exists in olfactory sensitivity. However, the underlying mechanisms of such variations remain unclear. We classified Drosophila with different olfactory sensitivities toward food-related odors from the same genetic stock using sequential olfactory trap assays. Transcriptome analysis of sensitive and insensitive flies, defined by consistent attraction or non-attraction across three assays, revealed differential expression of genes associated with chemosensation, lipid metabolism, and lipid transport. Flies attracted to food-related odors exhibited lower triacylglycerol levels than non-attracted flies. Sensitive flies also expressed higher levels of sNPF-R, a neuropeptide receptor induced by starvation, despite all flies being exposed to the same starvation stress before the trap assays. Moreover, sensitive flies were more vulnerable to starvation, and feeding decreased their attraction to food-related odors. Together, these findings indicate that individual variation in internal physiological state, particularly starvation level, influences olfactory sensitivity to food-related odors through neuropeptide signaling.

resumo_blocos.racional: Mesmo dentro de estoques geneticamente homogêneos de dípteros, existe ampla variação individual na sensibilidade olfatória a odores alimentares.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Classificação comportamental sequencial em armadilhas olfatórias de Drosophila isogênica seguida de transcriptômica comparativa (RNA-seq), quantificação de triacilgliceróis e ensaios de jejum/realimentação.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Moscas hipersensíveis ao odor apresentaram reservas reduzidas de triacilgliceróis, maior suscetibilidade ao jejum e expressão elevada do receptor neuropeptídico sNPF-R; a alimentação reverteu o fenótipo de atração olfatória.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Neurobiologia, Neuropeptídeos & Eixo Intestino-Cérebro' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente estoques lipídicos (triacilgliceróis em gotículas lipídicas) e sinalização neuropeptídica tipo sNPF/CCHa2 ao comportamento alimentar pós-dieta em insetos.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar se fêmeas de Aedes alimentadas com dieta HFHS apresentam dessensibilização prolongada de busca hospedeira mediada por sNPF-R e acúmulo de TAG.

43019082.titulo: Limitation of pantothenate bioavailability inby second-generation pantazines enhances restriction ofdevelopment
43019082.autores: Debebe Y, Isoe J, … Luckhart S (13 autores)
43019082.resumo: Duas pantazinas de segunda geração (PZ-3022, PZ-3883) reduzem o pantotenato no mosquito, não afetam o crescimento do parasito in vitro e diminuem o número de oocistos no intestino médio e de esporozoítos na glândula salivar de duas espécies de Plasmodium.
43019082.resumo_original:
Plasmodium parasites require pantothenate (Pan) from their hosts to synthesize coenzyme A (CoA), an essential metabolic cofactor. While blood-stage parasites can utilize both Pan and the immediate CoA precursor phosphopantetheine from mammals to synthesize CoA, mosquito-stage parasites rely critically on insect-derived Pan to synthesize CoA. Mosquito host pantothenate kinase (PanK), the rate-limiting enzyme in CoA biosynthesis, is therefore a promising drug target to reduce Pan bioavailability for parasite development. In support, we previously showed that the mammalian PanK activator PZ-2891 restricts Plasmodium yoelii and Plasmodium falciparum development in Anopheles stephensi. Two second-generation pantazines, PZ-3022 and PZ-3883, with improved stability significantly reduced Pan levels in A. stephensi at different time points post-treatment and had no effect on P. falciparum growth in vitro. In infection assays, mosquitoes provisioned with these pantazines exhibited markedly decreased midgut oocyst and salivary gland sporozoite burdens for both parasite species. These findings confirm that pantazines can effectively impair mosquito-stage parasite development and represent promising transmission-blocking small molecules.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-68982-w.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora parasitos sanguíneos de Plasmodium consigam contornar a falta de pantotenato (Pan) utilizando diretamente fosfopanteteína do hospedeiro mamífero para sintetizar coenzima A (CoA), os estágios desenvolvidos no mosquito dependem criticamente do pantotenato derivado do inseto. Ativar farmacologicamente a pantotenato quinase (PanK) do vetor com pantazinas desponta, portanto, como estratégia química seletiva de bloqueio de transmissão.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores testaram duas pantazinas de segunda geração com maior estabilidade metabólica (PZ-3022 e PZ-3883) administradas a fêmeas de Anopheles stephensi, quantificando os níveis teciduais de pantotenato ao longo do tempo pós-tratamento. Em paralelo, conduziram ensaios de crescimento in vitro de Plasmodium falciparum em hemácias e bioensaios de infecção in vivo no mosquito para ambas as espécies Plasmodium yoelii e P. falciparum, contando oocistos no intestino médio e esporozoítos nas glândulas salivares.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Ambos os compostos PZ-3022 e PZ-3883 reduziram significativamente a biodisponibilidade de pantotenato em Anopheles stephensi em múltiplos intervalos pós-tratamento, sem inibir diretamente a proliferação eritrocítica de P. falciparum in vitro. Nos mosquitos alimentados com as pantazinas, houve queda acentuada tanto na carga de oocistos no intestino médio quanto na densidade de esporozoítos na glândula salivar para P. falciparum e P. yoelii.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Abre uma via metabólica experimental limpa para os programas de bloqueio de transmissão e metabolismo do vetor no LUCHM, conectando o eixo de biossíntese de CoA no intestino médio do mosquito à sobrevivência de oocinetos e esporozoítos sem toxicidade direta sobre o estágio sanguíneo.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar se a suplementação de pantotenato ou ativação de PanK em fêmeas de Aedes e Anopheles altera a biogênese de gotículas lipídicas e o perfil de CoA intestinal pós-repasto hiperlipídico (HFHS), medindo viabilidade de oocistos.

43023846.titulo: Accumulation of Polyphosphate Inhibits Biofilm Formation in Mycobacteria by Activating RegX3 to Reduce Intracellular c-di-GMP Levels
43023846.autores: Huang T, Zhen J, … Xie J (6 autores)
43023846.resumo: Em Mycobacterium smegmatis, a falta da exopolifosfatase PPX1 acumula polifosfato e prejudica o biofilme: o polifosfato ativa o fator RegX3, que liga e induz dcpA, derruba o c-di-GMP e desorganiza a síntese de lipídios de parede.
43023846.resumo_original: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can persist in the host for prolonged periods. Biofilm formation represents a key strategy that promotes bacterial persistence, enhances antibiotic resistance, and facilitates immune evasion. Thus, targeting biofilm formation holds significant therapeutic potential for tuberculosis. Exopolyphosphatase 1 (PPX1), highly conserved among mycobacteria, hydrolyzes inorganic polyphosphate. Although changes in polyphosphate levels are known to influence mycobacterial biofilm formation, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. In this study, using a Mycobacterium smegmatis model strain, we found that the level of polyphosphate in the Δppx1 mutant significantly increases, concomitant with impaired biofilm formation. Further investigation revealed that elevated polyphosphate enhances the transcriptional activity of the transcription factor RegX3, which in turn represses biofilm formation. Mechanistically, activated RegX3 directly binds to and upregulates the dcpA gene, encoding a bifunctional enzyme that lowers intracellular cyclic di-GMP levels. This reduction ultimately perturbs cell wall lipid synthesis and compromises biofilm formation. In summary, this work reveals a signaling pathway through which polyphosphate governs biofilm formation in M. smegmatis.

resumo_blocos.racional: O acúmulo intracelular de polifosfato inorgânico (polyP) regula tolerância a estresse e persistência em múltiplos microrganismos, mas os circuitos de transdução bioquímica que ligam cadeias de polyP à remodelagem de superfície celular e formação de biofilmes em micobactérias permaneciam obscuros.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Uso de mutante nocaute da exopolifosfatase 1 (Δppx1) em Mycobacterium smegmatis para promover hiperacúmulo endógeno de polyP, combinado a ensaios de formação de biofilme, análise genética/transcricional do fator RegX3 e do gene dcpA, quantificação de di-GMP cíclico (c-di-GMP) intracelular e caracterização da síntese de lipídios de parede celular.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A deleção de ppx1 elevou acentuadamente o conteúdo de polifosfato inorgânico e inibiu a formação de biofilme micobacteriano. Mecanisticamente, o excesso de polyP ativou o regulador transcricional RegX3, que se ligou diretamente e induziu o gene dcpA (enzima bifuncional que degrada c-di-GMP), derrubando os níveis de c-di-GMP e desorganizando a biossíntese de lipídios da parede celular.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Dialoga diretamente com a tradição histórica do LUCHM/IBCCF em exopolifosfatases (PPX) e homeostase de polifosfato inorgânico, demonstrando um mecanismo inédito pelo qual o polyP atua como segundo mensageiro acoplado à regulação de lipídios de envelope celular.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar se perturbações químicas ou genéticas nos estoques de polifosfato de acidocalcisomos em protozoários ou no intestino de insetos modulam vias lipídicas análogas via sinalização por nucleotídeos cíclicos.

43023858.titulo: Polyphosphate Metabolism and Pyoverdine Production Modulate Zebrafish Survival Following Larval Immersion Exposure to Pseudomonas aeruginosa
43023858.autores: Ortiz-Severín J, Lecaros C, … Chávez FP (6 autores)
43023858.resumo: Em Pseudomonas aeruginosa, deletar ppk1 atenua a virulência em larvas de zebrafish por imersão e deletar ppk2 a aumenta; a proteômica indica que a perda de polyP reduz a pioverdina, e um mutante de pioverdina confirma o efeito.
43023858.resumo_original: Bacterial metabolism is increasingly recognized as a central determinant of bacterial virulence, linking the physiological state of the pathogen to its ability to survive and damage the host. Understanding how bacterial metabolism shapes virulence requires models that are both biologically informative and experimentally accessible. Here, we used zebrafish (Danio rerio) larvae for static immersion assays as a simple model to study Pseudomonas aeruginosa host-pathogen interactions and virulence regulation. Using this approach, we show that disruption of polyphosphate (polyP) synthesis by loss of ppk1 gene (Δppk1) leads to marked attenuation of virulence, whereas interrupting ppk2 gene (Δppk2) results in increased mortality in zebrafish larvae. Phenotypic assays and quantitative proteomics revealed that loss of polyP impairs siderophore production, with minimal effects on other canonical virulence factors. Consistently, a pyoverdine-deficient mutant (ΔpvdF) exhibited reduced virulence in zebrafish, validating the capacity of the zebrafish model to functionally resolve key virulence factors. Together, our results highlight polyphosphate metabolism as a central regulator of P. aeruginosa virulence and position zebrafish immersion assays as an efficient and ethically aligned alternative to mammalian models for studying bacterial pathogenesis.

resumo_blocos.racional: Entender como o metabolismo de reserva de polifosfato inorgânico (sintetizado por PPK1 e PPK2) coordena a produção de fatores de virulência secretados exige modelos animais completos que combinem manipulação genética bacteriana e proteômica quantitativa.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios de imersão estática em larvas de zebrafish (Danio rerio) infectadas com mutantes Δppk1 e Δppk2 de Pseudomonas aeruginosa e mutante deficiente no sideróforo pioverdina (ΔpvdF), integrados a fenotipagem de virulência e proteômica quantitativa diferencial.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A perda de síntese de polifosfato em Δppk1 atenuou fortemente a virulência e mortalidade em zebrafish, enquanto o nocaute Δppk2 elevou a letalidade larval. A proteômica revelou que a depleção de polyP compromete especificamente a produção do sideróforo quelante de ferro pioverdina, sem grandes alterações nos fatores de virulência canônicos — achado validado pelo fenótipo atenuado de ΔpvdF.

43037205.titulo: Phosphorus limitation shifts cellular phosphorus allocation toward polyphosphate by depleting other phosphorus pools in Synechococcus.
43037205.autores: Filella A, Segura-Noguera M, … Duhamel S (6 autores)
43037205.resumo: Em Synechococcus WH8102 em quimiostato, a razão polyP/P particulado total sobe com a limitação de fosfato porque os outros reservatórios de P (RNA, fosfato livre, ATP, fosfolipídios) caem 2,6 a 11,8 vezes; o polyP por biovolume fica estável e os genes do metabolismo de polyP quase não mudam.
43037205.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous and evolutionarily conserved form of phosphorus (P) present in all living organisms, yet its role in cellular and biogeochemical P cycling remains poorly constrained. In P-depleted marine environments, polyP consistently represents a larger fraction of total particulate P (TPP) than in P-replete environments, contradicting its classical role as a luxury storage compound. This unresolved discrepancy has been hypothesized to arise from reductions of other cellular P pools rather than by de novo polyP synthesis, but this has not been tested under steady-state conditions. Using continuous cultures of the globally important marine cyanobacterium Synechococcus sp. WH8102 grown across a gradient of phosphate availability, we address this knowledge gap. Although phosphate availability strongly affected growth rates, single-cell C:N:P stoichiometry and the expression of P-stress genes, polyP:TPP increased with decreasing phosphate availability, reproducing the pattern observed in oligotrophic oceans. This shift was not driven by de novo polyP synthesis; cellular polyP concentrations (polyP per biovolume) remained stable across growth rates (Kruskal-Wallis, P value = 0.06), whereas other intracellular P pools, including RNA, free intracellular phosphate, ATP, and phospholipids, were preferentially depleted with decreasing phosphate availability (2.6-11.8-fold across P pools), increasing the relative contribution of polyP to TPP. Expression of polyP metabolism genes showed minimal changes across treatments. These results indicate that P deficiency responses observed in oligotrophic environments and various microorganisms in batch culture reflect slow-growing physiology resulting in polyP maintenance and preferential depletion of more labile P pools, with consequences for interpreting particulate P stoichiometry and export.

43024619.titulo: GM-CSF and M-CSF driven differentiation differentially regulates Chikungunya virus infection and antiviral responses in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
43024619.autores: Veloz J, Zyulina V, … Fernandez-Sesma A (15 autores)
43024619.resumo: Macrófagos humanos diferenciados com GM-CSF são permissivos a CHIKV e MAYV e sustentam replicação; os diferenciados com M-CSF resistem e produzem mais IFNα e CXCL10. Poli(I:C), mas não R848, reproduz a resposta antiviral, o que aponta o sensor de dsRNA.
43024619.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. The mechanisms driving CHIKV-associated arthralgia is poorly understood, however, macrophages have been implicated as potential reservoirs of persistent viral material and mediators of immunopathology. Granulocyte Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (GM-CSF) and Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (M-CSF) are cytokines that serve as myeloid growth factors that bias macrophages toward pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory phenotypes, respectively. In this study, we examined how cytokine-driven macrophage differentiation via GM-CSF and M-CSF influences susceptibility to and responses against CHIKV infection in vitro. Using parallel donor-matched cultures of primary macrophages, we show that GM-CSF-differentiated macrophages are highly permissive to CHIKV and Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection and support robust viral replication, whereas M-CSF-differentiated macrophages are resistant to CHIKV replication and lack detectable levels of viral protein expression. Despite these differences, we observed pro-inflammatory, M1-skewing of CHIKV-infected macrophages, regardless of differentiation state. Interestingly, we observe higher production of IFNα and IP10/CXCL10 in M-CSF differentiated macrophages, suggesting that M-CSF promotes an antiviral state that restricts CHIKV infection. Stimulation of macrophages with double-stranded RNA (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid; poly(I:C)), but not with single-stranded RNA (resiquimod, R848), recapitulated the antiviral cytokine and chemokine response induced by CHIKV infection. These findings suggest that dsRNA sensing plays a more prominent role than ssRNA sensing in driving the macrophage antiviral response to CHIKV. Together, these findings highlight macrophage differentiation as a critical determinant of CHIKV susceptibility and antiviral immunity in humans, with implications for understanding inflammatory pathogenesis during infection.

43045701.titulo: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
43045701.autores: Tan L, Guo Z, … Li R (9 autores)
43045701.resumo: Com sequenciamento direto de RNA em nanoporo, o Eilat virus (alfavírus restrito a mosquito) produz genomas virais defeituosos por deleção em quantidade muito maior que arbovírus relacionados nas mesmas condições; a terminação prematura na síntese do RNA genômico sugere baixa processividade da replicase, e um subconjunto de DVGs é replicado, empacotado e interfere no vírus parental ao longo de passagens seriadas.
43045701.resumo_original: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS), we profile full-length RNA species of Eilat virus (EILV), a mosquito-restricted alphavirus. We found that EILV produces abundant deletion-type DVGs far exceeding those seen in related arboviruses under identical conditions. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

43046336.titulo: Fitness costs and effects on the peritrophic matrix associated with chitin synthase 2 gene knockout in Vip3Aa-resistant Helicoverpa zea
43046336.autores: Heu CC, Schutze IX, … Fabrick JA (8 autores)
43046336.resumo: Linhagem de Helicoverpa zea com chitina sintase 2 nocauteada por CRISPR/Cas9 (resistência de 29.000 vezes à Vip3Aa) paga custos de aptidão de 27,8% na sobrevivência de neonato a adulto, 23,2% no tempo de desenvolvimento e 17,8% na massa pupal; a matriz peritrófica íntegra, presente na linhagem suscetível e em larvas F1, não aparece nas larvas nocaute.
43046336.resumo_original:
Genetically engineered crops producing insecticidal Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) proteins are used globally to manage key insect pests, including Helicoverpa zea (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). In the United States, H. zea has evolved practical resistance to Bt corn and cotton producing crystalline Bt proteins and early warning of resistance to the vegetative insecticidal protein Vip3Aa has been reported. CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing that introduced disruptive mutations in the H. zea chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene facilitated creation of a strain (CHS2-KO) with 29 000-fold resistance to Vip3Aa relative to its parental susceptible strain, LAB-S. However, quantitative information about fitness costs associated with CHS2-mediated resistance remains limited. Here, we tested whether CHS2-KO exhibited costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass on diet without Vip3Aa, and examined direct effects on the peritrophic matrix (PM).
Relative to LAB-S, fitness costs in CHS2-KO were 27.8% for neonate to adult survival, 23.2% for neonate to adult development time, and 17.8% for pupal mass. An intact PM was evident in LAB-S and F1 larvae, but not in CHS2-KO larvae.
Mutations disrupting the CHS2 gene in the CHS2-KO strain of H. zea were associated with large fitness costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass when reared on diet under laboratory conditions. Also, no intact PM was evident in CHS2-KO. These results suggest that costs could oppose the spread of knockout alleles in the absence of Vip3Aa, although their magnitude on host plants and applicability to less disruptive CHS2 resistance alleles remain to be determined. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry. This article has been contributed to by U.S. Government employees and their work is in the public domain in the USA.

43039935.titulo: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
43039935.autores: Amato C, Graham R, … Wood W (7 autores)
43039935.resumo: Em macrófagos embrionários de Drosophila, corpos apoptóticos engolidos deformam o núcleo e aumentam Lamin B; silenciar Lamin B ou componentes do complexo LINC reduz a captação de corpos apoptóticos in vivo, de modo que a plasticidade nuclear regula a capacidade fagocítica.
43039935.resumo_original: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

43045759.titulo: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET.
43045759.autores: Lisicki E, Taubitz T, … Tacke S (5 autores)
43045759.resumo: Fresagem com plasma-FIB de xenônio em correntes de até 2500 nA, avaliada em mais de 4700 tomogramas (9000 µm³ de lift-out), mantém a integridade da amostra e acelera o preparo de lamelas para crio-ET. Uma rotina escalonada para preparos tipo waffle e lift-outs seriados de tecido permite um experimento completo em 24 h, com ribossomos de levedura em alta resolução.
43045759.resumo_original: Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. To mill thick samples, plasma ion sources are used. However, the practicality of high plasma currents, which offer the greatest potential for increasing throughput, and their possible damaging effects on the sample have not yet been investigated. Here, we systematically examine high-current xenon plasma-FIB (PFIB) milling and quantify the current-dependent damage in over 4700 tomograms by preparing a total lift-out volume of 9000 µm³. We find that currents of up to 2500 nA can be used in cryo-ET lamella preparations, enabling increased milling speeds and sample volumes that can be examined while maintaining sample integrity. We demonstrate this using a newly developed high-throughput staggered milling routine for waffle-like preparations, in which we achieve high-resolution reconstructions of yeast ribosomes, and for tissue serial lift-outs, enabling a complete experiment within 24 hours. Our results and approach provide a strong foundation for future in situ structural investigations of medically relevant protein complexes in organoids, tissues, or entire organisms.

resumo_blocos.racional: A combinação de fresagem por feixe de íons focado criogênico (cryo-FIB) com crio-tomografia eletrônica (cryo-ET) permite observar macromoléculas em contexto nativo, mas o baixo rendimento em amostras espessas e o receio de dano por feixe limitavam o uso de fontes de plasma em altas correntes.

resumo_blocos.resultados: Correntes de até 2.500 nA puderam ser empregadas na preparação de lamelas para cryo-ET acelerando drasticamente a velocidade de fresagem e o volume tecidual inspecionado sem comprometer a integridade ultraestrutural, viabilizando reconstruções de alta resolução de ribossomos e um experimento completo de lift-out seriado de tecido em menos de 24 horas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.

43049932.titulo: Microbial Shifts in Metisa plana (Lepidoptera: Psychidae) Larvae Exposed to Bacillus thuringiensis and Flubendiamide.
43049932.autores: Maidin MST, Hashim AM, … Jamian S (7 autores)
43049932.resumo: Em larvas do bicho-do-cesto da palma (Metisa plana), Bt MPOB Bt1 combinado com flubendiamida aumentou a riqueza microbiana e a densidade da rede de co-ocorrência (0,1354 no DAT0 para 0,2279 no DAT3), com co-ocorrência positiva de Bacillus com Enterobacter e Pseudomonas. Os autores descrevem o estudo como preliminar e dizem que falta análise funcional.
43049932.resumo_original: Microbial communities in the insect body, especially in the gut, are crucial for host development, health, and environmental adaptation. However, little is currently understood about how these communities react to anthropogenic stressors, particularly when pesticides are used. This study aims to investigate the independent and synergistic effects of the biopesticide, Bacillus thuringiensis MPOB Bt1 (MPOB Bt1) and the synthetic diamide insecticide, flubendiamide (Fbd) on the microbial community of the oil palm bagworm, Metisa plana larvae. Larvae were collected at zero (DAT0), one (DAT1), and three days (DAT3) post-treatment and analyzed for bacterial genus abundance and network responses using shotgun metagenomic-derived taxonomic profiling. Analysis of larval microbial community shifts showed that the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment resulted in a significant increase in microbial richness, with network density rising from 0.1354 at DAT0 to 0.2279 at DAT3 compared to the individual Fbd treatment. Pearson correlation analysis also showed that the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment was associated with the growth of the microbiome members that can co-occur with Bacillus. The positive co-occurrence patterns between Bacillus and the genera Enterobacter and Pseudomonas in the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment may reflect treatment-associated microbial shifts during dysbiosis, with their ecological and functional relevance requiring further investigation. This preliminary study provides insights into microbial community responses to the mixture of MPOB Bt1-Fbd compared to the individual treatments. Further functional analysis of the microbial community is needed to clarify the potential roles of these taxa in pathogenicity, treatment response, and pesticide tolerance in the development of M. plana control methods in the future.

43053073.titulo: Identification of vertebrate hosts of mosquito blood meals following the 2017-2018 yellow fever outbreak in São Paulo State.
43053073.autores: Coelho-Rocha E, Fernandes LN, … Lima-Camara TN (15 autores)
43053073.resumo: Em 143 fêmeas ingurgitadas do Parque Estadual Alberto Löfgren (SP), o sequenciamento Nanopore identificou o hospedeiro vertebrado em 74,8% (107/143); 76,6% desses repastos eram humanos e, em Haemagogus leucocelaenus, 94,6% (35/37). O sequenciamento não direcionado recuperou um genoma completo do vírus da febre amarela de um espécime com sangue humano.
43053073.resumo_original:
The 2016-2019 sylvatic yellow fever epidemic in Brazil spread into the peri-urban areas of São Paulo State, raising concerns about the potential resurgence of urban yellow fever transmission in the Americas. In Alberto Löfgren State Park (PEAL), Serra da Cantareira, one of the world's largest urban forests, southern brown howler monkeys became locally extinct in early January 2018 following a short-lived outbreak.
To investigate mosquito feeding patterns during and after the yellow fever outbreak, we collected 5,001 female mosquitoes between December 2017 and March 2020, and screened 143 blood-engorged specimens using Nanopore sequencing.
Vertebrate hosts were identified as the source of blood meals in 74.8% (107/143) of samples, revealing that mosquitoes fed predominantly on mammals (83.2%, 89/107), but also on birds (10.3%, 11/107), and on multiple hosts (6.5%, 7/107). Humans accounted for 76.6% (82/107) of identified blood meals. Other hosts included non-human primate, dog, opossum, mouse and passerine birds. Among Haemagogus leucocelaenus, the primary yellow fever virus (YFV) vector at PEAL, 94.6% (35/37) of blood meals were human-derived, while 5.4% (2/37) contained non-human primate blood. Additionally, two engorged Haemagogus capricornii (100%, 2/2), another YFV vector, fed on humans. Untargeted sequencing recovered a complete YFV genome from an Hg. leucocelaenus specimen with human blood, providing direct evidence of active viral circulation within PEAL.
Sylvatic YFV vectors captured in urban forest fragments of the Serra da Cantareira exhibited marked anthropophilic feeding behaviour. Our findings underscore the risk of mosquito-mediated spillover into densely populated São Paulo, emphasising the urgent need for sustained vaccination together with entomological and virological surveillance to track and respond to yellow fever outbreaks in peri-urban settings.

resumo_blocos.racional: A epidemia silvestre de febre amarela de 2016–2019 atingiu parques periurbanos de São Paulo e extinguiu localmente bugios no Parque Estadual Alberto Löfgren (Serra da Cantareira), levantando a questão crítica de para quais hospedeiros vertebrados os mosquitos vetores redirecionaram seus repastos sanguíneos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Coleta longitudinal de 5.001 fêmeas de mosquitos entre dezembro/2017 e março/2020 no PEAL (São Paulo), com triagem de 143 fêmeas ingurgitadas de sangue e identificação molecular da fonte alimentar vertebrada por sequenciamento Nanopore.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Fontes sanguíneas foram identificadas em 74,8% (107/143) das amostras: mamíferos responderam por 83,2%, sendo humanos 76,6% (82/107) de todos os repastos, seguidos por aves (10,3%) e refeições mistas (6,5%). No vetor primário Haemagogus leucocelaenus, impressionantes 94,6% (35/37) dos repastos eram de origem humana.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Evidência empírica brasileira de alto valor ecológico para o LUCHM: mostra plasticidade alimentar extrema em vetores silvestres após o colapso de primatas não humanos e valida o sequenciamento Nanopore para rastreamento de fontes de repasto sanguíneo.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Aplicar o fluxo de identificação molecular por Nanopore como referência metodológica para caracterizar fontes mistas de sangue e impactos dietéticos em capturas de campo periurbanas no Rio de Janeiro.

43047261.titulo: Dynamics of Drosophila immune stress hematopoiesis assessed by single cell transcriptomics.
43047261.autores: Morin-Poulard I, Liu X, … Crozatier M (8 autores)
43047261.resumo: Atlas de célula única da glândula linfática de Drosophila e do nicho (centro de sinalização posterior) em vários tempos após desafio imune: estados celulares permanentes e transitórios, células em divisão preparadas para virar efetoras, e dois novos participantes na hematopoiese de estresse: via IMD e receptor tipo colecistoquinina.
43047261.resumo_original: The molecular complexity of the hematopoietic microenvironment (niche) and its response to immune stress remain largely unknown. Here, we establish the transcriptional profile of the lymph gland, the Drosophila hematopoietic organ, and its associated niche, the posterior signaling center, at single-cell resolution and at different time points following an immune challenge. Among blood cells, we identify permanent cellular states present with and without stress, but also transient states specific to the immune response, which correspond to dividing cells primed to differentiate into dedicated effector cells. The niche itself is a heterogeneous cell population, and most niche cells undergo dynamic transcriptional remodeling following immune stress. Finally, we identify two new players involved in the hematopoietic stress response: the immune deficiency pathway and the cholecystokinin-like receptor, both of which are expressed in niche cell subsets during immune stress conditions. This molecular atlas of lymph gland cells at different time points after an immune challenge provides new insights into the control of stress hematopoiesis by discrete niche cell subsets.

resumo_blocos.racional: A complexidade molecular do microambiente hematopoiético (nicho) de insetos e sua remodelação dinâmica durante a resposta a estresse imune ainda eram pouco resolvidas em nível de célula única.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Perfilamento transcriptômico por sequenciamento de RNA de célula única (scRNA-seq) da glândula linfática — órgão hematopoiético de Drosophila — e de seu nicho associado (centro de sinalização posterior, PSC) em múltiplos pontos temporais após desafio imune.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identifica estados permanentes de hemócitos presentes com ou sem estresse ao lado de estados transitórios específicos do desafio imune, correspondentes a células em divisão já preparadas para diferenciação em células efetoras dedicadas. Demonstra heterogeneidade e remodelamento transcricional dinâmico na maioria das células do nicho PSC e revela dois novos reguladores expressos em subpopulações do nicho sob estresse imune: a via IMD e o receptor tipo colecistoquinina (CCKR).
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece um atlas de marcadores de subpopulações de hemócitos e sinalização de nicho sob estresse imune altamente relevante para caracterizar subtipos de hemócitos em lepidópteros (Anticarsia/Spodoptera) e conectar a via IMD e receptores tipo CCK ao eixo neuroendócrino intestino-cérebro em insetos.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar marcadores homólogos da via IMD e do receptor tipo colecistoquinina na caracterização de subtipos de hemócitos e resposta ao estresse em insetos do biotério.

43003214.titulo: Geldanamycin and novobiocin induce unique conformational shifts in Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90.
43003214.resumo: Geldanamicina e novobiocina induzem mudanças conformacionais distintas na Hsp90 de Plasmodium falciparum.
43003214.resumo_original: Hsp90 is a molecular chaperone essential for the development of Plasmodium falciparum, the main agent of malaria. The emergence of drug-resistant malaria parasites continues to slow down efforts to control and eliminate the disease effectively. To mitigate antimalarial drug resistance, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends combination therapies. P. falciparum Hsp90 (PfHsp90) is an essential molecular chaperone. In addition, PfHsp90 is a promising antimalarial drug target, and its inhibition has been shown to reverse resistance to otherwise ineffective antimalarial drugs such as chloroquine. As such, understanding the functional features of PfHsp90 remains important for designing effective antimalarial therapies. In the current study, we expressed and purified recombinant PfHsp90 and investigated its interactions with one of its chaperone partners, PfHsp70, and a co-chaperone, PfHop, which brings the two chaperones into a functional complex to facilitate substrate exchange. Furthermore, we combined in silico and biochemical approaches to compare how PfHsp90 interacts with two known small-molecule inhibitors: geldanamycin and novobiocin. We demonstrated that both geldanamycin and novobiocin bind to PfHsp90 with higher apparent affinity than ATP. Furthermore, novobiocin registered a more dramatic conformational shift on PfHsp90 than geldanamycin. In addition, novobiocin more effectively inhibited the following functions of PfHsp90: self-association, co-chaperone (PfHop) binding, and holdase chaperone activity. We discuss the implications of our findings on the role of PfHsp90 and the prospect of this chaperone as an antimalarial drug target.

43007515.titulo: Diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers for pediatric cerebral malaria: a review.
43007515.autores: Drelichowska A, Pikor D, … Paul M (9 autores)
43007515.resumo: Revisão de biomarcadores da malária cerebral pediátrica: PfEMP1–EPCR/ICAM-1, via heme–STING1 (interferon tipo I/CXCL10) e NLRP3–IL-1β, remodelagem juncional e sinalização EphA2 na quebra da barreira, e proteínas neuronais circulantes.
43007515.resumo_original: Pediatric cerebral malaria (PCM) kills 15% to 25% of the African children in whom it is diagnosed and leaves many survivors with neurocognitive deficits. It is a disease of the cerebral microvasculature whose pathogenic sequence is now partly resolved at the molecular level. Plasmodium falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 binds a broad range of endothelial cell receptors, of which binding to the endothelial protein C receptor, in some cases together with intercellular adhesion molecule 1, is the combination linked to severe and cerebral disease. CD36 is the receptor most commonly used by field isolates but is associated with uncomplicated malaria, at least two dozen further receptors have been described for parasitized erythrocytes, and a PfEMP1 binding domain has been identified for only a few of them. The ensuing endothelial activation releases von Willebrand factor and angiopoietin-2 and disables Tie - 2 signaling. Free heme, delivered in part by histidine-rich protein 2 nanoparticles internalized by caveolin-1-dependent endocytosis, is proposed to engage two separable innate arms, one through stimulator of interferon genes 1 (STING1) yielding type I interferon and CXCL10, the other through NLRP3 and caspase - 1 yielding interleukin-1-beta; the first was shown in murine brain endothelium and the second in a human cerebral endothelial cell line, and the two have not been demonstrated in one system. Junctional remodeling and ephrin type-A receptor 2 signaling open the blood-brain barrier in murine models, barrier disruption is documented histologically in human autopsy series, and neuronal and axonal proteins reach the circulation of affected children. The sequence summarized here therefore combines links established in human disease with links that remain experimental or proposed, and the review marks which is which at each step. This review treats candidate biomarkers as readouts of that cascade rather than as free-standing correlates. Because the clinical definition cannot separate malaria-attributable coma from coma with incidental parasitemia, we appraise malarial retinopathy as the in vivo reference standard and set out why a negative result is heterogeneous. Parasite-derived and host-derived markers are mapped onto those steps, with attention to the few evaluated against non-malarial coma rather than against milder malaria, and to what a marker adds at the bedside. Extracellular vesicles and microRNAs are assessed as emerging platforms. We close on druggable nodes in the cascade and on using molecular readouts to stratify children for host-directed therapy.

43013819.titulo: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination
43013819.autores: Tchouatieu AM, Wells TNC, Achan J (3 autores)
43013819.resumo: Revisão da NEJM sobre prevenção da malária (282 milhões de casos e 610 mil mortes em 2024): controle de vetores, intervenções bloqueadoras de transmissão, quimioprevenção, anticorpos monoclonais e vacinas (RTS,S e R21), com ênfase em vigilância orientada e adaptação local.
43013819.resumo_original: Malaria continues to be a major health challenge worldwide, causing an estimated 282 million cases of illness and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly among African children. Despite recent stagnation in the progress of malaria prevention, the landscape is undergoing rapid transformation. This review examines current and emerging approaches to preventing malaria infection and supporting malaria elimination, including vector control, transmission-blocking interventions, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines. Next-generation insecticide-treated nets, expanded use of seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and the introduction of RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are already reshaping control strategies. Looking ahead, long-acting injectable chemoprevention, transmission-blocking medicines and vaccines, and improved surveillance-driven deployment may further accelerate progress. As funding becomes constrained and decision making shifts increasingly to countries where malaria is endemic, effective malaria prevention will depend on locally tailored, integrated combinations of interventions supported by strong surveillance, regulatory capacity, and national leadership.

resumo_blocos.racional: Com 282 milhões de casos e 610 mil óbitos por malária estimados em 2024, urge integrar novas ferramentas profiláticas diante de restrições financeiras e resistência vetorial.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão crítica translacional no NEJM avaliando ensaios clínicos e estratégias de campo para redes impregnadas de nova geração, quimioprevenção sazonal e injetável de longa ação, anticorpos monoclonais e vacinas RTS,S/AS01 e R21/Matrix-M além de intervenções bloqueadoras de transmissão.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Combinações integradas combinando bloqueio pré-eritrocítico (vacinas/mAbs), controle vetorial de nova geração e fármacos bloqueadores de transmissão aceleram a trajetória rumo à eliminação quando ancoradas em vigilância genômica local.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.

43015796.titulo: Role of Anopheles funestus in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal
43015796.autores: Faye MB, Dia AK, … Samb B (12 autores)
43015796.resumo: Em dois distritos do centro do Senegal (2018–2019), An. funestus s.s. foi 73,7% de 6.932 Anopheles; taxa de circunsporozoíto de 0,3% e EIR de 0,008 e 0,038 picadas infectantes por pessoa por noite; só 22,3% de 1.452 fêmeas alimentadas tinham sangue humano.
43015796.resumo_original:
Anopheles funestus is one of the major malaria vectors in sub-Saharan Africa. In Senegal, it is found across nearly all biogeographical areas, often replacing An. gambiae s.l. and sustaining malaria transmission during the dry season. Despite its recognized role as a major vector, the specific contribution of An. funestus to malaria transmission in many malaria-endemic areas remains underexplored. This study aims to assess the contribution of An. funestus in malaria transmission in two health districts in Central Senegal.
Adult mosquitoes were collected from July 2018 to November 2019 in the health districts of Nioro (Ndramé Ndimb) and Ndoffane (Tawa Mboudaye) using Human Landing Catches (HLCs) and Pyrethrum Spray Catches (PSCs). Anopheline specimens were identified morphologically using standard dichotomous keys, with species confirmation performed by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Plasmodium falciparum infection and blood meals sources were determined using Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) techniques.
A total of 6,932 Anopheles mosquitoes were collected. Of these, 73.7% (5,108/6,932) were identified as An. funestus, which was the predominant species at both study sites, with 1,364 specimens collected in Nioro and 3,744 in Ndoffane. Molecular analysis confirmed that An. funestus sensu stricto (s.s) was the only member of the An. funestus group recorded. In Ndramé Ndimb, the mean human biting rate and indoor resting density were 2.8 bites per person per night (b/p/n) and 9.0 females per room (f/r), respectively, compared to 12.4 b/p/n and 19.1 f/r in Tawa Mboudaye. The P. falciparum circumsporozoite rate was 0.3% in both villages, resulting in estimated entomological inoculation rates (EIRs) of 0.008 and 0.038 infected bites per person per night in Ndramé Ndimb and Tawa Mboudaye, respectively. The human blood index was relatively low, with only 22.3% (324/1,452) of An. funestus specimens found to have fed on humans.
This study highlights the predominance of An. funestus and its important role in sustaining residual malaria transmission in central Senegal, even where overall transmission intensity remains low.

43019107.titulo: The prediction of Aedes mosquito abundance using remote sensing and machine learning in Harris County, Texas
43019107.autores: Li H, Zhou J, … Gunter SM (9 autores)
43019107.resumo: Predição da abundância de Aedes por sensoriamento remoto e aprendizado de máquina em Harris County.
43019107.resumo_original:
Vector-borne diseases, particularly those transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, remain a major public health challenge globally, with species like Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus as primary vectors of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. The management of these mosquitoes is complicated by their adaptability to urban environments and the resource limitations of mosquito control programs. This study presents a proof-of-concept approach to improve Aedes surveillance and control by integrating remote sensing data and machine learning techniques. We used Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and environmental data to predict Aedes abundance across Harris County, Texas, incorporating both weather and socioeconomic features into predictive models. Using XGBoost, a machine learning algorithm, we identified high-risk areas for mosquito abundance with increased accuracy over traditional methods. This study demonstrates the potential of combining remote sensing with machine learning for enhancing mosquito surveillance programs, offering an innovative new strategy to improve vector control and mitigate the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. Future research should explore broader geographic applications and additional environmental variables to further refine predictive models.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-64249-6.

43022950.titulo: A climate-driven mechanistic transmission model to characterize dengue epidemiology in Dhaka, Bangladesh
43022950.autores: Paul KK, Regan DG, … Gray RT (5 autores)
43022950.resumo: Modelo mecanístico de transmissão de dengue dirigido pelo clima em Dhaka.
43022950.resumo_original: Dengue is a major public health concern in tropical and sub-tropical areas of the world. Dengue virus is transmitted to humans primarily by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and its epidemiology is heavily influenced by the climate. We developed a mechanistic compartmental model to characterize how climate and the evolution of population-level immunity influence changes in the epidemiology of dengue. The model explicitly incorporates aquatic and adult stages of the mosquito vector and cross-immunity (to another serotype) to better represent the transmission of dengue compared to previous models. It incorporates parameters related to mosquito development, behaviour, and mortality that are dependent on temperature, rainfall, and humidity. We calibrated the model to available dengue seroprevalence estimates for Dhaka, Bangladesh as it is a well-observed densely populated endemic area for dengue and will be strongly impacted by climate change. We then simulated dengue epidemiology for the period of 1995-2014 and compared the simulation output with available epidemiologic data. The model produced repeating annual outbreaks of dengue with strong seasonality, as observed in the dengue case reports for Dhaka. The median number of annual dengue infections produced by the model was 1.6 million (IQR: 0.6-2.3 million) and the median of the annual daily peak size of dengue infections was 24,121 (IQR: 7,807-39,308) across the simulations. These figures while exceeding reported cases in Dhaka, which do not include asymptomatic infections or cases not seeking healthcare, align with previous estimates. The modelled seroprevalence of 62% (IQR: 58-75%) aligned with survey results from Dhaka. In most model simulations, dengue infections occurred during August to December with the median peak occurring in October. The model outputs demonstrated a high degree of conformity to the reported data in terms of seasonality, and seroprevalence, indicating that the model provides a good representation of overall dengue epidemiology in Dhaka. By accounting for climate variables, host immunity, and their interplay, our model is well-suited for evaluating the long-term impact of climate change on dengue transmission in Dhaka and other settings where climate and epidemiological data are available.

10.64898/2026.11.13.763891.titulo: Parasite-induced ER-PVM contacts promote CERT-dependent ceramide delivery to the apicomplexan vacuole
10.64898/2026.11.13.763891.resumo: Preprint: contatos RE-membrana do vacúolo parasitóforo induzidos pelo parasito promovem entrega de ceramida dependente de CERT ao apicomplexo. Só título lido.
10.64898/2026.11.13.763891.resumo_original: Apicomplexan parasites rely on host lipids for replication, yet how host transport machinery is coupled to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) remains unresolved. Here, we uncover a host-parasite membrane contact site mechanism driving ceramide delivery to the vacuole. Host ceramide transfer protein (CERT) targets the PVM via its PH domain, cooperating with host VAP-B to promote sphingolipid accumulation and support Toxoplasma and Plasmodium development. By combining VAP-B proximity labeling with FFAT motif predictions, we identified TgVPS13 as a parasite-encoded FFAT effector that physically engages host VAP-B at the host-parasite interface. Conditional depletion of TgVPS13 markedly reduces vacuolar sphingolipid enrichment, partially impairs host CERT recruitment at the PVM, disrupts intravacuolar parasite organization, and severely restricts replication. Together, these findings establish a model in which TgVPS13-VAP-B tethering creates ER-PVM proximity, organizing a functional contact site that optimizes CERT-mediated ceramide transfer for efficient host lipid acquisition.

43031333.titulo: No cross-resistance to cry toxins and strong fitness costs associated with Vip3Aa resistance in a chitin synthase knockout strain of Helicoverpa armigera.
43031333.autores: Zhang M, Liu C, … He YZ (7 autores)
43031333.resumo: Helicoverpa armigera com CHS2 nocauteado resiste >2852 vezes a Vip3Aa, sem resistência cruzada a Cry1Ac/Cry2Ab e com custo de aptidão claro em dieta e em planta.
43031333.resumo_original:
Genetically modified crops expressing insecticidal proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) are widely planted to suppress pest populations, but the emergence of resistance in pests threatens their durability. The evolution of resistance is strongly shaped by cross-resistance patterns and associated fitness costs. Recent studies have linked loss-of-function mutations in the chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene with resistance to Vip3Aa in several lepidopteran pests, including the cotton bollworm Helicoverpa armigera. However, whether disruption of CHS2 confers cross-resistance to Cry toxins and imposes fitness costs in H. armigera remains unknown. Here, we examined the cross-resistance profile of a Vip3Aa-resistant H. armigera strain with CHS2 knocked out (CHS2-KO) and assessed its fitness costs when reared on wheat germ diet, cotton leaves, and corn ears lacking Vip3Aa.
The CHS2-KO strain exhibited >2852-fold recessive resistance to Vip3Aa but had no cross-resistance to Cry1Ac or Cry2Ab. When maintained on wheat germ diet without Vip3Aa, CHS2-KO had delayed development and lower larval survival, lower pupal weight, and reduced adult fecundity relative to the susceptible parental strain SCD. Survival of CHS2-KO larvae was 1% after 7 days on cotton leaves and 2% after 5 days on corn ears, indicating marked fitness costs. No peritrophic matrix was found in the midguts of CHS2-KO larvae. Midgut transcriptome profiling of CHS2-KO larvae revealed upregulation of transcripts involved in protein digestion, cellular absorption, and immune responses with a corresponding decline in transcripts involved in metabolism.
Vip3Aa resistance in H. armigera mediated by loss-of-function mutations in CHS2 is inherited as a recessive trait, lacks cross-resistance to Cry toxins, and incurs strong fitness costs. These findings suggest that complete loss of CHS2, as seen in the CHS2-KO strain, may be negatively selected in the absence of Vip3Aa. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

43043975.titulo: Robust CD8 T-cell response generated via attenuated Plasmodium sporozoite prime and multi-epitope mRNA vaccine boost
43043975.autores: Arumugam S, Hassert M, … Harty JT (4 autores)
43043975.resumo: Camundongos CB6F1 recebem dose única subprotetora de esporozoítos de P. berghei atenuados (por genética ou radiação) para gerar células T de memória residentes no fígado e circulantes, seguida de reforço com vacina de mRNA em nanopartícula lipídica que codifica epítopos CD8 de proteínas do estágio hepático.
43043975.resumo_original: Plasmodium infections and subsequent malaria disease remain a global health scourge. Liver-resident and circulating memory CD8 T cells elicited by whole parasite vaccines such as genetically or radiation-attenuated sporozoites can provide potent immunity to Plasmodium infection and prevent the development of the symptomatic blood stage of infection in humans, nonhuman primates, and mice. However, this requires multiple, large doses of attenuated sporozoites, posing numerous logistical challenges. To partially address these logistical challenges, here, we prime CB6F1 mice with a human weight-normalized, subprotective single dose of genetically or radiation-attenuated Plasmodium berghei sporozoites to elicit liver-resident and circulating memory T cells prior to boosting with a novel lipid nanoparticle mRNA vaccine encoding multiple CD8 T-cell epitopes from liver-stage proteins. We show that boosting primed mice with this mRNA vaccine engenders sterilizing immunity against sporozoite challenge by generating a robust liver-stage-specific CD8 T-cell response when administered intravascularly or intramuscularly. Thus, combining a single, dose-sparing attenuated sporozoite immunization with a multi-epitope translationally relevant mRNA vaccine can engender protective immunity against P. berghei sporozoite challenge via the generation of a potent circulating and resident memory liver CD8 T-cell response. Minimizing the number of attenuated sporozoite doses required to prime CD8 T cells with a full complement of liver-stage malaria-specific epitopes effectively mitigates some logistical challenges associated with attenuated sporozoite vaccination.
