10.64898/2026.11.16.766917.titulo: Synergistic mechanistic and deep learning approaches for modeling insect thermal responses and geographic distributions
10.64898/2026.11.16.766917.autores: Vanalli C, van Tiel N, … Tuia D (6 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.16.766917.resumo: Preprint não revisado por pares que combina abordagem mecanística e aprendizado profundo para modelar respostas térmicas e distribuições geográficas de insetos (Aedes aegypti e albopictus, Helicoverpa, Spodoptera). Sem abstract na captura: avaliado pelo título.
10.64898/2026.11.16.766917.resumo_original: Aim The Hutchinsonian shortfall, the lack of knowledge about species' abiotic tolerance, limits our understanding of species responses to environmental change and consequently also the outlining of their distribution in space and time. Such environmental tolerance is commonly inferred with two distinct approaches: i) trait performance studies, which use lab experiments to model species' functional responses, often overlooking real-world complexity, and ii) species distribution models, which infer environmental suitability from occurrence data, but offer limited causal insights. In this paper, we argue that these two strategies bring complementary information that can be integrated to estimate species-environment relationships more robustly and accurately map species distributions. Location Global scale Time period 2000-2019 Major taxa studied Given their exceptional diversity and climatic sensitivity, insects provide a powerful system for studying these responses. We selected key insect species representing i) disease vectors: the yellow fever (Aedes aegypti) and Asian tiger (Aedes albopictus) mosquitoes; ii) agricultural pests: the cotton bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) and the fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda); and iii) biocontrol agents: the green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea) and the 14-spotted ladybug (Propylea quatuordecimpunctata). Methods We compared predicted insect thermal suitability and distributions derived from two complementary methodological approaches: mechanistic models based on experimentally derived thermal responses of ecological rates, and deep learning-based species distribution models based on occurrence data. We further tested hybrid frameworks integrating mechanistic and correlational information through model ensembling, mechanistic regularization, and mechanistically informed deep learning. We assessed the efficacy of these methods under increasing data scarcity by progressively removing up to 80% of species occurrence records using three strategies: removal from the warmest or coldest parts of species' thermal ranges, removal from the least-sampled locations based on geographic sampling bias, and random removal as a baseline. Results Our findings highlight that occurrence-derived thermal suitability closely reproduces the observed distributions of insects. Compared to the mechanistic estimates, these thermal response curves are consistently shifted towards lower temperatures, potentially reflecting niche underfilling. However, when challenged with progressive data removal, correlative methods fail to extrapolate reliably in data-deficient regimes, where mechanistic knowledge becomes increasingly more crucial. Hybrid approaches in turn leveraged complementary information, improving predictive performance and reducing the sensitivity of environmental suitability estimates to sampling biases. Main conclusions Ultimately, we show how the synergistic integration of experimental ecology with observational biogeography can lead to more accurate and ecologically robust predictions for species distributions and their environmental responses to climatic changes.

43044838.titulo: Modelling modified insect release interventions for malaria control: a scoping review and thematic comparison with dengue
43044838.autores: Lakshminarayanan P, Tiley K, … Brady O (7 autores)
43044838.resumo: Revisão de escopo de 110 estudos de modelos de liberação de insetos modificados (Wolbachia) para malária, comparados a modelos de dengue em Aedes aegypti e a modelos de gene drive em Anopheles; entre as lacunas, efeitos de aptidão dependentes de contexto raramente entram (muitos assumem alta transmissão materna e incompatibilidade citoplasmática) e a heterogeneidade espacial é pouco modelada.
43044838.resumo_original: Wolbachia is a promising new intervention for malaria control. While modelling has supported Wolbachia deployment for dengue control, its application in Anopheles is still emerging. We systematically reviewed dynamic transmission models of Wolbachia-based modified insect releases for malaria using PubMed and Embase. Evidence was compared primarily with Wolbachia-based dengue models from a parallel Wolbachia-Aedes aegypti scoping review and secondarily with gene drive-based Anopheles models identified through a separate systematic search. Across 110 included studies, three major gaps were identified. First, context-dependent fitness effects are rarely incorporated, with many models assuming high maternal transmission (MT) and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), limiting assessment of how environmental variability influences persistence. Second, spatial heterogeneity is infrequently modelled despite evidence that mosquito movement shapes Wolbachia spread. Third, few studies embed Wolbachia dynamics within integrated malaria transmission models, preventing estimation of epidemiological impact to assess Wolbachia's role in malaria control and elimination. Lessons from Wolbachia-based dengue control and parallel developments in gene drive provide an established framework, with actionable pathways for advancement. Addressing these priorities will be essential to guide safe, effective and scalable implementation of Wolbachia as a new malaria control intervention.

43053179.titulo: An actionable field practice integrated with real-time quantitative vector surveillance for precision intervention during the 2025 Chikungunya outbreak in Foshan.
43053179.autores: Guo X, Chen H, … Chen XG (23 autores)
43053179.resumo: Prática de campo integrada a vigilância quantitativa de vetores em tempo real para intervenção de precisão (Parasites & Vectors). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43053179.resumo_original: Following the activation of Level III emergency response, China's grassroots public health systems, exemplified by initiatives like the Patriotic Health Campaign and community-based prevention networks, can be rapidly mobilized. To enhance precision in controlling China's first large-scale chikungunya fever outbreak in Shunde, Foshan, Guangdong Province, real-time quantitative surveillance was implemented. Real-time quantitative surveillance was conducted using MS400 traps and Intelligent Mosquito Ovitraps (IMTs) to monitor Aedes mosquito populations. These tools established a rapid monitoring network in Foshan, enabling daily data reporting with high spatiotemporal resolution. During comprehensive and targeted vector control phases, real-time data from MS-400 and IMT informed adaptive adjustments in local control strategies, optimizing resource allocation and intervention timing. This integrated field practice combining advanced surveillance technologies with community mobilization validates a scalable framework for precision Aedes-borne disease control, yielding actionable insights into mitigating emerging arboviral threats in resource-limited settings.

43059454.titulo: Detection of dengue virus in Aedes albopictus following imported dengue cases and absence of detections after vector control, Ticino Canton, Switzerland, August to September 2026.
43059454.autores: Zezza-Torriani G, Nobile A, … Guidi V (15 autores)
43059454.revista: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin
43059454.resumo: Detecção de DENV em Ae. albopictus após casos importados e ausência de detecção depois do controle (Euro Surveill); vigilância entomológica ativa.
43059454.resumo_original: After three dengue cases following exposure in Italy were identified in southern Switzerland, reactive entomological surveillance around cases' residence detected a dengue virus (DENV)-positive Aedes albopictus mosquito pool. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed close genetic relationship between viruses from one case and the mosquitoes. Emergency vector control measures (100-m radius) were rapidly implemented according to the cantonal response plan. Follow-up surveillance did not detect any additional DENV-positive pools, highlighting the value of integrated clinical and entomological surveillance for mitigating local transmission risk.

43046041.titulo: S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation in subarachnoid hemorrhage.
43046041.autores: Zhang L, Pang J, … Jiang Y (13 autores)
43046041.resumo: Após hemorragia subaracnóidea, astrócitos passam a glicólise aumentada via S1P1 (mTOR/HIF1α); o lactato acumulado eleva H3K9la, ativa a transcrição de MFF e causa fissão e disfunção mitocondrial.
43046041.resumo_original:
Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central event in the pathophysiology of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that mitochondrial function is vulnerable to metabolic alterations. While the role of neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction in SAH pathology is firmly established, less is known about mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes, the key regulators of brain homeostasis, especially its potential regulation by metabolic reprogramming after SAH. Hence, we aimed to define the metabolic reprogramming and its potential role in mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes post SAH.
We established in vivo and in vitro models of SAH. Glucose uptake, lactate production, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) measurement were employed to profile the metabolic alterations in astrocytes after SAH. ATP level, mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, oxygen consumption rate (OCR), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were applied to assess the structural and functional integrity of astrocytic mitochondria. Lentivirus carrying short hairpin RNA (shRNA) and adeno-associated virus (AAV) were used to knockdown sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1P1) to explore the role of S1P1 in astrocytic metabolism switch. Additionally, ChIP-qPCR was utilized to elucidate the epigenetic mechanism of S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming in regulating the mitochondrial function of astrocytes post SAH.
We provided new evidence that astrocytes underwent metabolic switch with enhanced glycolysis in the early stage of SAH which was mediated by S1P1 through mammalian target of rapamycin/hypoxia-inducible factor 1ɑ (mTOR/HIF1ɑ) activation. Notably, enhanced glycolysis-derived lactate accumulation in astrocytes promoted mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, we found that the enhanced glycolysis facilitated mitochondrial fission factor (MFF) transcription by elevated H3K9la, resulting in excessive mitochondrial fission and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction in the early stage of SAH.
Our findings demonstrate that S1P1-driven glycolysis enhancement promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation and provide a potential therapeutic strategy for SAH.

43009996.titulo: Resistance selection and biological performance of Aedes aegypti following laboratory spinosad exposure.
43009996.autores: Rique HL, Menezes HSG, … Silva-Filha MHNL (5 autores)
43009996.resumo: Aedes aegypti de Recife selecionado por 20 gerações com espinosade: razão de resistência de 9,7 (CL50) e 8,5 (CL90), com avaliação de custo de aptidão (repasto, fecundidade, fertilidade, longevidade).
43009996.resumo_original:
Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of arboviruses of major public health importance which are spreading worldwide. Spinosad has been an important compound adopted for Ae. aegypti management, with selective larvicidal action based on the metabolites produced by the bacterium Saccharopolyspora spinosa. The expanding use of spinosad in mosquito control programs highlights the need for monitoring the potential development of resistance. This study evaluated the effects of continuous laboratory selection of an Ae. aegypti field-derived colony with spinosad, focusing on resistance development, cross-resistance patterns, and biological performance.
Ae. aegypti field sample from Recife city, Brazil, was used to establish the RecCam colony and the RecSpi strain. This strain was subjected to artificial selection with spinosad under controlled laboratory conditions for 20 generations, while RecCam was used as a reference colony for the study. Larvae susceptibility to spinosad and to other three larvicides, not used in selection process, was determined by in vivo assays. The biological fitness of RecSpi individuals was evaluated and compared to RecCam based on blood-feeding performance, fecundity, fertility, pre-imaginal development, adult production, and longevity assays.
The baseline susceptibility of the RecCam larvae to spinosad (LC₅₀ = 0.222 mg/L and LC₉₀ = 0.383 mg/L) was similar to another local reference colony (RecLab), while the Rockefeller colony exhibited the highest susceptibility (LC₅₀ = 0.160 mg/L, LC₉₀ = 0.265 mg/L). After 20 generations of spinosad selection, RecSpi larvae displayed a 9.7- and 8.5-fold resistance ratio at LC₅₀ (2.146 mg/L) and LC₉₀, (3.240 mg/L), compared to the RecCam reference, respectively. Notably, no cross-resistance was observed against Bacillus thuringiensis svar. israelensis (Bti), a combined larvicide based on Lysinibacillus sphaericus/Bti, or temephos. The RecSpi individuals displayed reduced biological performance characterized by prolonged larval development, reduced adult emergence, decreased adult longevity, and lowered blood intake compared to the RecCam strain.
Continuous selection with spinosad promoted resistance in Ae. aegypti RecSpi strain accompanied by a reduced biological performance. The absence of cross-resistance to commonly used larvicides underscores the unique spinosad mode of action and supports its use in rotation strategies. To maintain the efficacy of spinosad, resistance management approaches including rotational use and longitudinal susceptibility monitoring are necessary.

43015419.titulo: Strain-Specific Reduction of Ndel1 Enzymatic Activity During Early Zika Virus Infection in the Neonatal Brain
43015419.autores: de Farias IS, Ximenes AP, … Hayashi MAF (9 autores)
43015419.resumo: A atividade enzimática de Ndel1 cai em cérebro neonatal infectado por ZIKV de forma dependente da linhagem viral, e não como resposta conservada do hospedeiro.
43015419.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during early development is associated with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including congenital microcephaly, yet the molecular mechanisms linking viral exposure to neuronal dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Ndel1 (nudE neurodevelopment protein 1 like 1) is an oligopeptidase critically involved in neuronal migration, neurite outgrowth, and cytoskeletal dynamics, processes essential for proper brain development. Building on previous observations that Ndel1 enzymatic activity is reduced in ZIKV-infected embryonic and neonatal brains, we investigated whether this modulation represents a conserved host response or a strain-specific molecular effect. Using a neonatal intracerebroventricular infection model in Swiss mice at postnatal day 0, we compared the effects of a Brazilian ZIKV strain (ZIKVBR), an African lineage strain (ZIKVAF), and dengue virus (DENV) on Ndel1 regulation in the brain. We found that Ndel1 enzymatic activity was significantly reduced at early post-infection time points (P3 and P7) exclusively in ZIKVBR-infected animals, whereas ZIKVAF and DENV did not alter enzyme activity relative to controls. Notably, at the earliest timepoint (P3), this reduction occurred in the absence of changes in Ndel1 mRNA expression, indicating an initial post-transcriptional or functional mechanism of regulation, although Ndel1 mRNA expression was also significantly reduced by P7. Although both ZIKV strains induced robust inflammatory gene expression, only ZIKVBR infection resulted in decreased Ndel1 activity, dissociating neuroinflammatory signaling from enzymatic modulation. Importantly, this strain-specific reduction parallels the unique capacity of ZIKVBR to induce microcephaly and supports Ndel1 dysfunction as an early molecular event associated with neurodevelopmental impairment. Together, these findings identify a virus- and strain-specific regulation of a key neuronal enzyme and provide mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of ZIKVBR-associated neurodevelopmental outcomes.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a infecção congênita por vírus Zika (ZIKV) cause microcefalia grave ao perturbar migração neuronal e citoesqueleto, permanecia incerto se a queda descrita na atividade da oligopeptidase neurodesenvolvimental Ndel1 no cérebro neonatal refletia uma resposta inflamatória inespecífica do hospedeiro ou um efeito dependente da linhagem viral.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Modelo de infecção intracerebroventricular neonatal em camundongos Swiss no dia pós-natal P0 comparando diretamente três grupos virais frente a controles: uma linhagem brasileira associada a microcefalia (ZIKVBR), uma linhagem africana (ZIKVAF) e vírus Dengue (DENV). Os cérebros foram coletados precocemente em P3 e P7 para ensaios fluorimétricos/enzimáticos de atividade de Ndel1, RT-qPCR de transcritos de Ndel1 e perfilamento de citocinas neuroinflamatórias.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A atividade enzimática de Ndel1 caiu significativamente em P3 e P7 exclusivamente nos animais infectados pela linhagem brasileira ZIKVBR, enquanto ZIKVAF e DENV não alteraram a função da enzima. Notavelmente, em P3 a queda catalítica ocorreu sem redução nos níveis de mRNA de Ndel1 — evidenciando modulação pós-transcricional precoce anterior à queda transcricional vista em P7 — e mesmo quando ambas as cepas de ZIKV dispararam neuroinflamação robusta.

43004473.titulo: Histone lactylation encodes innate immune memory in atherosclerosis: a hypothesis of epigenetic bookmarking for residual inflammatory risk.
43004473.autores: Yang H, Zhang Y, … Jian W (6 autores)
43004473.resumo: Hipótese de que a lactilação de H3K18 (lactato–p300) funciona como código de memória epigenética em imunidade treinada, ligando glicólise sustentada a responsividade persistente; contexto: risco inflamatório residual em aterosclerose.
43004473.resumo_original: Histone lactylation, particularly H3K18 lactylation (H3K18la), has emerged as a lactate-derived epigenetic modification that links metabolic reprogramming to sustained chromatin states. Here, we advance a hypothesis that the lactate-p300-H3K18la axis functions as an epigenetic memory code, converting transient glycolytic signals into persistent transcriptional responsiveness in innate immune cells-a mechanism we term "context-dependent lactylation memory." We integrate evidence from three converging domains: the persistence of lactylation at trained immune loci, the requirement of H3K18la for trained immunity demonstrated in recent BCG vaccination studies, and the hypoxic, glycolytic microenvironment of the atherosclerotic plaque. We propose that cardiovascular risk factors stabilize HIF-1α, which drives glycolytic reprogramming and sustained lactate production. Lactate-derived lactyl-CoA then serves as a substrate for p300/CBP-mediated H3K18la deposition at immune gene regulatory elements, creating a poised chromatin state that sustains innate immune hyperresponsiveness. This cascade provides a mechanistic explanation for residual inflammatory risk, the observation that elevated cardiovascular events persist despite optimal lipid-lowering therapy. The framework is constrained by the context-dependent duality of lactylation, whereby cell type, lysine site, and metabolic flux direction jointly determine whether the modification drives pro-inflammatory or reparative outcomes. We delineate testable predictions that define a roadmap for empirical validation or refutation of the lactate-lactylation memory hypothesis in human CHD.

43061389.titulo: NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 contributes to sleep regulation in Drosophila.
43061389.autores: Ishikawa T, Nitta Y, … Masuda S (11 autores)
43061389.resumo: 🎲 [exploração] A atividade de NADPH fosfatase de Mesh1 (resíduo W138) regula sono em Drosophila.
43061389.resumo_original: Metazoans possess Mesh1, an enzyme with both ppGpp hydrolase and NADPH phosphatase activities, raising questions about their respective physiological roles. To distinguish these functions, we combined biochemical characterization, structure-guided mutagenesis, genome editing, and behavioral analysis in Drosophila. We found that Drosophila Mesh1 dephosphorylates NADPH but not NADP+ in vitro. Substitution of tryptophan 138 with phenylalanine (W138F) abolished detectable NADPH phosphatase activity while retaining detectable but severely reduced ppGpp hydrolase activity. Flies carrying the W138F mutation exhibited reduced total sleep duration and increased sleep fragmentation. These findings implicate the NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 in sleep regulation and identify W138 as a critical residue for this function. Our results highlight a physiological role for Mesh1 beyond ppGpp metabolism and suggest a connection between NADPH metabolism and the regulation of sleep in metazoans.

43024008.titulo: Inflammation-driven epigenetic memory in infertility and chronic endometritis.
43024008.autores: Chen R, Diao L, … Arck PC (4 autores)
43024008.resumo: Revisão de memória epigenética inflamatória na endometrite crônica, em células imunes e não imunes.
43024008.resumo_original: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent, low-grade inflammatory condition of the endometrium, typically caused by microbial infections. CE is often asymptomatic, leading to frequent underdiagnosis. It is frequently identified during the assessment of causes for infertility. Even after resolving the infectious etiology by antibiotic treatment, infertility persists in a number of patients. Emerging evidence from chronic inflammatory diseases affecting epithelial tissues, e.g., in the gut, suggests that inflammatory conditions can induce long-lasting epigenetic changes, e.g., in innate immune cells. Notably, tissues outside the immune system can also retain memory of inflammatory events and environmental insults via epigenetic modifications. This review summarizes how epigenetic changes can affect endometrial function, drawing on current knowledge of CE. It also discusses how inflammation prompts these changes. We propose that persistent epigenetic memory in both immune and non-immune endometrial cells plays a crucial role in sustaining CE-associated adversities, such as infertility. Future research should focus on pinpointing specific epigenetic patterns in CE and exploring how inflammation-induced memory leads to cellular dysfunction in the endometrium. Understanding these mechanisms will advance CE diagnosis and open doors to new treatment options for infertility, focusing on reversing the inflammatory memory retained upon treatment of CE.

43041090.titulo: Development of a model of tick-borne encephalitis virus transmission from experimentally infected bank voles to Ixodes ricinus ticks
43041090.autores: Sick F, Răileanu C, … Wernike K (5 autores)
43041090.resumo: Os autores tentam estabelecer em laboratório um modelo de transmissão do vírus da encefalite transmitida por carrapato do reservatório (arganaz infectado) para Ixodes ricinus, simulando a infecção por alimentação em animal virêmico, o co-feeding e a transmissão transestadial.
43041090.resumo_original: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is an important arbovirus in Europe. TBEV is transmitted mainly by ticks of the Ixodes ricinus (Ixodes ricinus-Ixodes persulcatus) species complex and causes infections of the central nervous system, making it one of the most important viral tick-borne diseases of humans in Europe. The natural transmission cycle relies on a complex interplay of arthropod vector and mammalian host factors. Besides the infection of ticks by feeding on viremic animals and co-feeding, transstadial transmission of the virus within the tick is also essential for further TBEV transmission to the next vertebrate host during the subsequent bloodmeal. In this study, we attempted to establish a mammalian host-tick transmission model for the simulation of the natural transmission under controlled laboratory conditions in order to study virus transmission from the reservoir host bank vole (Myodes glareolus) to I. ricinus larvae and to evaluate transstadial transmission of TBEV when engorged larvae moult into nymphs. We demonstrated acquisition of TBEV by larval ticks that blood fed on TBEV-infected viremic bank voles, although the TBEV infection prevalence of the engorged larvae was low (9.3%). Fully and partially engorged larvae were collected and further kept in the insectary and were allowed to moult into nymphs to assess transstadial virus transmission. No transstadial virus transmission was observed, as all nymphs tested negative by real-time RT-PCR. Although no general conclusions on transstadial transmission could be drawn yet, the establishment of this model forms a basis for future research.

43057552.titulo: Entomological survey for potential Anopheles malaria vectors and their insecticide resistance status in agricultural and peri-urban sites of Central and Southern Greece.
43057552.autores: Balaska S, Parnassa V, … Kioulos I (10 autores)
43057552.resumo: Levantamento entomológico de vetores Anopheles e status de resistência a inseticida em área agrícola.
43057552.resumo_original: Greece has eliminated malaria for several decades now, however the ecological settings as being transformed in response to climatic crisis and the current geo-political situation may pose an epidemiological risk. Evidence on Anopheles vector species occurrence and their insecticide resistance (IR) profile in the country is limited and this study aims to narrow this gap. To this end, Anopheles collections were performed in selected agricultural and peri-urban sites throughout Greece, during 2021-2024. Α sub-set of the populations was assessed for their response to insecticides commonly used in the country, showing evidence of resistance to deltamethrin in Corinthia and Boeotia, and possible resistance for the Phthiotis collection, based on CDC guidelines, while all the characterized populations showed a tendency towards susceptibility to the bacterial larvicide Bti (WHO larval bioassays). A multi-locus DNA barcoding approach identified totally five Anopheles species, with distinct abundances and distribution patterns, including epidemiologically relevant malaria vectors, such as An. sacharovi, Αn. labranchiae and An. claviger. In parallel, monitoring of common pyrethroid resistance-associated mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene revealed the exclusive presence of the wild-type allele L1014. Lastly, a Plasmodium parasite detection assay was applied in the adult Anopheles specimens from Phthiotis producing negative results. In all, our survey updates the Anopheles species distribution map of central and southern Greece and provides valuable evidence on populations' IR status, to support future vector control targeted initiatives. The presence of malaria competent vector species, along with sporadic deltamethrin resistance records, stress the importance of systematic monitoring practices to maintain malaria transmission elimination.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a Grécia tenha eliminado a malária há décadas, mudanças climáticas e fluxos populacionais mantêm risco de reintrodução, exigindo dados atualizados sobre a presença de espécies competentes de Anopheles, seu perfil de resistência a inseticidas e eventual infecção parasitária.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Coletas entomológicas em áreas agrícolas e periurbanas da Grécia central e meridional entre 2021 e 2024 foram identificadas por código de barras de DNA multilocus. Subamostras passaram por bioensaios de resistência a inseticidas segundo diretrizes do CDC e bioensaios larvais da OMS para Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti), genotipagem de mutações no gene do canal de sódio dependente de voltagem (alelo L1014) e pesquisa molecular de Plasmodium em fêmeas adultas de Phthiotis.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identificaram-se cinco espécies de Anopheles, incluindo vetores competentes de malária como An. sacharovi, An. labranchiae e An. claviger. Os bioensaios detectaram resistência à deltametrina na Coríntia e Beócia e possível resistência em Phthiotis, enquanto todas as populações testadas tenderam à susceptibilidade frente ao larvicida Bti; o sequenciamento revelou apenas o alelo selvagem L1014 no canal de sódio, e todos os adultos de Phthiotis testaram negativos para Plasmodium.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Documenta resistência fenotípica incipiente a piretróides (deltametrina) dissociada da mutação clássica kdr L1014, sugerindo mecanismos metabólicos alternativos e preservando sensibilidade ao Bti — dado relevante tanto para vetores de malária quanto para o eixo de bioinseticidas do grupo.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Rastrear em colônias resistentes a piretróides sem mutação L1014 quais enzimas metabólicas ou barreiras cuticulares sustentam o fenótipo de resistência antes da perda de eficácia de Bti.

43015198.titulo: New sites of vulnerability to stop vivax malaria
43015198.resumo: Comentário sobre sítios vulneráveis da PvCSP, a proteína circunferencial do esporozoíto de P. vivax, como alvos vacinais pelo modelo já usado com PfCSP.
43015198.resumo_original: Malaria vaccines based on the PfCSP molecule are now being deployed to prevent infection by the deadly parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. Can we apply the same tricks to stop the second major malaria parasite, Plasmodium vivax? Visweswaren and colleagues studied PvCSP, revealing new sites of vulnerability to target with vaccines.

resumo_blocos.racional: Vacinas de subunidade dirigidas à proteína circunsporozoíta PfCSP vêm sendo implantadas contra Plasmodium falciparum, levantando a questão translacional crítica de quais epítopos estruturais equivalentes na PvCSP podem sustentar imunógenos eficazes contra Plasmodium vivax.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Comentário analítico de literatura estrutural e imunológica examinando o mapeamento fino de anticorpos monoclonais e epítopos de vulnerabilidade na proteína circunsporozoíta de P. vivax (PvCSP) em comparação à arquitetura funcional de PfCSP.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Destaca novos sítios vulneráveis conservados na molécula de PvCSP capazes de guiar o desenho de vacinas pré-eritrocíticas de segunda geração contra malária por vivax segundo os princípios validados para PfCSP.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Relevante para contextualizar as estratégias pré-eritrocíticas em malária sul-americana onde Plasmodium vivax predomina e interage com anofelinos neotropicais na transição intestino-glândula salivar.

43044898.titulo: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
43044898.autores: Song X, Feng M, … Luan Y (5 autores)
43044898.resumo: Hipótese de persistência e gating circadiano da memória neuroimune em dor crônica e depressão (Neurosci Biobehav Rev). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43044898.resumo_original: Chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction provide distinct settings in which inflammatory responses and persistent vulnerability may intersect. Evidence for specific cytokine, synaptic, and microglial mechanisms differs across these conditions and does not establish a single comorbidity mechanism. We examine whether circadian context influences the formation or later expression of neuroimmune memory. Circadian regulation of inflammatory responses and innate immune memory each have experimental support, while their coupling in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved. Human BCG vaccination studies provide a peripheral timing-and-training precedent, which cannot be assumed to operate in the brain. We distinguish immune memory from ongoing inflammation, neuronal chromatin regulation, and sustained symptoms, and separate cell-autonomous microglial timing from rhythmic environmental inputs. The framework generates distinct tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal. A convincing test requires a resolved first challenge, control of initial inflammatory exposure and recall phase, and cell-resolved molecular measurements coupled to altered secondary-response function. Failure to reverse an established imprint would not exclude a role for timing during its formation. Perioperative studies offer a defined exposure but must distinguish delirium from longer-term cognitive decline. This evidence-calibrated hypothesis specifies what must be demonstrated before circadian interventions can be linked to prevention or modification of neuroimmune memory.

43057893.titulo: Profiling Histone Modifications in Harpegnathos saltator Brains by CUT&Tag.
43057893.autores: Kuang M, Antonova A, … Bonasio R (5 autores)
43057893.resumo: 🎲 [exploração] Protocolo CUT&Tag para modificações de histona em cérebros de formiga (Harpegnathos), com isolamento de núcleos de órgão pequeno e baixa entrada.
43057893.resumo_original: Harpegnathos saltator ants are a powerful model for studying socially induced adult brain plasticity. In this species, adult workers can transition into reproductive gamergates, which is accompanied by extensive behavioral, physiological, and gene regulatory changes arising from a single genome. Understanding the chromatin mechanisms that regulate these transitions requires epigenomic methods that are sensitive enough to profile small organs such as insect brains. Cleavage under targets and tagmentation (CUT&Tag) is a genome-wide chromatin profiling method that can be used to map histone modifications at high resolution from low-input samples by using an antibody-directed protein A/G-Tn5 transposase to perform targeted, in situ DNA tagmentation, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio compared with other chromatin profiling approaches. Here, we provide a CUT&Tag protocol that has been optimized for profiling histone modifications in Harpegnathos brains. We describe the steps for nuclei isolation from insect brains, followed by antibody incubation, transposase binding and tagmentation, and library preparation for high-throughput sequencing. This protocol is further adaptable to single-cell multiomic assays, enabling high-resolution profiling of the epigenomic landscape in social insect brains and other organs.

43061799.titulo: NET-Inhibiting Bio-Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence.
43061799.autores: Li F, Li X, … He XT (20 autores)
43061799.resumo: Neutrófilos e NETs mantêm imunidade treinada maladaptativa em periodontite, com reprogramação epigenética da medula; plataforma de neutrófilos gelatinados com DNase I e tPA apaga a memória e evita recidiva.
43061799.resumo_original: Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis-induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET-inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs-DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation-homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co-delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs-DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature-induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm-shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.

43057231.titulo: Clock misalignment, not structural loss, underlies memory impairment following disruption of the mushroom body.
43057231.autores: Dissel S, Tan WJ, … Shaw PJ (23 autores)
43057231.resumo: Perda do corpo cogumelar de Drosophila por hidroxiureia prejudica memória por desalinhamento do relógio (via PDF/Pdfr em neurônios dopaminérgicos), não por perda estrutural; restaurar sono ou reduzir Pdfr corrige. Sem ligação direta com mosquito; interessa como lógica de temporização circadiana em circuito de aprendizado.
43057231.resumo_original: The Drosophila mushroom body (MB) is a central circuit for many forms of associative learning, including olfactory conditioning, courtship conditioning, and aversive phototaxic suppression (APS). Kenyon cells (KCs), the intrinsic neurons of the MB, can be severely disrupted but not entirely eliminated by hydroxy urea (HU) treatment during development. Here, we show that HU-treated flies are profoundly impaired in short- and long-term memory under baseline conditions and that enhanced sleep restores learning in these animals. We establish the robustness of this finding using multiple behavioral assays and two independent methods to enhance sleep. Mechanistic analyses reveal that HU treatment disrupts circadian clock output, mistiming activity in γ-lobe-projecting dopaminergic neurons (DANs) and MB output neurons (MBONs). We further show that this mistiming is mediated, in part, by pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) signaling onto γ2-projecting DANs. Enhanced sleep restores the proper temporal coordination of these circuits. Strikingly, selectively reducing PDF receptor (Pdfr) signaling in these DANs also restored memory in HU-treated flies despite markedly reduced sleep, demonstrating that correcting mistimed clock signals can reproduce the restorative effects of sleep. These findings indicate that memory impairments after HU treatment can arise from disrupted temporal coordination within the MB circuit and demonstrate that downstream MBON-DAN interactions can support learning when properly regulated.

43008141.titulo: What do we really know about human immunometabolism in inflammatory disease?
43008141.autores: Gunawardana S, Romero Arocha S, Clarke AJ (3 autores)
43008141.resumo: Revisão crítica do que se sabe de imunometabolismo humano: limites de culturas artificiais, medidas estáticas e uso do sangue como substituto de tecido; propõe cinco prioridades (tecido inflamado, fluxo por isótopos estáveis, modalidades de célula única, espacial e imagem, perturbações metabólicas desenhadas, contexto sistêmico e pré-analítico).
43008141.resumo_original: Cellular metabolism is now recognised as an active regulator of immune cell activation, differentiation, and function. However, much of this conceptual framework derives from in vitro systems and animal models that may not fully reproduce human physiology or disease. Many studies of human immune metabolism are constrained by artificial culture conditions, tissue dissociation, limited pathway coverage, and a reliance on static measurements that do not directly quantify metabolic flux in vivo. Interpretation is further complicated by the use of blood samples as a surrogate for diseases that arise in specialised tissues, such as synovium, gut, and skin, and by the influence of systemic physiology, including hepatic substrate regulation, adipose tissue, endocrine and neuronal signalling, and the gut microbiota. In this review, we examine what current experimental approaches can infer about immune metabolism in humans, with a focus on immune-mediated inflammatory diseases. Oncology provides a valuable methodological precedent through its use of tissue sampling, spatial profiling, and stable isotope tracing, while also illustrating the challenges of assigning metabolic activity to individual cell populations within heterogeneous tissues. We propose five priorities for the field: move beyond blood to inflammatory tissue; complement static abundance with dynamic, stable isotope flux analysis; integrate single cell, spatial, and imaging modalities; incorporate carefully designed human metabolic perturbations; and account for the wider systemic and pre-analytical context. The next phase of human immunometabolism should move from pathway annotation in reductionist models towards dynamic, tissue-resolved, and clinically anchored studies of immune cell metabolism in vivo.

43005892.titulo: Hepatocyte-derived lipid droplets in MASH: macrophage sensing and inflammation
43005892.resumo: Mini-revisão sobre gotículas lipídicas derivadas de hepatócitos e seu sensoriamento por macrófagos na MASH: a captação da gotícula é distinta do efeito imune; MS4A7 contribui para a ativação do inflamassoma NLRP3 e TREM2 sustenta a supressão inflamatória sem ser necessário à captação.
43005892.resumo_original: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) develops through interactions between hepatocyte injury and hepatic immune responses. Lipid droplets (LDs) exposed or released from damaged hepatocytes provide a potential link between lipid accumulation and macrophage-mediated inflammation. Experimental studies indicate that these structures can both promote disease-associated macrophage responses and attenuate inflammatory signaling. This mini-review examines how hepatocyte-derived LDs influence macrophage sensing, uptake, and inflammatory responses in MASH. We discuss the contribution of membrane-spanning 4-domains A7 (MS4A7) to NLRP3 inflammasome activation and disease progression, alongside evidence that LD treatment suppresses inflammatory responses in cultured macrophages. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) supports this suppression without being required for LD uptake in the tested system, while reduced MS4A7 expression contributes to the attenuation of inflammatory signaling. These findings distinguish LD internalization from its downstream immune effects and warrant separate consideration from the efferocytosis of intact apoptotic hepatocytes. We examine experimental conditions and macrophage states as possible explanations for differing outcomes and identify unresolved questions about LD recognition and relevance to human disease. Finally, we consider therapeutic strategies that limit pathogenic macrophage activation while preserving beneficial clearance functions. Defining the molecular basis of LD sensing and establishing its consequences in vivo will be essential for translating this form of hepatocyte-macrophage communication into immunological interventions for MASH.

43027377.titulo: Trained Immunity and Persistent Myeloid Responsiveness in MASH.
43027377.autores: Fu L, Guo R, … Zhang Q (4 autores)
43027377.resumo: Revisão de imunidade treinada na MASH: liga lipídios, glicólise, acetil-CoA e lactilação de histona à capacidade de resposta mieloide e pede desenhos com injúria, regressão e reexposição.
43027377.resumo_original: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) involves hepatocellular injury, myeloid activation, and fibrotic remodeling that may resolve unevenly following metabolic improvement. Whether previous injury leaves a functionally consequential innate immune imprint remains unresolved. This review evaluates trained immunity as a candidate mechanism linking exposure history to persistent hepatic myeloid responsiveness. We distinguish continued activation by lipotoxic and stromal signals from responses retained after stimulus withdrawal, macrophage replacement, and hematopoietic progenitor programming. Evidence from Kupffer cells, monocyte-derived macrophages, and lipid- or scar-associated populations reveals divergent inflammatory, efferocytosis, and matrix remodeling functions. Receptor-dependent lipid handling intersects with glycolysis, citrate-derived acetyl-CoA, serine and one-carbon metabolism, NAD+ availability and histone methylation, acetylation, and lactylation. These pathways explain how metabolic inputs regulate inflammatory competence, but their alteration during active MASH does not establish immune memory. Rested monocyte training models provide stronger temporal evidence than most disease-specific studies, whereas protective TREM2-dependent responses caution against indiscriminate suppression of disease-associated macrophages. Establishing a contribution to MASH recurrence requires lineage-resolved investigations spanning injury, regression, and rechallenge, with interventions separating memory establishment, maintenance, and effector output. If exposure-dependent myeloid memory contributes causally to MASH recurrence, targeting maladaptive responsiveness could complement injury control while preserving hepatic repair.

43036379.titulo: Immunometabolic alterations in young adults with obesity are accompanied by divergent monocyte and muscle mitochondrial bioenergetic profiles.
43036379.autores: Ursel S, Nekkanti S, … Islam H (14 autores)
43036379.resumo: Adultos jovens com obesidade (n=17) e sem obesidade (n=20), pareados por idade, sexo e atividade, tiveram respiração mitocondrial muscular maior, mas respiração de monócitos menor (OXPHOS e ETS), com menor TLR4, menor mtROS estimulado por citocina e marcadores pró-inflamatórios ex vivo exagerados (p=0,07).
43036379.resumo_original:
Mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation are implicated in obesity-associated metabolic disorders. Studies interrogating muscle mitochondrial bioenergetics in obesity are confounded by the impact of age and/or physical activity. How obesity impacts mitochondrial bioenergetics in monocytes-precursors to muscle-resident macrophages-is poorly understood. We aimed to compare whole-body immunometabolic function and mitochondrial respiration in muscle and monocytes in adults with or without obesity of similar sex, age and physical activity levels.
In this cross-sectional study, young adults with obesity (BMI ≥ 30) or without obesity (BMI < 30) of similar age, sex and activity levels provided a fasted blood sample and muscle biopsy (vastus lateralis), and underwent a mixed-meal tolerance test. Mitochondrial respiration was measured in permeabilised muscle fibres and blood monocytes using high-resolution respirometry alongside muscle mitochondrial proteins and enzyme activity. Blood monocyte phenotype, polarisation and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) were quantified using flow cytometry.
Young adults with obesity (n = 17 [9 female/8 male], age 23.1 [SD 5.7] years, BMI 33.2 [SD 3.1] kg/m2) exhibited impaired whole-body insulin sensitivity (d = 1.2) and elevated white blood cell counts (d = 0.9; both p < 0.01) compared with those without obesity (n = 20 [10 female/10 male], age 22.8 [SD 4.6] years, BMI 21.8 [SD 2.1] kg/m2). Muscle oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS; d = 0.7-0.8) and electron transfer system capacity (ETS; d = 1.0) were higher in young adults with obesity than in those without obesity (p < 0.05) despite similar mitochondrial content markers (d = 0.2; p > 0.6). Monocyte OXPHOS (d = 1.0) and ETS (d = 0.8) were attenuated in those with obesity and accompanied by lower Toll-like receptor 4 expression (d = 0.7-0.8), diminished cytokine-stimulated mtROS production (d = 0.8-1.0) (all p < 0.05) and exaggerated proinflammatory marker expression ex vivo (d = 0.8; p = 0.07).
Young adults with obesity exhibit elevated muscle mitochondrial respiration-consistent with early adaptive remodelling in response to energy surplus-accompanied by heightened systemic inflammation and cellular markers suggestive of a dysregulated immunometabolic phenotype.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s44357-026-00031-5.

43040116.titulo: Metabolic and Signaling Pathways of Macrophage Reprogramming in Atherosclerosis and Myocardial Infarction
43040116.autores: Ding Z, Wang Y, … Yu L (4 autores)
43040116.resumo: Revisão do imunometabolismo da reprogramação de macrófagos: M1 com glicólise aeróbia, via das pentoses e ciclo TCA rompido, M2 com fosforilação oxidativa e oxidação de ácidos graxos, e vias integradoras TLR/NF-κB, JAK/STAT e PI3K/Akt/mTOR.
43040116.resumo_original: Atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction remain the predominant contributors to mortality despite advances in interventional cardiology. Chronic inflammatory responses mediated by macrophages serve as a critical determinant of the pathogenesis of cardiovascular diseases. This review systematically dissects the immunometabolic and signaling networks underlying macrophage reprogramming, with a focus on key cardiovascular diseases. We assess the characteristics of M1 macrophages, which involve aerobic glycolysis, activation of the pentose phosphate pathway, and disruption of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, compared to M2 macrophages that rely on oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid oxidation. Integrated signaling pathways dynamically regulate these metabolic programmes-centred on TLR/NF-κB-mediated inflammatory priming, JAK/STAT-dependent transcriptional polarization, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR-AMPK-PPARγ metabolic checkpoints, which interpret microenvironmental signals to control macrophage polarization. Within atherosclerotic lesions, we demonstrate that M1-dominant macrophage populations exacerbate plaque inflammation and compromise structural integrity, whereas M2 macrophages augment inflammatory resolution and tissue restoration. Following myocardial infarction, the timely therapeutic reprogramming from M1 to M2 phenotype is essential for efficiently attenuating adverse cardiac remodeling and improving cardiac function. Targeting metabolic enzymes and signaling pathways offers a promising strategy for reprogramming macrophages and mitigating cardiovascular diseases.

43054402.titulo: When location makes oxidative stress lethal: mitoxyperilysis at the immunometabolic stress interface.
43054402.autores: Zhang Y, Xia XP, Zhao L (3 autores)
43054402.resumo: Revisão que propõe a mitoxiperilise: mitocôndrias oxidadas retidas na membrana plasmática tornam-se letais; nos modelos fundadores, TLR mais restrição de carbono ativam MYD88 e BAX/BAK1/BID, mTORC2-RhoA-actina prolonga a retenção e NINJ1 contribui para a ruptura. Os autores dizem que oxidante, ancoragem e ligação entre dano local e falha de membrana seguem sem resolução.
43054402.resumo_original: Mitoxyperilysis is a proposed lytic death pathway in which oxidatively damaged mitochondria become membrane-lethal when retained at the plasma membrane. In founding models, TLR stimulation plus carbon restriction engaged MYD88-dependent innate signalling and BAX/BAK1/BID-dependent mitochondrial oxidative stress, while mTORC2-RhoA-actin remodelling prolonged peripheral mitochondrial retention. Mitoxyperiosis denotes prolonged mitochondria-plasma membrane association and localised oxidative membrane injury, whereas mitoxyperilysis denotes the subsequent plasma membrane rupture and lytic cell death. In these models, NINJ1 contributed to terminal rupture and LDH/HMGB1 release without being required for cell death. The damaging oxidant, physical tether, and mechanism linking local injury to membrane failure remain unresolved. Sepsis may reproduce upstream metabolic-redox conditions, but direct evidence for the complete spatial sequence in patient-derived cells is lacking. This review separates founding-model findings from disease-relevant observations and untested steps.

43053064.titulo: Itaconate as a central node in immunometabolism and inflammatory control.
43053064.autores: Lin J, Wang G, Zi F (3 autores)
43053064.resumo: Revisão do itaconato como nó de imunometabolismo e controle inflamatório.
43053064.resumo_original:
Mitochondria serve as central regulators of cellular bioenergetics and inflammatory signaling, integrating metabolic status with immune responses. Disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis, including altered tricarboxylic acid cycle dynamics, redox imbalance, and aberrant reactive oxygen species production, contributes to persistent inflammation and disease pathogenesis. Among emerging mitochondrial immunometabolic regulators, the IRG1/ACOD1-derived metabolite itaconate has gained attention as a critical molecular integrator linking mitochondrial metabolism to inflammatory control.
This review systematically summarizes the biosynthesis of itaconate and its role in mitochondrial metabolic remodeling during inflammation. Itaconate reshapes the tricarboxylic acid cycle and inhibits succinate dehydrogenase, thereby limiting mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation and preventing amplification of pro-inflammatory signaling. Through covalent modification of KEAP1, it activates the NRF2 antioxidant program, while concurrently restraining NLRP3 inflammasome activation, establishing a mitochondrial metabolic checkpoint that constrains excessive immune activation. Beyond acute metabolic regulation, itaconate coordinates sustained immunoregulatory programs via the ATF3-IκBζ transcriptional axis, autophagy-lysosome system modulation, and epigenetic reprogramming. We further integrate cell-type-specific effects of itaconate across macrophages, dendritic cells, T cells, and neutrophils, and discuss how mitochondrial immunometabolic dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammatory and metabolic disorders.
By positioning the IRG1-itaconate axis within the broader framework of mitochondrial immunometabolism, this review highlights mitochondria as a central hub linking metabolic remodeling with inflammatory regulation. Targeting mitochondrial metabolic checkpoints such as the itaconate pathway may provide promising therapeutic strategies for restoring immune homeostasis and treating inflammation-associated diseases.

resumo_blocos.racional: A disfunção mitocondrial — envolvendo alterações do ciclo dos ácidos tricarboxílicos (TCA), desequilíbrio redox e excesso de espécies reativas de oxigênio — impulsiona inflamação persistente, colocando o metabólito itaconato (derivado de IRG1/ACOD1) como possível elo central de controle imunometabólico.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão mecanística sistemática sobre a biossíntese de itaconato via IRG1/ACOD1 e seus mecanismos de remodelamento metabólico e imunorregulador em macrófagos, células dendríticas, linfócitos T e neutrófilos, integrando inibição da succinato desidrogenase (SDH), alquilação de KEAP1/NRF2, contenção do inflamassoma NLRP3, eixo transcricional ATF3-IκBζ, modulação autofágica-lisossomal e reprogramação epigenética.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Posiciona o eixo IRG1-itaconato como ponto de controle metabólico mitocondrial que limita a geração de ROS mitocondrial pela inibição de SDH, ativa a resposta antioxidante via modificação covalente de KEAP1/NRF2, restringe NLRP3 e coordena programas anti-inflamatórios sustentados via ATF3-IκBζ e remodelamento lisossomal e epigenético.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Dialoga diretamente com a frente de imunometabolismo mitocondrial, estresse redox e autofagia em macrófagos e células de inseto (linhagem Aag2), sugerindo checagem de vias análogas de controle redox/TCA após desafio metabólico.

43022429.titulo: Connectome analysis reveals brain-wide visual processing in
43022429.resumo: Análise do conectoma de Drosophila classifica neurônios de projeção entre lobo óptico e cérebro central em feedforward, feedback e bilaterais por polaridade sináptica e conectividade.
43022429.resumo_original: Sensory processing relies on a brain-wide network that integrates specialized sensory circuits with the rest of the brain. To understand how this integration shapes visual processing, we used the whole-brain Drosophila melanogaster connectome to analyze the long-range projections that reciprocally connect the optic lobe (OL)-the principal visual center-with the central brain and with the contralateral OL. By quantifying synaptic polarity and connectivity, we classified the projection neurons into feedforward, feedback, and bilateral groups. Feedforward projection neurons form an information bottleneck, consolidating diverse visual features from the OL and distributing them through modular pathways for higher-order processing. Feedback projection neurons densely innervate OL structures, conveying contextual signals from the central brain via recurrent loops formed with specific feedforward projection neurons. Bilateral projection neurons link local visual circuits across the two OLs, providing a substrate for inter-ocular processing. Together, these findings reveal how early visual circuits interface with the rest of the brain, establishing a structural basis for future functional studies on brain-wide visual processing.

43041067.titulo: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in thebrain.
43041067.autores: Choucri M, Rainey T, Treiber CD (3 autores)
43041067.resumo: Réplica de Treiber e Waddell à crítica de Azad et al.: com análise quantitativa de exonização, mostram que inserções intrônicas de elementos transponíveis são recrutadas como éxons alternativos no cérebro de Drosophila, com uso de raro a quase total, e que o RT-PCR valida os sete loci contestados em condições apropriadas. A disputa metodológica segue aberta.
43041067.resumo_original: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE-gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE-gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE-gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE-gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE-gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity and functional adaptability of the brain.

43040328.titulo: Drosophila CerS homeodomain sites differentially alter insulin resistance
43040328.autores: Vera-Granda C, Sociale M, … Bauer R (11 autores)
43040328.resumo: Alelos knock-in no homeodomínio da ceramida sintase Schlank aumentam ou atenuam a resistência à insulina induzida por dieta rica em açúcar conforme o sítio e o tecido: KIE118A e KINLS1 pioram hiperglicemia e recrutamento de tGPH, KIE118A acumula mais FoxO nuclear e retém DILP2 nas células produtoras de insulina, e no corpo gorduroso NLS2 e H215D reduzem o pool de ceramidas.
43040328.resumo_original:
Ceramides are central sphingolipid intermediates whose abundance and molecular composition are closely linked to insulin resistance. Ceramide synthases (CerSs) generate ceramides and, in several family members, also contain a conserved homeodomain with poorly understood metabolic functions. Drosophila has a single CerS, Schlank, which contains a catalytic Lag1p motif and two predicted nuclear localization sequences, NLS1 and NLS2. We investigated how distinct Schlank homeodomain mutations affect high-sugar diet (HSD)-induced insulin resistance.
Endogenous KINLS1 and KIE118A knock-in alleles retained DNA binding and transcriptional repression under basal conditions but increased susceptibility to HSD-induced metabolic dysfunction. Both mutants developed enhanced hyperglycemia and impaired insulin-responsive tGPH recruitment, while KIE118A additionally showed increased FoxO nuclear localization and DILP2 retention in insulin-producing cells. By contrast, fat-body-specific switching to the DNA-binding-deficient NLS2 variant or the catalytically inactive H215D variant attenuated selected HSD-induced phenotypes, including FoxO nuclear accumulation and DILP2 retention, without fully correcting hyperglycemia or reduced body weight. Lipidomic analysis revealed extensive diet-dependent sphingolipid remodeling. In particular, NLS2 and H215D markedly reduced the fat-body ceramide pool, including abundant d14:1/20:0- and d14:1/22:0-containing Cer, CerPE, and HexCer species.
The Schlank homeodomain regulates insulin homeostasis in a site- and tissue-dependent manner. Distinct homeodomain mutations can either increase susceptibility to or partially attenuate HSD-induced insulin resistance, potentially involving insulin signaling, inter-organ communication, and sphingolipid composition.

43050364.titulo: Rhodopsin 7 is an ancestral non-canonical photoreceptor that shapes light-responsive behavior.
43050364.autores: Kirsch V, Reinhard N, … Senthilan PR (8 autores)
43050364.resumo: A rodopsina 7 de Drosophila funciona como sensor de luz não canônico, semelhante à melanopsina, expresso no cérebro e no lobo óptico: detecta mudanças temporais de luminância, guia respostas rápidas e regula a atividade diária (moscas sem RH7 ficam menos ativas no escuro). A filogenia a coloca como rodopsina antiga presente em panartrópodes.
43050364.resumo_original: Animals rely on light not only for vision but also to adapt behavior to their environment through non-image-forming pathways. In Drosophila, most rhodopsins mediate retinal image formation, but Rhodopsin 7 (RH7) is widely expressed in the brain and optic lobe, acting as a non-canonical light sensor reminiscent of mammalian melanopsin. We combined expression mapping, behavioral assays, and phylogenetic comparisons to investigate its function. RH7 detects temporal changes in luminance, guiding rapid behavioral responses, and regulating daily activity patterns. Flies lacking RH7 are less active during the dark phase, while strains with constitutively active RH7 show increased activity. Phylogenetic analyses suggest that RH7 is an ancient rhodopsin present across panarthropods, representing an intermediate between G protein-coupled receptors and specialized rhodopsins, highlighting a key step in the evolution of non-visual light perception. These findings show that RH7 functions as a melanopsin-like sensor, shaping behavior, and illuminating the origins of light detection.

A filogenia a coloca como rodopsina antiga presente em panartrópodes.

43009698.titulo: GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infectious diseases: basic biology, immunometabolic mechanisms, and therapeutic translation.
43009698.autores: Yue X, Fu H, … Chen J (13 autores)
43009698.resumo: Revisão do eixo GLP-1/GLP-1R em infecção: os agonistas atenuam inflamação e lesão tecidual de forma mais consistente do que alteram a carga do patógeno, e a evidência de sinalização intrínseca em célula imune é limitada.
43009698.resumo_original: Infectious diseases remain a major global health burden, and metabolic disorders such as diabetes and obesity further increase susceptibility to infection and adverse outcomes. These intersecting metabolic and infectious risks have prompted growing interest in the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)/GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) axis beyond its established role in glycaemic regulation. GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) modulate systemic metabolism, neuroimmune signalling, vascular and epithelial homeostasis, and inflammatory responses. Whether their infection-related effects arise from direct immune-cell GLP-1R signalling, improved pathogen control, or indirect host protection remains unresolved. This narrative review critically evaluates GLP-1/GLP-1R signalling in infection. It distinguishes live-pathogen models from endotoxin and sterile-injury models, host resistance from host tolerance, and direct receptor-dependent actions from indirect systemic effects. It also differentiates chronic pre-infection exposure from treatment initiated after infection onset. Across selected preclinical models, GLP-1RAs more consistently attenuate inflammation and tissue injury while preserving organ function, whereas their effects on pathogen burden and clearance remain variable. Receptor-specific evidence for immune-cell-intrinsic GLP-1R signalling remains limited, and many reported immune phenotypes may instead reflect metabolic improvement, neuroimmune regulation, or barrier protection. Human evidence is derived mainly from observational studies and secondary analyses of chronic GLP-1RA exposure, with limited evidence from trials initiating treatment during acute infection. Future translation will require cell-specific receptor validation, live-pathogen models with post-infection treatment, parallel assessment of pathogen control and host protection, clinically relevant standard-of-care comparators, and infection-specific safety evaluation. GLP-1RAs are therefore best regarded as candidate host-directed adjuncts. Current evidence does not establish them as direct anti-infective therapies.

43009129.titulo: Microglial, migrasomes promote high-fat diet-induced neurotoxicity.
43009129.autores: Qin Q, Liu Z, … Cai W (9 autores)
43009129.resumo: Dieta hiperlipídica induz, antes de dislipidemia ou lesão vascular, remodelação lipídica da substância branca e migrassomos microgliais ricos em S100A9 que causam lesão neuronal; o knockout de Tspan9 em microglia reduz a toxicidade.
43009129.resumo_original:
Systemic metabolic abnormalities are established drivers of cognitive decline, traditionally attributed to secondary sequelae of cerebrovascular dysfunction. However, cellular events linking early metabolic stress to subsequent neuronal injury and neurodegenerative processes remain poorly defined.
Here, we demonstrate that high-fat diet (HFD) triggers microglia to release pathogenic migrasomes (long-lived organelle-like vesicles) that promote neuronal injury, during an early phase of metabolic stress, before the emergence of overt dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, and vascular pathology. We found that HFD feeding remodels the lipid environment of myelin-rich white matter and disrupts myelin homeostasis. Upon phagocytosis of this altered myelin, microglia generate migrasomes enriched with the neurotoxic alarmin S100A9. The pathogenicity of these vesicles was supported by complementary gain- and loss-of-function studies: intracerebral injection of HFD-induced microglial migrasomes was sufficient to impair cognition and induce neuronal injury in healthy mice, whereas Tspan9 conditional knockout in Cx3cr1-CreERT2 mice markedly reduced migrasome formation and thereby attenuated HFD-induced neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, we show that S100A9 is sorted into migrasomes post-myelin phagocytosis and is a critical mediator for their neurotoxic effects.
These results uncover a metabolic-myelin-migrasome axis as a critical driver of neuronal injury and cognitive decline, identifying the blockade of microglial migrasome biogenesis as a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolism-associated neurological dysfunction.

43044582.titulo: Evolutionary repurposing of a pore-forming toxin drives epithelial remodeling during terrestrial adaptation
43044582.autores: Siciliani D, Benedicenti O, … Salinas I (15 autores)
43044582.resumo: Uma toxina pequena formadora de poro do pulmonado africano (Protop-CrTX-A) é suficiente para ativar programas transcricionais de morfogênese epitelial e funciona como interruptor reversível da remodelação da pele entre os estados aquático e terrestre; goblet cells a secretam no muco e, na estivação, granulócitos tornam-se a fonte principal. Os autores propõem que a imunidade inata, por remodelar tecidos, foi motor da transição água-terra.
43044582.resumo_original: The ability of vertebrates to conquer land is attributed to innovations in respiration and locomotion. However, land adaptation profoundly reshaped mucosal surfaces such as the skin, the main interface between hosts and the environment. To adapt to land, African lungfish annually remodel their skin, forming a cocoon. Here, we report the discovery of a small pore-forming toxin in African lungfish, Protop-CrTX-A, with no other vertebrate counterpart that is sufficient to drive epithelial morphogenesis transcriptional programs. In free-swimming lungfish, goblet cells secrete Protop-CrTX-A into the mucus. During estivation, this niche is replaced by a mucin-low/basal epithelial niche, adjacent to a granulocyte immune niche that becomes the predominant source of Protop-CrTX-A in the estivated skin. Protop-CrTX-A acts as a reversible switch for skin remodeling, sufficient to convert African lungfish skin between aquatic and terrestrial states. We propose that innate immunity, through its capacity to remodel tissues, was a key driver of vertebrate water-land transitions.

43021391.titulo: Partial connectivity and fine-scale population structure in Honduran Anopheles albimanus inferred from microsatellite markers
43021391.autores: Mejía A, Escobar D, … Fontecha G (4 autores)
43021391.resumo: Microssatélites em 176 An. albimanus de dez populações de Honduras mostram conectividade parcial e estrutura populacional em escala fina.
43021391.resumo_original:
Understanding population connectivity in malaria vectors is important for surveillance in elimination settings, where local dispersal and population subdivision may influence residual transmission and the spread of adaptive traits. Anopheles albimanus is the major malaria vector in Honduras, yet its population structure remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to assess the genetic diversity and population structure of Honduran An. albimanus populations using microsatellite markers.
Adult mosquitoes collected from ten populations across Honduras (n = 176) were genotyped at eight species-specific microsatellite loci. Genetic diversity was estimated using the number of alleles, effective number of alleles, observed and expected heterozygosity, and Wright's fixation index. Population differentiation was evaluated using pairwise FST estimates and analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA). A hierarchical AMOVA was used to assess regional structure, and Bayesian clustering implemented in STRUCTURE was used to infer genetic clusters, with the most likely number of clusters determined using the Evanno ΔK method. Isolation by distance was tested with a Mantel test.
All loci were polymorphic and showed moderate to high genetic diversity (He = 0.513-0.817). Observed heterozygosity was consistently lower than expected, with widespread heterozygote deficits and frequent departures from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium across populations. Pairwise FST values ranged from 0.008 to 0.195, consistent with heterogeneous levels of genetic connectivity. AMOVA showed that 88% of genetic variation occurred within populations and 12% among populations (PhiPT = 0.117, P < 0.001), consistent with moderate but significant differentiation. Hierarchical AMOVA indicated minimal differentiation between La Mosquitia and the rest of Honduras (PhiRT = 0.012), while Bayesian clustering supported two inferred genetic clusters (K = 2) with evidence of admixture across populations, and Mantel analysis detected no evidence of isolation by distance.
Honduran An. albimanus populations harbor substantial genetic diversity while exhibiting moderate differentiation and fine-scale substructure despite overall connectivity. These findings are consistent with a model of partial connectivity shaped primarily by local population-level processes and illustrate the utility of microsatellite markers for detecting contemporary population structure relevant to malaria vector surveillance and control in elimination settings. Given the limited number of loci and the modest, cross-sectional sample, the structure reported here should be regarded as a conservative estimate of underlying population subdivision.

resumo_blocos.racional: Na transição para eliminação da malária neotropical, compreender se populações locais de Anopheles albimanus funcionam como uma população panmítica ou subdividida em subpopulações discretas define a escala espacial necessária de vigilância e bloqueio vetorial.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Genotipagem de 176 espécimes adultos de An. albimanus coletados em dez populações de Honduras usando oito locos microssatélites espécie-específicos, com estimativa de diversidade genética (He), estatísticas F (FST), AMOVA hierárquica, agrupamento Bayesiano (STRUCTURE / ΔK de Evanno) e teste de Mantel para isolamento por distância.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Todos os microssatélites exibiram polimorfismo moderado a alto (He = 0,513–0,817) com déficit recorrente de heterozigotos e desvios do equilíbrio de Hardy-Weinberg. A AMOVA apontou 12% de variação entre populações (PhiPT = 0,117; p < 0,001), conectividade parcial com dois grupamentos genéticos (K = 2) e ausência de isolamento geográfico simples pelo teste de Mantel.

43041240.titulo: Serum context shapes macrophage baseline state and LPS responsiveness in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
43041240.autores: Cosma NC, Eren N, … Hellmann-Regen J (4 autores)
43041240.resumo: Em macrófagos humanos derivados de monócitos (32 doadores), a diferenciação com soro autólogo em vez de soro fetal bovino muda o estado basal (FCS: mais inflamatório; autólogo: lipídios, matriz, vigilância) e aumenta a resposta a LPS (TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23), sem diferença com IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β.
43041240.resumo_original:
Human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) are central to translational immunology, yet most differentiation protocols rely on xenogeneic fetal calf serum (FCS), which may alter macrophage functional states. Autologous serum (AS) maintains the donor-specific immunometabolic milieu, but its impact on macrophage baseline programming and stimulus responsiveness has not been systematically evaluated.
Monocytes from 32 healthy donors were differentiated in parallel with 10% AS or FCS for five days with M-CSF, followed by 24-hour stimulation with LPS, IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β, or vehicle. Cytokine secretion was quantified by multiplex assay, activation markers by qPCR, and baseline transcriptional programs by bulk RNA sequencing.
AS- versus FCS-differentiated MDMs showed significantly greater LPS-induced secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23, TARC and IL-1RA together with higher CD86 and CCR7 expression, whereas these differences were not observed following IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β stimulation or in unstimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis of unstimulated MDMs identified distinct serum-dependent baseline programs, with FCS associated with increased expression of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and innate immune activation genes, whereas AS was associated with genes involved in lipid metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune surveillance.
Serum context is a major determinant of macrophage baseline state and inflammatory responsiveness. FCS is associated with a more inflammatory baseline and attenuated LPS-induced activation, while AS shows a metabolically and immunologically homeostatic baseline with greater LPS responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that serum composition shapes basal macrophage programs and differentially modulates responses to inflammatory versus alternative stimulation, supporting consideration of autologous serum when modeling donor-specific innate immune responses.

43008048.titulo: Spatio-temporal clustering of dengue in Valle del Cauca, Colombia
43008048.autores: Sy H, Vargas-Gonzalez DA, … Alexander ND (6 autores)
43008048.resumo: Varredura espaço-temporal de Kulldorff em 1.973 casos de dengue confirmados (SIVIGILA, 2022) em nove municípios do Valle del Cauca: 28 clusters sub-municipais, raio de 0 a 0,98 km, duração de 1 a 6 meses; hospitalização associada a menor nível socioeconômico, regime subsidiado e idade a partir de 70 anos.
43008048.resumo_original:
Dengue is endemic in Colombia's Valle del Cauca region. The precise timing and spatial scale of seasonal dengue transmission necessary for effective reactive interventions at the sub-municipal level across the 42 municipalities of Valle del Cauca remain unclear. This study aimed to identify spatio-temporal dengue clusters in Valle del Cauca.
A retrospective observational study was conducted using individual laboratory-confirmed dengue cases, including residential geolocation and consultation dates, reported by healthcare providers to the Sistema Nacional de Vigilancia en Salud Pública (SIVIGILA) in 2022. Residence was utilized as the probable site of infection. Spatio-temporal clustering was analyzed using Kulldorff's space-time scan statistic to identify statistically significant dengue clusters. Results were mapped using R. As a second aim, the association between clinical and demographic characteristics and dengue hospitalization was evaluated. Of 3,964 dengue cases reported in Valle del Cauca in 2022, 2,232 (56%) were laboratory-confirmed. Of these, 1,973 occurred in the defined areas of the nine municipalities included in the spatio-temporal analysis of this study. We identified 28 clusters at the sub-municipal level, with radii of 0-0.98 km, lasting 1-6 months and containing 10-114 cases. Twenty-six clusters (92.9%) spanned both warm-dry and cool-wet seasons, and clusters accounted for 32.0% of spatially analyzed cases. 960 patients were hospitalized. Lower socioeconomic status (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.07-1.57), enrollment in the state-subsidized insurance scheme (OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.41-2.15) compared with the contributory scheme, and age ≥ 70 years compared to ages 20-29 years (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.51-4.04) were associated with higher odds of hospitalization.
This study identified dengue clusters at the sub-municipal level with the potential to inform reactive dengue control interventions and demonstrated a disproportionate impact on socioeconomically disadvantaged populations and the elderly in Valle del Cauca, Colombia.
