43038261.titulo: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning.
43038261.autores: Chuwongin S, Kaewthamasorn M, … Kittichai V (8 autores)
43038261.resumo: O modelo auto-supervisionado DINOv2-L14 classificou 30 espécies de mosquito a partir de imagens (acurácia 99,2%, F1 86,1%, AUC 0,996) e superou uma ResNet101; com 20% dos dados (11 a 13 imagens por classe) igualou o baseline treinado com tudo. O conjunto é desbalanceado (15 a 124 imagens por classe).
43038261.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. In response to these challenges, this study harnesses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a robust, accessible diagnostic tool. We introduce an innovative application of the Distillation of knowledge with NO labels v2 (DINOv2-l14) algorithm, a self-supervised learning (SSL) model, for the classification of 30 distinct mosquito species from image data. A key focus was enabling the model to learn effectively from a highly imbalanced dataset, where the number of images per class ranged from 15 to 124. We also investigated the data efficiency of SSL by determining the minimum data partition required to match the performance of a conventional supervised model. Our image processing pipeline involved cropping, padding, and dividing images into 14 × 14 patches before converting them into embedded vectors for classification. The fully trained DINOv2-l14 model significantly outperformed a selected ResNet101 baseline, achieving 99.2% accuracy, 97.7% specificity, an F1 score of 86.1%, and a robust area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.996. Most notably, when fine-tuned on just 20% of the available data (averaging 11-13 images per class), the SSL model achieved performance comparable to the baseline model trained on the entire dataset, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency. Although limitations exist, including dataset imbalance and a lack of standardization for broader application, the model's high performance across five-fold cross-validation and strong Cohen's Kappa coefficients (up to 0.836) confirm its reliability. This work validates a novel, efficient, and highly accurate AI-driven approach to mosquito identification. By integrating such a model into a mobile application using an embedding AI framework, this technology holds significant promise for empowering field personnel with a practical, powerful tool to enhance vector surveillance and control programs worldwide.

43041013.titulo: Targeting the Lactate-Lactylation Axis in Cancer Immunotherapy Resistance: From Tumor Acidosis to Context-Dependent Immune Reprogramming
43041013.autores: Liang X, Lin M, … Li Y (6 autores)
43041013.resumo: Revisão que trata o lactato como regulador imunometabólico no microambiente tumoral e a lactilação de histonas e proteínas como elo entre disponibilidade de lactato e cromatina; propõe a lactilação como mediador plausível da conversão de estresse metabólico sustentado em reprogramação imune persistente e diz que persistência após a retirada do estímulo e memória celular ainda não foram demonstradas no câncer.
43041013.resumo_original: Lactate is now recognized as an active immunometabolic regulator in the tumor microenvironment (TME), not simply as a glycolytic byproduct. Its immunological effects arise through several related but distinct routes. Extracellular acidosis, glucose competition, and impaired monocarboxylate transporter-dependent flux can impair CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Lactate- and proton-sensing receptors can also favor suppressive myeloid and regulatory-cell programs. Histone and non-histone lactylation add another layer by linking lactate availability to chromatin regulation and protein function. During sustained or repeated metabolic stress, these processes may support regulatory T-cell fitness, suppressive programs in tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, checkpoint expression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Lactylation is a plausible mediator through which sustained metabolic stress may be converted into persistent immune reprogramming; however, post-withdrawal persistence and cellular memory remain to be demonstrated in cancer. We distinguish lactate-dependent regulation from acidosis and evaluate the links to immune dysfunction and treatment resistance by their temporal, causal, and clinical support. This framework defines tests of post-exposure persistence and connects mechanistic evidence and pharmacological specificity to biomarker development and mechanism-matched trial design.

43057496.titulo: Antimalarial activity of Croton caudatus Geiseler leaf extract and its ability to reduce experimental cerebral malaria pathogenesis.
43057496.autores: Chatterjee A, Singh N, … Nagaraj VA (7 autores)
43057496.resumo: Extrato de folha de Croton caudatus: atividade contra P. falciparum 3D7 (CI50 6,84 µg/mL da fração hexano), inibição de β-hematina, efeito gametocitocida e, em P. berghei ANKA, preservação da barreira hematoencefálica e menos infiltração imune no modelo de malária cerebral experimental. Mecanismo é de heme/ROS; interessa pelo painel de ECM (integridade de BHE e infiltrado) como referência de leitura.
43057496.resumo_original:
Croton caudatus Geiseler is widely used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including malaria. However, scientific evidences supporting its antimalarial activity and the associated molecular mechanisms, and its potential to reduce severe malaria complications are lacking.
The present study was aimed to evaluate the antimalarial activity of C. caudatus leaf extract and its fractions, and to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Methanolic leaf extract of C. caudatus (CcLE) was fractionated into water (CcWater), butanol (CcBut), chloroform (CcChl), and hexane (CcHex) fractions. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against two different strains of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf): Pf3D7 and PfCam3.IR539T, alongside cytotoxicity and hemolysis assays. Phytochemical profiling of the most active fraction was performed by chemical fingerprinting. Mechanistic studies included β-hematin polymerization inhibition, hemozoin quantification, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement. Acute oral toxicity and in vivo antimalarial efficacy were carried out in Plasmodium berghei (Pb) ANKA-infected BALB/c mice. Experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) studies were performed in Pb ANKA-infected C57BL/6 mice through the assessment of blood-brain barrier integrity, inflammatory marker expression, and immune cell infiltration analyses. Examining the gametocyte numbers and ex vivo exflagellation assays were carried out with Pb ANKA-infected mouse blood to assess the gametocytocidal activity.
CcHex exhibited the highest antiplasmodial activity against Pf 3D7 (IC50 = 6.84 ± 0.61 μg/mL) without detectable cytotoxic or hemolytic effects. Phytochemical analysis suggested the presence of bioactive metabolites associated with antimalarial activity. CcHex inhibited β-hematin formation in a cell-free assay and reduced hemozoin levels in Pf3D7 parasites, supporting its potential to interfere with parasite heme detoxification. It also increased intracellular ROS levels in the parasites, suggesting the disruption of heme detoxification. Further, CcHex treatment reduced gametocyte formation and impaired male gametocyte exflagellation, indicating gametocytocidal activity. Acute toxicity studies demonstrated a favourable safety profile. In Pb-infected Balb/c mice, CcHex treatment produced ∼62% parasite suppression at 1000 mg/kg/day. Importantly, CcHex treatment could protect against ECM by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and significantly reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ), chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCR3), the adhesion molecule ICAM-1, and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the brain.
The present study demonstrates that C. caudatus, a traditionally used medicinal plant, possesses significant antiplasmodial activity, exhibits protective effects against ECM, and impairs male gametocyte exflagellation. CcHex showed potent antimalarial efficacy through inhibition of parasite heme detoxification, induction of oxidative stress, and modulation of host inflammatory responses. These results support the ethnopharmacological use of C. caudatus and highlight its potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals for the development of novel antimalarials and adjunctive therapies against severe malaria.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora Croton caudatus Geiseler seja empregado na medicina tradicional contra a malária, faltavam evidências experimentais sobre sua atividade antiplasmódica, seus alvos moleculares no parasito e sua capacidade de conter a patogênese da malária cerebral experimental (ECM).

Testaram-se ainda toxicidade oral aguda e supressão parasitária em camundongos BALB/c com Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA), integridade da barreira hematoencefálica, expressão de citocinas/quimiocinas e infiltrado imune cerebral em camundongos C57BL/6 com ECM, além de gametocitemia e exflagelação ex vivo.

43017141.titulo: Comparative analysis of serum antibody responses and immune landscapes in patients with acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and Chikungunya virus infections
43017141.autores: Zhang Y, Zhang S, … Wu N (13 autores)
43017141.resumo: 80 soros (DENV-1 n=29, DENV-2 n=10, CHIKV n=26, controles n=15): ativação associada a interferon e inflamação sistêmica contida nos três grupos, com perfis de mediadores distintos; associações compartilhadas envolvendo IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4 e CXCL1 após correção de Benjamini-Hochberg.
43017141.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are major mosquito-borne arboviruses that increasingly co-circulate in tropical and subtropical regions, including southern China. However, the extent to which these viruses induce shared or distinct host immune responses remains poorly understood. This study aimed to comparatively characterize immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections.
A total of 80 serum samples were analyzed, including 65 samples from patients with laboratory-confirmed DENV-1 (n = 29), DENV-2 (n = 10), or CHIKV (n = 26) infections and 15 healthy controls.Viral RNA was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction. Virus-specific IgM and IgG responses were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and serum cytokines were quantified using a multiplex assay. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests, and associations among antibody responses, cytokine concentrations, and viral RNA levels were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure.
The three infections shared features of interferon-associated immune activation and relatively restrained systemic inflammation but exhibited distinct immune mediator profiles, characterized by differential inflammatory mediator and growth factor responses. After multiple-testing correction, cytokine-cytokine correlation analysis revealed both shared and infection-specific patterns of immune mediator covariation, with shared associations involving IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4, and CXCL1 across all three infection groups. Positive associations between pathogen-specific IgM responses and Ct values were observed across the infections, although the association was not statistically significant for DENV-2 after multiple-testing correction. IgG responses showed a similar association only in DENV-1 infection. Integration of cytokine and antibody profiles further revealed distinct immune association patterns: DENV-1 showed broader associations involving viral RNA levels, inflammatory mediators, and humoral responses, whereas CHIKV displayed a more restricted pattern centered on associations between inflammatory mediators and IgM responses.
These findings reveal shared and distinct immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections and provide a comparative framework for investigating virus-associated immune regulation during acute arboviral infections.

43018279.titulo: Maternal-fetal health in arboviral diseases: clinical outcomes following prenatal dengue and chikungunya virus infections
43018279.autores: Salem GM, Tang KH, … Foo S-S (7 autores)
43018279.resumo: Revisão (Clin Microbiol Rev) sobre DENV e CHIKV na gravidez: disfunção placentária, desregulação imune materna e efeitos sobre o desenvolvimento imune fetal e neonatal; discute evasão imune viral, inflamação placentária e imunopatologia mediada por anticorpos, e o acompanhamento de gestações expostas.
43018279.resumo_original: SUMMARYArthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) are an increasingly important cause of global infectious disease, yet their effects during pregnancy and early life remain incompletely understood. In the context of declining fertility and birth rates globally, infectious threats to successful pregnancy and neonatal health warrant greater attention. Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), two of the most prevalent mosquito-borne viruses, are underrecognized contributors to maternal-fetal health. Although these infections rarely result in classical congenital syndromes, accumulating clinical, epidemiological, and experimental evidence indicates that prenatal exposure can impair placental function, drive maternal immune dysregulation, and influence fetal and neonatal immune development. This review summarizes current knowledge on the maternal, placental, and pediatric consequences of DENV and CHIKV infection during pregnancy. We outline the immunological features of the maternal-fetal interface and discuss how pregnancy-associated immune modulation shapes antiviral responses and placental homeostasis. We then review epidemiological and clinical evidence linking prenatal arboviral infection with adverse pregnancy outcomes, neonatal disease, and potential long-term neurodevelopmental effects. Mechanistic insights, including viral immune evasion, placental inflammation, and antibody-mediated immunopathology, are examined. Finally, we discuss clinical considerations for monitoring arboviral-exposed pregnancies and progenies, alongside emerging strategies to reduce maternal infection and improve neonatal outcomes.

43014495.titulo: Venezuelan equine encephalitis, Mayaro and chikungunya viruses as causative agents of febrile syndrome in Colombian patients during 2013 and 2014
43014495.autores: Rodas JD, Montoya-Ruíz C, … Weaver SC (8 autores)
43014495.resumo: Em 90 pacientes febris negativos para malária e dengue em Urabá, Colômbia (2013–2014), anticorpos contra VEEV em 28,3%, CHIKV em 5% e MAYV em 1,7%; um paciente soroconverteu para CHIKV antes do primeiro surto reconhecido; VEEV isolado e sequenciado, próximo ao subtipo ID panamenho.
43014495.resumo_original:
Colombia's tropical climate and low-altitude cities create an ideal environment where mosquito-borne diseases can thrive. During 2013-2014, dengue was the most diagnosed cause of febrile syndrome. However, other viruses like Venezuelan equine encephalitis (VEEV), Mayaro (MAYV), and chikungunya viruses (CHIKV) were also present, and their true prevalence was likely underestimated due to limited surveillance.
We conducted a cross-sectional study involving 90 febrile malaria- and dengue-negative patients from the Urabá region. For each patient, we collected both acute and convalescent serum samples, which were analyzed to detect antibodies against VEEV, CHIKV, and MAYV. Additionally, we attempted virus isolation from the acute-phase serum samples.
We found that antibodies against VEEV were present in 28.3% of samples, CHIKV antibodies were detected in 5%, and MAYV antibodies in 1.7%. Notably, one patient seroconverted against CHIKV even before the first outbreak was recognized in Colombia in 2014. Furthermore, we isolated and fully sequenced VEEV, and our analysis revealed a close phylogenetic relationship with subtype ID Panamanian strains.
This study highlights the need to consider arboviruses beyond just dengue (DENV), when evaluating febrile illness in Colombia. The detection of VEEV and CHIKV, even before they were officially recognized as significant public health threats in this region, underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and diagnostic capabilities.

43015982.titulo: Heterogeneous Permissiveness of Chicken Cells and Tissues to Oropouche Viruses
43015982.autores: Limonta D, Salas-Quinchucua C, … Osorio JE (7 autores)
43015982.resumo: Fibroblastos embrionários e explantes de fígado, coração e pulmão de galinha são infectados por cepas de OROV da América do Sul, incluindo o novo rearranjo; propõe modelo aviário para determinantes de infecção e transmissão.
43015982.resumo_original: Massive outbreaks of a reassortant Oropouche virus (OROV) spread across Latin America and the Caribbean in 2023-2025. OROV is a reemerging arbovirus belonging to the trisegmented RNA peribunyavirus family. Viral transmission occurs in sylvatic and urban cycles involving humans and other vertebrates with Culicoides biting midges as the main vector in urban settings. Anti-OROV antibodies have been found in domestic and wild birds in Brazilian OROV-endemic areas. However, no studies exist on the permissiveness of OROV in avian models, and the contribution of birds to the OROV spread remains largely unexplored. Our research indicates that chicken embryonic fibroblasts and chicken tissue explants from the liver, heart, and lung are selectively infected by OROV strains isolated by our group in South America, including the novel OROV reassortant. This work contributes to the development of avian models to investigate new determinants in the infection and transmission of an important arbovirus in the Americas.

resumo_blocos.resultados: Fibroblastos e explantes teciduais específicos exibiram permissividade heterogênea e seletiva às cepas sul-americanas e ao reassortante de OROV, estabelecendo um modelo aviário ex vivo reprodutível.

43021958.titulo: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the immune response to CHIKV infection
43021958.autores: Huang P, Wang H, … Pan W (10 autores)
43021958.resumo: scRNA-seq de PBMC de 29 pacientes com CHIKV agudo e 10 controles, com pseudobulk por doador e validação por qPCR e ELISA.
43021958.resumo_original:
The Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, is responsible for acute febrile illness and severe polyarthralgia. Although both innate and adaptive immune responses influence the disease outcomes, the detailed cellular immunopathogenesis of CHIKV in peripheral blood is not yet fully elucidated.
We profiled PBMCs from 29 patients with acute CHIKV infection and 10 controls via single-cell RNA sequencing. Between-group analyses treated donors as biological replicates, incorporating pseudobulk differential expression analysis as well as donor-level comparisons of pathway scores and cell proportions. Orthogonal validation was performed using qPCR and ELISA, and an exploratory analysis was conducted on a publicly available DENV dataset.
Interferon-response signatures were upregulated across the majority of PBMC populations, with particularly prominent signals observed in monocytes and NK cells. Differences in relative cell composition were detected in descriptive statistics, but did not retain statistical significance after donor-level multiple testing correction. B-cell immunoglobulin isotypes varied across cell subsets, and their transcripts did not allow determination of antigen specificity. Cross-study analysis of DENV did not support the quantitative conclusion that the CHIKV-induced immune response is stronger.
Acute CHIKV infection is associated with a broad interferon-stimulated transcriptional program in PBMCs. Conclusions drawn from cross-sectional and cross-study comparisons require cautious interpretation.

resumo_blocos.racional: A febre Chikungunya (CHIKV) produz poliartralgia incapacitante, porém faltavam perfis transcriptômicos de célula única em humanos com controle rigoroso de replicação biológica por doador para distinguir mudanças reais da imunidade sistêmica de artefatos estatísticos entre indivíduos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Sequenciamento de RNA de célula única (scRNA-seq) em células mononucleares de sangue periférico (PBMCs) de 29 pacientes com infecção aguda por CHIKV versus 10 controles saudáveis, usando modelagem pseudobulk por doador, validação ortogonal por qPCR e ELISA e análise exploratória comparativa com conjunto público de Dengue (DENV).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Assinaturas gênicas estimuladas por interferon (ISGs) mostraram-se fortemente induzidas na maioria das populações de PBMCs, sobretudo em monócitos e células NK. Contudo, diferenças aparentes nas proporções celulares e na comparação quantitativa frente a DENV perderam significância estatística após correção estrita para múltiplos testes em nível de doador.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Traz dois ganhos práticos: mapeia eixos inatos de interferon e monócitos na fase aguda de alfavírus e serve de alerta estatístico metodológico obrigatório para qualquer ensaio transcriptômico ou de citometria com múltiplos doadores/pools no LUCHM.

43033300.titulo: Systemic cytokine profiling reveals distinct pro-inflammatory signatures of arboviruses infections.
43033300.autores: Sarmento IV, Fantecelle CH, … Gomes DCO (13 autores)
43033300.resumo: Perfil de 12 citocinas em 163 pacientes com DENV1, DENV2, CHIKV e OROV: o OROV tem resposta seletiva (IL-18 e CCL2 altas, IL-1β e TNF-α baixas) e as citocinas independem da carga viral.
43033300.resumo_original: Arboviruses are a growing public health concern in tropical regions, where dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and oropouche virus (OROV) frequently co-circulate and cause overlapping clinical manifestations. In this study, we characterised the systemic inflammatory response by quantifying 12 cytokines and chemokines using a multiplex immunoassay in 163 patients with laboratory-confirmed acute arboviral infection: DENV1 (n = 28) and DENV2 (n = 39) patients without warning signs, CHIKV (n = 42) and OROV (n = 54). Thirty-one healthy controls (HC, n = 31) were also included. Clinically, arthralgia was the only feature that reliably distinguished the infections, occurring in 57.1% of CHIKV patients compared with 7.4-30.8% in the other groups, whereas fever, headache and myalgia overlapped substantially across all four. Immunologically, OROV induced a selective response with elevated IL-18 and CCL2/MCP-1 alongside reduced IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-23 and IL-17 A; DENV1 and DENV2 elicited broad activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral mediators, with DENV1 engaging a wider range of cytokines than DENV2; and CHIKV elevated IFN-α2, IFN-γ, IL-18, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and IL-17 A. Cytokine network analysis revealed virus-specific patterns of immune connectivity, with OROV showing the most coordinated cytokines and chemokine response and CHIKV the most fragmented. Circulating cytokine concentrations were largely independent of viral load across all viruses, indicating that systemic inflammation during acute arboviral infection is driven primarily by host immune activation rather than by viral replication kinetics. These findings establish distinct immunological signatures for DENV, CHIKV, and OROV that may support differential diagnosis and inform the development of pathogen-specific therapeutic strategies.

43027889.titulo: Synergistic Anti-Zika Activity of Repurposed Statin and Clofibrate Combinations: Evidence from Oleic Acid-Mediated Metabolic Complementation.
43027889.autores: Lee CD, Park SI, … Park JG (11 autores)
43027889.resumo: Combinações de estatina e clofibrato reaproveitadas com atividade sinérgica anti-Zika in vitro.
43027889.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) substantially relies on host lipid metabolism, presenting a prime target for host-directed antivirals. To identify host-directed antiviral interventions while circumventing interferon-mediated transcriptomic masking, we curated a dual-virus (dengue and ZIKV) gene signature to query the Connectivity Map. Top lipid-lowering candidates were validated using a reporter virus (rZIKV-Venus) and an authentic wild-type (WT) ZIKV in Vero E6 cells-a model deliberately selected for its interferon deficiency to isolate pure metabolic responses. Dose-response screening of 67 prioritized compounds identified atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, and clofibrate as potent ZIKV inhibitors. Statin-clofibrate combinations exhibited strong synergy, with fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) values of 0.203 (atorvastatin-clofibrate) and 0.117 (rosuvastatin-clofibrate) for the 4:1 clofibrate-to-statin ratio and an optimized selectivity index. Mechanistically, exogenous oleic acid supplementation induced significant metabolic complementation, significantly restoring both host lipid droplet (LD) abundance and ZIKV replication readouts suppressed by the dual treatment. Relative LD intensity strongly correlated with viral intensity in both models (Pearson r = 0.951 and 0.956, respectively; both p < 0.0001). These findings demonstrate that concurrent pharmacological modulation of host lipid metabolism exerts synergistic anti-ZIKV effects, highlighting highly curated transcriptomic repurposing as a mechanistic prioritization strategy for host-directed antiviral discovery.

43037222.titulo: Identification of Arboviruses and Other Viral Signatures Using Entomo-Virological Surveillance in the Santa Marta District, Colombia.
43037222.autores: Franco-Salazar JP, Quintero-Cortés P, … Usme-Ciro JA (8 autores)
43037222.resumo: Identificação de arbovírus e outras assinaturas virais por vigilância entomovirológica.
43037222.resumo_original:
Current surveillance strategies for arboviral diseases involve serological and virological study of clinical cases and characterization of presence and densities of immature and mature stages of vectors. Our objective was to establish an entomo-virological surveillance of flaviviruses and alphaviruses in urban and rural areas of the Santa Marta district, Colombia.
Mosquitoes and sandfly specimens were collected using CO2-baited CDC light, Shannon traps, and entomological nets with aspirators. Specimens belonging to every morphotype were separated and stored for processing through classical taxonomy, molecular systematics, and for virus detection using generic, specific RT-PCR methods, and DNA sequencing. Sequences were aligned through MAFFT and phylogenetic trees reconstructed through IQ-TREE.
A total of 2953 specimens were collected. Several species of vectors were identified, with Ae. aegypti and Culex sp. being predominant in both urban and rural areas. Viral detection and sequencing revealed the circulation of genotype V (American/African) of Orthoflavivirus denguei (DENV) type 1, cocirculation of lineages 1V_D.1 and 1V_D.2 with different recent origins, and presumptive cryptic circulation of Orthoflavivirus zikaense (ZIKV) based on molecular detection without sequence confirmation. Alphavirus chikungunya (CHIKV) was not detected in the tested pools during the study period. In addition, the presence of Culex flavivirus and a putative nonretroviral integrated RNA virus (NIRV) element derived from a Menghai-like flavivirus was detected in the genome of Ae. aegypti.
This study demonstrated the circulation of DENV in the vector population and provided presumptive molecular evidence of ZIKV. In-depth analysis of flavivirus-positive samples allowed the detection of the Culex flavivirus, as well as a putative NIRV element in the genome of Ae. aegypti, whose effects on vector competence and arboviruses dynamics justify further research.

43038110.titulo: Efficacy of Early Ivermectin Administration in Acute Chikungunya Virus Infection: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
43038110.autores: Chusri S, Surasombatpattana S, … Fernandez S (20 autores)
43038110.resumo: Ensaio aberto randomizado na Tailândia (127 adultos, 120 analisados) com ivermectina 400 µg/kg/dia por 3 dias, iniciada em até 72 h dos sintomas: a dor articular aguda resolveu em mediana de 3,5 contra 12 dias (aHR 3,65), a dor persistente em 1 mês caiu de 30% para 6,6% (aOR 0,08) e a depuração viral até o dia 7 foi mais rápida. Sem cegamento e com registro retrospectivo.
43038110.resumo_original:
Acute and chronic joint pain is the hallmark of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection, often progressing to debilitating persistent joint pain. No approved antiviral therapy is available. We evaluated the clinical and virological efficacy of early ivermectin administration in acute CHIKV infection.
This open-label, randomized trial enrolled and randomized 127 adult patients with acute chikungunya within 72 hours of symptom onset in Thailand. Patients were assigned (1:1) to oral ivermectin (400 µg/kg/day for 3 days) plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Before the 1-month endpoint, 7 patients were lost to follow-up, leaving a finalized complete-case cohort of 120 participants (n = 60 per arm) for primary efficacy analysis. Co-primary outcomes were time to acute joint pain clearance and the proportion of patients with persistent joint pain at 1 month.
Early ivermectin significantly accelerated acute joint pain resolution compared to controls (median 3.5 days [IQR 2, 6] vs 12.0 days [IQR 8, 35]; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 3.65, 95% CI 2.28, 5.84; p < 0.0001). Ivermectin was associated with a 92% reduction in the odds of persistent joint pain at 1 month (6.6% vs 30%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.08, 95% CI 0.03, 0.21; p < 0.0001). It also shortened fever clearance (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days; p < 0.0001) and accelerated viral clearance by day 7.
Early ivermectin intervention within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly accelerates clinical recovery, suppresses viral replication, and profoundly reduces persistent joint pain at 1 month. These findings position ivermectin as a promising, scalable therapeutic strategy against CHIKV.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06259383 (Retrospectively registered on February 20, 2024 prior to thawing bio-banked samples for sequential assays, laboratory assay and final analysis).

43054615.titulo: Chikungunya virus: from global emergence to immunopathology and therapeutic frontiers.
43054615.autores: Li D, Wang Q, … Zhang S (4 autores)
43054615.resumo: Revisão sobre chikungunya, da emergência global à imunopatologia e às frentes terapêuticas (Front Immunol). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43054615.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, has transitioned from an endemic pathogen to a global public health threat. In May 2026, the World Health Organization's second rapid risk assessment classified the global public health risk of CHIKV transmission as moderate. Although two vaccines (IXCHIQ® and VIMKUNYA®) have been authorized in selected countries, no antiviral therapy has been approved, and supportive care remains the mainstay of clinical management. We synthesize current knowledge of CHIKV epidemiology, replication, host immune signaling, and immune evasion, together with the developmental landscape of vaccines and antivirals. Through a critical appraisal of available evidence, we propose a hierarchical evidence-weighting framework that distinguishes in vivo mechanistic findings, cell-line observations, and human validation, and we highlight the stage-dependent functions of cytokines. Finally, we outline unresolved questions in chronicity, antiviral development, next-generation vaccine design and optimization, and cross-regional public health coordination, with particular emphasis on bridging the evidence gap between animal models and human infection.

43052209.resumo_original: To assess the circulation of Oropouche, Mayaro, West Nile, and St. Louis encephalitis viruses, we tested samples from 824 patients with acute febrile illness, 3,484 mosquitoes, and 113 nonhuman primates from northern Minas Gerais, Brazil. All samples were negative for dengue, Chikungunya, and Zika virus. One imported Oropouche virus infection was detected.

43053130.titulo: Emerging orthobunyaviruses: genomic diversity, reassortment, and expanding public health risks.
43053130.autores: Sankhe S, Ndiaye NA, … Diagne MM (4 autores)
43053130.resumo: Revisão de ortobunyavírus emergentes: diversidade genômica, rearranjo e riscos de saúde pública (Virol J); Oropouche é um ortobunyavírus. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43053130.resumo_original: Orthobunyaviruses (family Peribunyaviridae) represent one of the most diverse groups of arboviruses, infecting humans, livestock, and wildlife worldwide. Despite their broad geographic distribution and ecological complexity, most orthobunyaviruses remain poorly characterized, with limited understanding of their genomic diversity, transmission dynamics, and pathogenic potential. While research has focused on clinically recognized viruses such as Oropouche virus (OROV), La Crosse virus (LACV), Jamestown Canyon virus (JCV), and Schmallenberg virus (SBV), numerous neglected lineages like Ilesha virus (ILEV), Bwamba virus (BWAV), and Ingwavuma virus (INGV) continue to circulate silently, particularly in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Recent outbreaks of OROV in South America and the emergence of SBV in Europe highlight their capacity for rapid spread and significant public and animal health impact. The segmented negative-sense RNA genome of orthobunyaviruses enables reassortment, a key evolutionary mechanism that drives diversification and may generate strains with altered virulence or host range. In addition, climate change, environmental disruption, and increased human-animal-vector interactions may facilitate expansion into new regions. This review synthesizes current knowledge on taxonomy, evolution, ecology, clinical features, diagnostics, and surveillance strategies. We emphasize the importance of integrated genomic monitoring and One Health approaches to strengthen preparedness against emerging and neglected orthobunyaviruses.

resumo_blocos.racional: Ortobuniavírus da família Peribunyaviridae possuem genoma de RNA segmentado de fita negativa altamente propenso a rearranjo genético (reassortment), mas além do Oropouche grande parte de sua diversidade viral permanece negligenciada na vigilância global.

resumo_blocos.resultados: Sintetiza como eventos de rearranjo entre segmentos genômicos podem gerar cepas com virulência alterada ou ampliação de espectro de vetores e hospedeiros, explicando a rápida expansão recente de OROV na América do Sul e SBV na Europa.

43044932.titulo: Serum untargeted metabolomics reveals infection-associated metabolic alterations in chikungunya, dengue, and influenza A virus infections.
43044932.autores: Ouyang F, Chen X, … He M (8 autores)
43044932.resumo: Metabolômica sérica por LC-MS em pacientes com chikungunya, dengue e influenza A mostrou alterações amplas frente a controles (319, 300 e 295 características diferenciais em modo positivo), com predomínio de lipídios e aminoácidos. Coorte pequena, de um centro e sem validação independente.
43044932.resumo_original:
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and influenza A virus (IAV) infections may present with overlapping febrile symptoms during the early clinical phase. Routine laboratory tests provide useful clinical information but do not fully capture the circulating metabolic alterations associated with different viral infections. This study aimed to characterize serum metabolic profiles in CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics.
In this comparative cross-sectional study, serum samples from patients with CHIKV, DENV, or IAV infection and healthy controls were analyzed using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Data were acquired in both positive and negative electrospray ionization modes, and the datasets were processed to characterize infection-associated metabolic alterations. Quality-control assessment, principal component analysis, orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis, differential metabolite screening with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway classification, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed.
Thousands of metabolic features were detected across positive and negative ion mode datasets, and annotated features were retained for downstream comparative analyses. Principal component analysis revealed group-dependent metabolic clustering with partial overlap between healthy controls and viral infection groups. Compared with healthy controls, 319, 300, and 295 differential metabolic features were identified in the CHIKV, DENV, and IAV groups, respectively, in positive ion mode, whereas 52, 40, and 33 differential features were identified in negative ion mode. Downregulated features predominated in the positive-ion comparisons, while the direction of metabolic alterations varied across groups in negative ion mode. KEGG pathway classification showed that differential metabolites were mapped to several major categories, including lipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, metabolism of cofactors and vitamins, xenobiotics biodegradation and metabolism, and chemical structure transformation maps. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis within the discovery cohort identified multiple metabolites with high discriminatory performance for distinguishing viral infection groups from healthy controls, although these findings were not independently validated. Additional mode-specific analyses further characterized shared differential metabolic features, their directional changes, and the distribution of candidate metabolites with high AUC values.
CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections were associated with broad serum metabolic alterations compared with healthy controls. The CHIKV-versus-control comparison yielded the largest number of altered metabolic features in the current dataset, although this observation should be interpreted cautiously because of unequal sampling proportions and the absence of direct comparisons between infection groups. Given the relatively small sample size, single-center and single-outbreak design, and lack of an independent validation cohort, the candidate metabolites identified in this study should be regarded as exploratory and require validation in larger independent cohorts and targeted metabolomic assays.

43057551.titulo: Semi-field efficacy of conspecific egg- and larva-derived chemical cues for manipulating Aedes aegypti oviposition.
43057551.autores: Mulatier M, Loïal A, … Vega-Rúa A (5 autores)
43057551.resumo: Eficácia em semicampo de pistas químicas de ovos e larvas coespecíficas para manipular oviposição de Ae. aegypti.
43057551.resumo_original: Baited traps targeting gravid Aedes aegypti females are a promising tool for vector surveillance and control. Conspecific immature stages are known to influence oviposition-site selection and several egg and/or larvae derived compounds have been identified as potential oviposition cues under laboratory conditions. However, their performance under field conditions remains poorly understood, limiting their application in baited mass-trapping strategies. Using two-choice oviposition assays in outdoor cages, we evaluated under semi-field conditions the efficacy of five Ae. aegypti eggs and/or larvae associated compounds to influence oviposition in this mosquito species: (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid, pentadecanoic acid, n-heneicosane, palmitoleic acid and dodecanoic acid. An infusion of Ae. aegypti larvae was also tested under these conditions as positive control. We identified (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid as a potential volatile oviposition mediator, showing a trend toward increased oviposition (57 % of eggs received; oviposition attractivity index (OAI) = 0.14). For this compound, sticky-screen assays showed significant attraction compared to the control, excluding its detection by contact cues and suggesting its potential spatial activity to attract mosquitoes (attractivity index = 0.45). In contrast, n-heneicosane, and dodecanoic acid induced neutral oviposition responses (OAI = -0.03 and -0.1, respectively), whereas pentadecanoic and palmitoleic acids induced a trend toward slight oviposition deterrence in our settings (OAI = -0.17 and -0.20, respectively). Although previous laboratory or field evidence supporting their efficiency, our results reveal marked discrepancies between laboratory and semi-field behavioral responses. These findings emphasize the need for semi-field and field trials to assess mosquito semiochemicals, where long-range attraction can be distinguished from short-range oviposition stimulation, before considering their operational use in vector surveillance and control.

resumo_blocos.racional: Semioquímicos derivados de ovos e larvas coespecíficos modulam a escolha do sítio de oviposição de Aedes aegypti em laboratório, mas sua real eficácia comportamental em condições de semicampo permanece incerta para orientar armadilhas atrativas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Em gaiolas externas de semicampo, ensaios de oviposição de dupla escolha avaliaram cinco compostos associados a ovos e larvas de Ae. aegypti — ácido (Z)-5-dodecenoico, ácido pentadecanoico, n-heneicosano, ácido palmitoleico e ácido dodecanoico — frente a infusão larval como controle positivo, além de testes com tela adesiva (sticky-screen) para distinguir atração espacial de estímulo por contato.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O ácido (Z)-5-dodecenoico mostrou tendência a elevar a oviposição (57% dos ovos; índice OAI = 0,14) e atração espacial significativa em tela adesiva sem contato (índice de atratividade = 0,45). Em contraste, n-heneicosano (OAI = -0,03) e ácido dodecanoico (OAI = -0,10) foram neutros, e os ácidos pentadecanoico e palmitoleico tenderam a leve dissuasão (OAI = -0,17 e -0,20), evidenciando discrepâncias marcantes entre ensaios laboratoriais e de semicampo.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Reforça a importância de validar sinais lipídicos e ácidos graxos mediadores de oviposição em condições próximas às reais e de separar atração olfativa de longo alcance do estímulo de postura por contato.

43061087.titulo: Insecticide Resistance Dynamics in Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) from Different Habitats in the Punjab, Pakistan.
43061087.autores: Hayat M, Nasir S, … Sultana S (4 autores)
43061087.resumo: Dinâmica de resistência a inseticida em Ae. aegypti de habitats distintos no Punjab (Paquistão).
43061087.resumo_original:
The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the most important vector of many viral diseases, such as dengue virus. Thus, various chemical insecticides are being used to control this vector. On the other hand, due to the intensive blind use of chemical insecticides, mosquito vectors are rapidly developing resistance against most of them.
The present study was conducted during 2024-25 to explore the development of resistance in three Ae. aegypti strains with a previous history of insecticidal records compared with Laboratory (LAB) and Tidiwala (TDW) strains collected from localities (Tidiwala and rural barren land) with no or minimal use of insecticides. Resistance development was recorded by utilizing five commonly used insecticides against mosquitoes in Punjab, Pakistan.
Results showed that deltamethrin was the best during 2024 when compared with alpha-cypermethrin, temephos, lambda-cyhalothrin and Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis. All field-collected strains revealed significant resistance to the tested insecticides compared with LAB and TDW strains. The same findings were reflected in the enzyme spectrum (glutathione-S-transferase, mixed-function oxidases, esterase, and acetylcholinesterase).
These results may help to devise a comprehensive future strategy for mosquito control through selective insecticides by limiting the spread of resistance.

resumo_blocos.racional: O emprego intensivo de inseticidas químicos contra Aedes aegypti tem selecionado rapidamente resistência múltipla, tornando essencial monitorar o perfil de susceptibilidade em populações de campo frente a diferentes classes químicas, larvicidas bacterianos e enzimas detoxificantes.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Durante 2024–2025 no Punjab (Paquistão), três linhagens de campo de Ae. aegypti provenientes de áreas com histórico de controle químico foram comparadas à linhagem suscetível de laboratório (LAB) e à linhagem Tidiwala (TDW) de área rural sem ou com mínimo uso de inseticidas. Avaliou-se a resposta a cinco inseticidas (deltametrina, alfa-cipermetrina, temefós, lambda-cialotrina e Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) juntamente com o espectro enzimático de glutationa S-transferase (GST), oxidases de função mista (MFO), esterases e acetilcolinesterase (AChE).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Todas as populações de campo oriundas de áreas tratadas exibiram resistência significativa aos inseticidas avaliados em comparação às linhagens LAB e TDW, sendo a deltametrina o agente com maior eficácia relativa em 2024 frente a alfa-cipermetrina, temefós, lambda-cialotrina e B. thuringiensis israelensis. O padrão fenotípico de resistência refletiu-se nas alterações das atividades de GST, MFO, esterases e acetilcolinesterase.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta vigilância de resistência metabólica em Aedes aegypti (GST, MFO, esterases, AChE) ao monitoramento de eficácia de bioinseticidas como B. thuringiensis israelensis, dialogando com os programas de vetores e bioinseticidas do LUCHM.

43059912.titulo: Evolutionarily distinct dengue virus type 2 with a unique type-specific neutralization determinant.
43059912.autores: Mayer SV, Winkelmann ER, … Katzelnick LC (16 autores)
43059912.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
43059912.resumo: Preprint: DENV-2 evolutivamente distinto, com determinante de neutralização tipo-específico próprio. Relevante para vigilância sorológica; sem ângulo de vetor.
43059912.resumo_original:
Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes.
Dengue viruses that are most distantly related to the four canonical serotypes originated in Borneo, suggesting this island is a possible site of early dengue virus diversification as well as continued evolution within an unidentified host species. Here, we find divergent strain QML-22 from Borneo shares many neutralizing epitopes with DENV2 but has a distinct epitope in an important region affecting potent DENV2 neutralization. This region of the virus also is variable within DENV2 and in other DENV serotypes, highlighting an important site of dengue virus diversification and evolution. The spillover threat of viruses like QML-22 remains unknown, but ecological changes in Borneo may increase this risk.

resumo_blocos.racional: Linhagens silvestres divergentes do vírus da Dengue posicionadas entre os quatro sorotipos canônicos na filogenia levantam a questão de quanto diferenças genotípicas implicam escape antigênico frente à neutralização sorotípica clássica.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores caracterizaram antigenicamente a cepa divergente QML-22 de Bornéu (próxima a DENV-2) por cartografia antigênica, ensaios de neutralização com soros humanos endêmicos de DENV1–4, anticorpo monoclonal potente anti-DENV-2 (3F9) dirigido ao domínio I da proteína de envelope (E), depleção heteróloga de antissoros de primatas não humanos infectados com QML-22 ou com a cepa de referência DENV-2 S16803 e análises evolutivas de pressão seletiva sobre epítopos neutralizantes.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Embora QML-22 tenha se agrupado com cepas globais de DENV-2 no mapa antigênico, foi menos neutralizada por soros contra DENV-2 endêmico e melhor neutralizada por soros de DENV-1, 3 e 4 do que outras cepas DENV-2. QML-22 exibiu um agrupamento de resíduos distintos no domínio I da proteína E que reduziu em >1000 vezes a neutralização pelo anticorpo 3F9, cujo epítopo mostrou pressão seletiva relaxada na análise evolutiva; ensaios de depleção heteróloga confirmaram que a neutralização homóloga depende de epítopos distintos.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Relevante para a vigilância de diversidade antigênica de flavivírus e ensaios com arbovírus em Aedes, mostrando que mutações concentradas no domínio I da proteína E podem gerar escape acentuado a anticorpos neutralizantes específicos mesmo dentro do agrupamento DENV-2.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Verificar se variantes de domínio I da proteína E com perfil antigênico intermediário mantêm eficiência de ligação e entrada no intestino médio de Aedes aegypti.

43009000.titulo: In vitro tolerance and biotransformation of temephos and deltamethrin by gut bacteria Chryseobacterium gleum and Cedecea neteri isolated from Aedes aegypti.
43009000.autores: Viafara-Campo JD, Vivero-Gómez RJ, … Cadavid-Restrepo G (5 autores)
43009000.resumo: Bactérias intestinais isoladas de Ae. aegypti de Caquetá (Colômbia) toleram e transformam inseticidas: Chryseobacterium gleum reduziu o temefós em 76% em 72 h (cinco metabólitos) e Cedecea neteri reduziu a deltametrina em 75% em 24 h.
43009000.resumo_original: The progressive loss of insecticide susceptibility in Aedes aegypti compromises the control of this arbovirus vector. The mosquito gut microbiota may modulate susceptibility and contribute to insecticide degradation. This study evaluated the in vitro tolerance of gut bacteria isolated from Ae. aegypti populations exposed to temephos and deltamethrin in Caquetá (Colombia) and their capacity to transform these insecticides. Growth and growth kinetics were assessed in minimal medium in the presence of commercial insecticide formulations. Biotransformation was investigated by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-positive electrospray ionization-Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC-(+)ESI-Orbitrap/HRMS) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), which allowed the tentative identification of metabolites, whereas the reduction of the parent compounds was estimated from chromatographic peak areas relative to abiotic controls. All strains grew in Luria-Bertani medium, but only three showed consistent growth in M9 minimal medium with the insecticides. Although Enterobacter asburiae P2D2C1 was also analyzed by GC-MS with deltamethrin, its profiles did not allow a reliable characterization of products; the final characterization therefore focused on Chryseobacterium gleum P31D2 (temephos) and Cedecea neteri P2HD2 (deltamethrin). After 72 h, C. gleum P31D2 reduced the temephos signal by 76.05% relative to the abiotic control, and five metabolites were tentatively identified, including 4,4'-thiodiphenol, 4,4'-sulfinyldiphenol, and temephos sulfoxide. C. neteri P2HD2 reduced the relative abundance of deltamethrin by 75.39% over 24 h versus 8.52% in the abiotic control (net biotransformation, 66.87%), and four metabolites were tentatively identified, including 3-phenoxybenzaldehyde and 3-phenoxyphenylacetonitrile. Hypothetical metabolic pathways are proposed. These in vitro findings provide a basis for future studies on the role of gut bacteria in insecticide biotransformation.

43012655.titulo: ROS-dependent phosphorylation of insulin receptor and insulin receptor substrate during pupal diapause development in the cotton bollworm, Helicoverpa armigera.
43012655.autores: Su Z, Yang Y, … Jiang S (5 autores)
43012655.resumo: Em Helicoverpa armigera, p-InR e p-IRS sobem nos cérebros de pupas destinadas à diapausa, com ERK e Akt; ROS age a montante da fosforilação (revertida por eliminadores de ROS) e p-ERK associa-se a ubiquitinação global.
43012655.resumo_original: Insect diapause is a critical adaptive strategy characterized by developmental arrest and enhanced stress tolerance, orchestrated by intricate molecular networks. The insulin signaling pathway, which governs growth, metabolism, and stress responses, has been implicated in diapause regulation. However, the precise roles of insulin receptor (InR) and insulin receptor substrate (IRS) in modulating pupal diapause remain incompletely understood, particularly in the economically important pest Helicoverpa armigera. Here, we show that InR and IRS are associated with pupal diapause development through redox-sensitive phosphorylation cascades. Temporal profiling revealed a marked upregulation of phosphorylated InR (p-InR) and IRS (p-IRS) in diapause-destined pupal brains, concomitant with elevated phosphorylation of Akt (p-Akt) and ERK (p-ERK). Functional validation in Helicoverpa zea (HzAm1) cells, via overexpression and RNA interference (RNAi), showed that IRS positively regulates Akt and ERK signaling. Further mechanistic studies indicated that reactive oxygen species (ROS) act upstream of the phosphorylation of InR, IRS, Akt, and ERK in vitro and in vivo; these effects were reversible upon ROS scavenging. Further investigations revealed that increased p-ERK was associated with global protein ubiquitination, suggesting this kinase as a key regulator of proteasomal degradation in diapause development. Our findings delineate a ROS-InR-IRS-Akt/ERK signaling framework associated with diapause development and proteostatic regulation in H. armigera, thereby advancing our understanding of insect diapause biology and providing candidate molecular targets for future pest-management interventions.

43007365.titulo: CRISPR interference-based gene silencing in insects: from functional genomics to prospective insect-pest management applications.
43007365.autores: Saini A, Sharma N, … Thakur AK (6 autores)
43007365.resumo: Revisão de CRISPRi (dCas9 + sgRNA) em insetos, comparado a RNAi e CRISPR/Cas9: supressão transcricional reversível, sem quebra de DNA, já demonstrada em mosquitos vetores.
43007365.resumo_original: Insect-pests remain a major constraint to global agriculture, causing yield losses through direct feeding and transmission of phytopathogens. Chemical pesticides and transgenic crops expressing Bacillus thuringiensis toxins have shown initial success; however, their use is increasingly constrained by resistance, non-target effects, environmental contamination and regulatory restrictions. Although RNA interference (RNAi) presents a targeted and eco-friendly alternative, it is limited by species variability, rapid double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) degradation, inconsistent silencing and off-target effects. Nuclease-active Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats/CRISPR-associated protein 9 (CRISPR/Cas9) enables genetic editing, but its irreversible genome modifications raise ethical, ecological and regulatory concerns. CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) offers a programmable approach for sequence-specific, reversible transcriptional suppression without inducing double-strand DNA breaks. Using catalytically inactive Cas9 (dead Cas9 or dCas9) -guided by single-guide RNA (sgRNA), CRISPRi inhibits transcription initiation or elongation while maintaining genomic integrity. Experimental studies in insect models, including disease-vector mosquitoes, have demonstrated effective suppression of coding and non-coding genes, supporting CRISPRi as a functional genomics tool. This review discusses CRISPRi mechanisms, applications, advantages and limitations in insects, comparing it with RNAi and CRISPR/Cas9. Overall, current evidences indicate that CRISPRi is a precise and non-mutagenic platform for insect-pest management, particularly where controlled, reversible and species-specific gene regulation is desirable. However, its application in agricultural pest management remains an extrapolation from functional-genomics studies and requires validation in pest species under whole-organism and field-relevant conditions.

43015033.titulo: Mosquito vector abundance, spatial distribution and arboviral transmission risk in high-traffic cross-border zones of Tanzania
43015033.autores: Kakulu R, Kemibala E, … Kimaro EG (12 autores)
43015033.resumo: Levantamento entomológico em Mutukula e Namanga (Tanzânia), out–nov/2024: 6.952 mosquitos, 84,7% Cx. quinquefasciatus, 10,0% Ae. aegypti e 5,3% An. gambiae s.l.; Aedes e An. funestus s.l. mais abundantes até 400 m da fronteira; uma fêmea de Ae. albopictus; 4 de 10 povoados com índices larvários acima do limiar.
43015033.resumo_original: Arboviral diseases remain a major global public health challenge because mosquito vectors continue to expand their geographical range through increasing international travel, urbanization and climate change. This study aimed to assess the abundance, spatial distribution and larval indices of mosquito vectors of medical importance in a cross-border setting. A comprehensive entomological survey, using multiple collection techniques, was conducted between October and November 2024 at high-traffic cross-border zones at Mutukula ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Uganda and Namanga ground crossing connecting Tanzania and Kenya. Adult mosquitoes were collected using BG-Pro traps, CDC light traps and Prokopack aspirators, while larval surveys were conducted through cross-sectional household inspections of potential breeding habitats. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, and associations between variables were assessed using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Binomial and Poisson regression models were used to identify factors associated with mosquito abundance and breeding site occurrence, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 6952 mosquitoes were collected, comprising Culex quinquefasciatus (84.7%, n = 5895), Aedes aegypti (10.0%, n = 689) and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (5.3%, n = 369). Significantly higher abundance of Aedes spp. and Anopheles funestus s.l was recorded in hamlets located within 400 m of the international border (p < 0.0001), whereas Culex quinquefasciatus predominated in hamlets situated beyond 400 m from the border (χ2 = 1938, p < 0.000001). One female Aedes albopictus was detected among the adult Aedes collections, suggesting the potential introduction of this invasive vector. Four of the 10 hamlets surveyed had larval indices exceeding recommended thresholds, indicating an elevated risk of arboviral transmission. This study revealed a high prevalence of Aedes aegypti within the cross-border buffer zone and a broader distribution of Culex species beyond this zone. These findings underscore the urgent need for sustained vector control interventions and strengthened entomological surveillance and control beyond the International Health Regulations (2005) as amended in 2024, which recommended a 400 m buffer zone at points of entry to mitigate the risk of arboviral disease transmission and potential epidemics.

resumo_blocos.racional: Zonas fronteiriças de alto fluxo migratório atuam como corredores de introdução e expansão geográfica de Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus e arboviroses.

43022695.titulo: Detection ofandthroughout the life cycle of Colombian populations of: evidence of potential vertical transmission
43022695.autores: Yepes-Acevedo AJ, Lopez-Rivera N, … Saldamando-Benjumea CI (5 autores)
43022695.resumo: Detecção de endossimbiontes ao longo do ciclo de vida de populações colombianas de Spodoptera frugiperda, com indício de transmissão vertical.
43022695.resumo_original:
Spodoptera frugiperda, commonly known as the fall armyworm (FAW), is a pest of great economic importance in corn. The species has recently expanded from the Western Hemisphere to Africa, Asia, and Oceania, increasing its global impact. FAW has diverged into two strains, corn and rice, which differ in genetics, reproductive isolation, resistance to insecticides and to Bacillus thuringiensis, and, more recently found, in their microbiota. Endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus and Spiroplasma have been detected using next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the 16S rRNA gene. However, information on additional endosymbionts and their transmission dynamics remains limited. Therefore, the objectives of this study were to (i) evaluate the presence of endosymbionts such as Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia as well as the intracellular parasite Microsporidia, throughout the life cycle of both strains of S. frugiperda, (ii) assess their potential vertical transmission, and (iii) examine possible associations between these symbionts and life-history traits in this insect.
Larvae were sampled from corn and rice fields in central and eastern Colombia. Laboratory colonies of the corn and rice strains of S. frugiperda were maintained under controlled conditions. Strain identity was confirmed using diagnostic molecular markers (MspI, SacI, FR). Within each strain, one-to-one crosses were performed to construct life cycle tables and estimate life-history traits components. DNA was subsequently extracted from parental individuals and from eggs, larvae, pupae, and adults. Following extraction, conventional and real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using an intercalating dye were conducted to identify the genera Arsenophonus, Cardinium, Spiroplasma, and Wolbachia, the intracellular parasite Microsporidia and positive amplifications were confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
Arsenophonus was detected exclusively in the corn strain using conventional PCR and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Additionally, Spiroplasma was detected in both strains using real-time PCR using an intercalating dye. The detection of these endosymbionts across developmental stages is consistent with, vertical transmission. Differences in life-history traits components were observed between the two strains, but no clear association was detected between these differences and the presence of either endosymbiont under the conditions evaluated. These results highlight the need for further studies to evaluate the potential role of endosymbionts in the biology of this pest and to further on to better understand their transmission dynamics and possible ecological interactions.

43031381.titulo: Lipid metabolic reprogramming in honey bee response to Hafnia alvei infection: insights from temporal transcriptome analysis.
43031381.autores: Liu J, Wu Y, … Luo S (5 autores)
43031381.resumo: No corpo gorduroso de abelha, a infecção por Hafnia alvei induz primeiro lipídios e depois genes imunes; a microbiota viva antecipa e reforça a remodelação lipídica e imune em relação a bactéria morta ou abelha livre de germes.
43031381.resumo_original: Host defense against pathogen infection relies on coordinated immune activation and metabolic reprogramming, but how these processes are temporally organized in insects remains poorly understood. Here, time-series transcriptomic analyses of honey bee fat bodies revealed that Hafnia alvei infection induced a stage-dependent response. Genes involved in carbohydrate, glycerolipid, and glycerophospholipid metabolism were rapidly induced after infection, whereas immune signaling pathways and antimicrobial peptide genes were progressively upregulated later. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis further revealed positive correlations between lipid metabolism-related genes and immune genes, indicating tight coordination between metabolic and immune responses. Comparisons among germ-free, heat-killed bacteria-colonized, and conventionally colonized bees demonstrated that live gut microbiota promoted earlier and stronger lipid metabolic remodeling and immune activation, whereas heat-killed bacteria triggered delayed responses compared to live bacteria colonization. These findings indicate lipid metabolic reprogramming as a key component of honey bee defense against H. alvei and show that gut microbiota enhances host resistance by modulating metabolic-immune coordination.

43023714.titulo: boosts host tolerance and mitigates virulence ofspecies in.
43023714.autores: Mendiola SY, Safir WO, Vogel KJ (3 autores)
43023714.resumo: Em inseto com simbionte, a presença do simbionte reduz a virulência de cepas patogênicas e a ordem e a via de inoculação mudam o desfecho, usando indivíduos aposimbióticos.
43023714.resumo_original: Insects contend with myriad microbes throughout their lives. These microbial interactions, ranging from beneficial to pathogenic, have important consequences for the insect host, and simultaneous infection with multiple microbes is the norm. We are increasingly aware of how within-host interactions between the endogenous microbiota and invading pathogens can influence host infection outcomes. In this study, we examined how symbiont-pathogen interactions influence pathogen infection in the insect Rhodnius prolixus and how virulence can vary drastically with the context of infection, including cases where the endogenous microbiota is disrupted. Leveraging our ability to rear symbiont-free, or aposymbiotic, individuals, we first challenged symbiotic and aposymbiotic R. prolixus with three Serratia strains of varying virulence (two virulent Serratia marcescens strains and one avirulent Serratia ureilytica strain). We further altered the context of infection by varying the order of symbiont and pathogen colonization, as well as the method of inoculation (i.e., ingestion vs injection). Within R. prolixus, we showed a strong mitigating effect on virulence with the presence of Rhodococcus rhodnii, a well-established R. prolixus symbiont, despite high Serratia burdens. Virulence varied not only by Serratia strain but also by host species, with R. prolixus being particularly susceptible to infection among the four insect species tested. Our findings corroborate the importance of context in determining pathogen virulence, with symbiont presence, in particular, playing a key role in the outcome of pathogen infection for R. prolixus.IMPORTANCEThroughout their lives, insects encounter many bacteria, some beneficial and some detrimental. Increasingly, we are aware of how resident bacteria in the insect gut impact the ability of pathogenic microbes to establish and cause harm. Understanding the factors that underlie the specificity of these interactions is important in furthering our ability to leverage pathogenic microbes for the control of insect pests. This study focuses on the kissing bug, Rhodnius prolixus, a medically important insect that transmits Chagas disease. We tested the impact of different conditions in determining the virulence of the pathogen Serratia marcescens. Kissing bugs suffered high levels of mortality when infected with Serratia, particularly compared to other insect species. We determined that the presence of a beneficial bacterium (Rhodococcus rhodnii) in the kissing bug mitigated the ill effects of infection with Serratia. Early establishment of the beneficial bacteria was key to maximizing this effect.

43026029.titulo: Integrated population genomics and phenotypic analyses reveal geographic structure and signatures of recent positive-selection underlying insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from The Gambia, West Africa.
43026029.autores: Seck F, Mwangi JN, … Assogba BS (16 autores)
43026029.resumo: Genômica de populações de Anopheles arabiensis na Gâmbia: resistência a piretroides e DDT (Vgsc-L995S/F), variação em número de cópias de P450 e carboxilesterases e regiões sob seleção.
43026029.resumo_original: Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. We observed signals of population structure between coastal and inland An. arabiensis populations in The Gambia, indicating restricted gene flow likely influenced by environmental variation. Pyrethroid and DDT resistance were widespread. However, the prevalence of both phenotypic and genetic insecticide resistance differed between coastal and inland populations. For instance, the Vgsc-L995S and Vgsc-L995F substitutions conferring pyrethroid and DDT resistance were more frequent in coastal populations and were associated with markedly higher phenotypic resistance to these insecticides. We also identified increased frequencies of copy number variation at Cytochrome P450 (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1) and carboxylesterase (Coeae2-7 g) metabolic resistance markers in coastal An. arabiensis. Some observed gene amplifications were unique to Gambian coastal populations, suggesting their independent evolution. Furthermore, we found evidence of genomic regions under recent positive selection on chromosomes 2L:37,282,152-37,298,202 and 3R:28,590,243-28,602,280 with more pronounced selection signals observed among coastal populations. Coastal populations of An. arabiensis displayed an enrichment of resistance alleles, suggesting a localised pressure driving the evolution, selection and spread of resistance mechanisms. These findings underscore the importance of genomic surveillance in concert with bioassays to inform targeted vector control interventions. They also highlight the need to identify the sources and impacts of insecticide pressure acting on recently detected genomic regions under selection in the coastal regions of The Gambia.

43034830.titulo: Ion regulatory mechanisms supporting hypersaline tolerance in the coastal rock pool mosquito.
43034830.autores: Chiang J, Khodikian E, … Matthews BJ (7 autores)
43034830.resumo: Genoma em escala cromossômica do mosquito de poça costeira e caracterização da glândula de sal larval, com famílias gênicas de transporte iônico.
43034830.resumo_original: The coastal rock pool mosquito, Aedes togoi, is a remarkable example of a saline-tolerant mosquito. While most mosquitoes are obligate freshwater breeders, Ae. togoi larvae and pupae inhabit coastal rock pools that span freshwater to hypersaline conditions. We explore the ability of Ae. togoi larvae to tolerate hypersaline conditions by profiling the salt gland, an ion regulatory nexus within an anatomically unique, elaborated anal canal. We present a de-novo chromosome-scale genome assembly for Ae. togoi, highlighting its relatively small genome size and differences in chromosomal structure as compared to other Aedine mosquitoes. We detail repeat content and curate key multi-gene families encoding ion-transport proteins enriched in the larval salt gland, building a model of the machinery that likely facilitates hyperosmotic urine formation. Our work provides insights into molecular and anatomical adaptations that underpin the ability of mosquitoes and other insects to thrive in hypersaline rock pools and other dynamic environments.

43025879.titulo: Neuropeptide T2A-GAL4 Knock-Ins Illustrate Practical Considerations for Interpreting GAL4 Reporter Patterns in Drosophila.
43025879.autores: Jinnai K, Ozawa K, … Kondo S (5 autores)
43025879.resumo: Coleção de knock-ins T2A-GAL4 de neuropeptídeos em Drosophila e knock-ins fluorescentes de Brp como marcador de neurópilo; o padrão do repórter depende da atividade de GAL4 antes da eclosão.
43025879.resumo_original: Transgenic GAL4 lines are widely used in Drosophila to label and manipulate specific cell types, but the resulting reporter expression patterns do not always represent ongoing driver activity. We generated a collection of neuropeptide T2A-GAL4 knock-ins and developed fluorescent Brp knock-ins that serve as neuropil markers, enabling native-fluorescence imaging without immunostaining. The reporter patterns of these GAL4 drivers were broadly consistent with previously reported expression of the corresponding neuropeptides. During characterization, we observed both timing-dependent changes in adult GFP labeling and GAL4-associated cellular abnormalities. Using temperature-sensitive GAL80, we found that adult GFP labeling in certain neurons driven by CCHa2-T2A-GAL4 and Dsk-T2A-GAL4 depended on GAL4 activity before eclosion and was not reproduced by adult-restricted induction. Several GAL4 lines also showed dominant developmental phenotypes. Heterozygous Burs-T2A-GAL4 animals, for example, displayed wing expansion defects that were fully suppressed by GAL80. Severe wing defects were not accompanied by a reduction in the number of reporter-labeled neurons before eclosion, but the morphology of these neurons was affected. These observations illustrate how developmental driver history and GAL4-associated cellular effects can influence reporter patterns in the adult nervous system.

43042937.titulo: Profiling cultivable bacteria in Forcipomyia spp. (Diptera: Ceratopogonidae), feeding on the silkworm Antheraea mylitta (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae): insights into possible transmission routes.
43042937.autores: Maitra Mazumdar S, Banerjee N, … Mazumdar A (6 autores)
43042937.resumo: Bactérias cultiváveis do intestino e das glândulas salivares de Forcipomyia (mosquito-pólvora) que se alimentam de lagartas de Antheraea mylitta: predominam Bacillus e Lysinibacillus, incluindo B. cereus e B. thuringiensis; B. cereus e B. thuringiensis foram detectados em adultos da lagarta após o repasto, mas não em ovos nem em larvas jovens.
43042937.resumo_original: The co-occurrence of Antheraea mylitta Drury larvae (commonly known as tasar silkworm) and hemolymph-feeding Forcipomyia spp. (commonly known as biting midges) in the same habitat increases the likelihood of interaction and pathogen transmission. This study investigated bacterial species shared between Forcipomyia fuliginosa Meigen, Forcipomyia esakiana Tokunaga, and A. mylitta, with emphasis on potential pathogens affecting silk productivity, a sector valued at USD 220.58 million as of 2022 to 2023. As tasar rearing occurs outdoors, larvae are at risk of a plethora of biotic stressors, from prey and predators to pathogens. Cultivable bacteria were isolated from the gut and salivary glands of adult midges following their feeding on 5th instar silkworm larvae. The bacterial isolates obtained from these 2 tissues were then compared with those recovered from healthy and diseased 5th instar larvae to assess similarities and differences in bacterial composition. Bacterial identification was done using DNA barcoding, colony morphology, and biochemical characterization. The isolates belonged to Firmicutes (Bacillaceae), mainly Bacillus and Lysinibacillus. Common strains included Bacillus cereus FFG1, Bacillus thuringiensis IL4, Lysinibacillus fusiformis FFG3, and Lysinibacillus boronitolerans FFG2, the latter being the most prevalent. Bacillus subtilis FFS5 was found only in the salivary gland of F. fuliginosa, while all gut bacteria were also present in salivary glands. Transmission studies detected B. cereus and B. thuringiensis in adult A. mylitta but not in eggs or early larvae, suggesting unlikely trans-ovarian or trans-stadial transmission and a possible vector-mediated role of Forcipomyia spp. This study provides the first baseline report of their cultivable bacterial communities.

43048157.titulo: Shifting climates, shifting microbes: environmental determinants of the microbiome and impact on malaria transmission
43048157.resumo: Revisão sobre como variações ambientais diárias e sazonais alteram fisiologia, imunidade e microbioma do mosquito e, com isso, o desempenho de estratégias baseadas em micróbios (paratransgênese, larvicidas microbianos); aponta que a maioria dos experimentos usa 27 °C e 75–80% de umidade fixos.
43048157.resumo_original: Malaria transmission dynamics are governed by complex tripartite interactions between the Anopheles mosquito, the Plasmodium parasite, and the vector's gut microbiota, all mediated by the mosquito's innate immune system. Although global malaria control is increasingly hindered by drug and insecticide resistance, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding how climate shifts and environmental variations impact vector competence. While most experimental research relies on static laboratory conditions (typically fixed at 27 °C and 75-80% relative humidity), mosquitoes in nature experience continuous diurnal and seasonal environmental fluctuations that alter their physiology, immune responses, and microbiome. Here, we focus on how these environmental shifts likely influence the efficacy and translational success of innovative, microbial-based control strategies, including paratransgenesis, Wolbachia-based interventions, and microbial larvicides. By examining how climate-driven variations impact both the mosquito-microbiota-parasite system and the performance of biocontrol tools, we bridge ecological and molecular perspectives to identify the current understanding of how shifting environments influence the mosquito microbiome and microbial-based tools. We highlight the critical need to integrate dynamic climatic regimes into upstream laboratory evaluations to ensure future malaria control tools remain resilient in a global changing climate.
